Then he sprinkles them with water, saying, "I sprinkle you, the Rakṣas-slayers, the spell-destroyers, belonging to Viṣṇu," thus all of them in succession. Then he pours water upon them, saying, "I pour down upon you, the Rakṣas-slayers, the spell-destroyers, belonging to Viṣṇu," thus upon all of them in succession.
Then he scatters barley-grains upon them, saying, "Thou art barley; bar away from us hatred, bar away enemies," doing so for all of them in successive order.
Then he strews sacrificial grass over them, saying, "Slayers of Rakṣas, slayers of secret spells, I strew thee, belonging to Viṣṇu," doing so for all of them in successive order.

Then, having placed gold between [the grass and the grains], he makes an offering with the dipping-spoon (sruva) over them, saying, "Slayers of Rakṣas, slayers of secret spells, I offer thee, belonging to Viṣṇu, Svāhā! doing so for all of them in successive order.
Now, these two pressing-boards of his are perforated at the Dīrghasoma sacrifice, but unperforated at the Ekāha.

He places them in contact with one another, saying, "I place you two, the Rakṣas-slayers, the charm-destroyers, belonging to Viṣṇu. Then he fixes them around with pegs: two in front, two behind, and two on each side, so that they do not slip away. Then he heaps earth around them from left to right, saying, "I heap around you two, the Rakṣas-slayers, the charm-destroyers, belonging to Viṣṇu. Then he strews sacrificial grass around them, saying, "I strew around you two, the Rakṣas-slayers, the charm-destroyers, belonging to Viṣṇu. Then he touches them, saying, "The Rakṣas-slayers..."

"Valagahana, Vaiṣṇavī"—with these words, he spreads this skin over the two pressing-boards with its neck toward the east and the hair upward, either with the formula "O Sacrifice, be established" or silently.
Across the skin, he causes the pressing-stones to resound with the mantra:
"Thou art great, O great stone; utter for Indra a great voice."
He removes this skin from the nest and places a pressing-stone upon the stones;

then, in front of the support of the southern *havirdhāna* cart, he ties down a handful of sacrificial grass for the sake of the chants. He then asks for the wooden sword (*sphya*), a water-vessel, and earth and sand from the pit (*cātvāla*). Having taken these, he says, "Come, O sacrificer," and having run to the *āgnīdhra* shed, having dug up with the wooden sword and sprinkled with water, he pours down the earth and sand from the pit, saying: "Thou art the pervasive one, the carrier; with thy fierce aspect, protect me, O Agni; fill me, do not harm me."

He makes that hearth (dhiṣṇiya) circular; then he makes it radiant with sand; then he pours out the hearths within the Sadas, first that of the Hotṛ with the formula, "Thou art the bearer, the carrier of oblations";
to the south, that of the Maitrāvaruṇa with the formula, "Thou art the powerful one, the wise one."

With the formula, "Thou art Tutha, the all-knowing," he scatters [the earth] to the north of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin’s hearth; with "Thou art Uśij, the sage," to the north of the Potṛ’s; with "Thou art Aṅghāri, Bambhāri," to the north of the Neṣṭṛ’s; and with "Thou art Avasyu, the worshipful," to the north of the Acchāvāka’s. Then, at the southern edge of the altar, he scatters the Mārjālīya hearth with the formula, "Thou art Śundhyū, the Mārjālīya. He follows this with the Raudra formula for each and every one. Finally, he scatters [earth] at the Āgnīdhra fire-altar for the sake of completing the arrangement from left to right. Thus he has scattered eight [hearths]. Then he assigns eight [names]: with "Thou art Samrāj, Kṛśānu," he worships the Āhavanīya fire.
"Pavamāna, you are worthy of the assembly," [with these words] he approaches the *āstāva*; "You are the wind-bearer," [with these words] the *cātvāla* pit;
"You are unpolished, the preparer of the oblation," [with these words] the animal-cooking fire.
Then, standing at the door of the *sadas*, he worships the *audumbarī* post: "You are the abode of Truth, the light of heaven."
"Thou art the Brahman-light, the sustainer of heaven," [with these words] he approaches the seat of the Brahman.

Then, remaining right there, he worships the Gārhapatya fire with the mantra: "The goat art thou, the one-footed; the serpent art thou, dwelling in the depths," [recited] by those who are about to depart.

Then, standing right there, he issues the call: "Strew the sacrificial grass; set forth the ritual food; summon those who share in the ritual; strew the Āstāva extensively; strew the Sadas and the two Havirdhāna sheds extensively; O Unnetṛ, having placed the ten-stranded filter in the Droṇakalaśa, set down the pressing-stones and the Vāyavya cups in the wife's hall; O Agnīdh, place the clarified butter on the fire; O Pratiprasthātṛ, wipe the ladles and bring the ghee for the speckled butter; bring the curds."

They act according to the directions. Then, at the southern edge of the altar, he spreads a handful of sacrificial grass with the formula: "O divine sacrificial grass, soft as wool, I spread thee, a good seat for the gods.

They go along spreading it thickly from the east towards the west. Then, having taken the clarified butter mixed with speckled butter within the hall and handed it over to the attendants, he hands the King Soma to the Brahman.

Having taken that *brahman* grass-bundle, he stands to the north; standing to the north, he brings the fire forward with the verse: "O Agni, stand up, follow me, being in harmony with all the gods worthy of sacrifice. Place the sacrificer in the world of heaven; do not abandon this oblation for which we approach thee. Then he places the fuel for the leading forward [of the fire], and they arrange the supporting grass-bundles from the *cātvāla* pit.

Even when the vows have been undertaken and [the fires] have been properly covered, having melted the clarified butter over the *gārhapatya* fire and purified it, and having taken four portions into the *sruva*-ladle, he offers the *vaisarjana* oblations on the *śālāmukhīya* fire with the mantra: "O Soma, you are the wide-extender of protection against hostilities caused by ourselves or by others; svāhā! With the *sruva*-ladle, he causes the *aptu* (water) to spill forward with the mantra: "May the swift one, enjoying the clarified butter, partake of it; svāhā! Having taken another four portions, he issues the call: "Recite for Agni and Soma as they are being led forth. When this has been recited three times, they lift up [the fires].
They go to the Hotṛ’s choice; then it is said:
"They carry the fire forward, they lead the wife forward, and they move the wooden carts behind.

Whatever sacrificial vessel belongs to him here, with that they first settle down following the fire; then they proceed with the fire at their head, followed by the King (Soma) and the clarified butter offerings, and followed by the pressing-stones and the Vāyavya cups.

"May this Agni create wide space for us; may he go before us, shattering the adversaries; may he, exulting, conquer the enemies; may he win the prize in the winning of the prize"—with these words, having gone around the north of the *sadas* and placed the fire in the *āgnīdhra* shed, he offers an oblation in the *āgnīdhra* with a verse containing the word "lead": "O Agni, lead us by a good path to wealth, O God who knowest all ways."

"Drive away from us the crooked sin; we offer to you the most abundant speech of homage, Svāhā!"—at this very point, having set down the pressing-stones and the Vāyavya cup together, they pass by. With the King Soma and the clarified butter, he offers a spoonful into the Āhavanīya fire with the mantra: "O Viṣṇu, stride out widely; make wide room for our dwelling. O you whose source is ghee, drink the ghee; further on and on the lord of the sacrifice, Svāhā!
Then, rising up with the sprinkling waters, he sprinkles the fuel and sprinkles the altar.
He sprinkles the sacrificial grass (*barhis*).
Having sprinkled the sacrificial grass that has been placed down and having poured water over it, he takes up the *āśvavāla* bunch as the *prastara* from the front.

Having spread the fivefold sacrificial grass, holding the *prastara* in his hand, he moves forward toward the east and lays the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*) made of *kārṣmarya* wood around the fire. He places two upright fuel-sticks (*samidh*) and sets down two transverse separating-blades (*vidhṛti*) made of *ikṣu* cane.

Having touched the *āśvavāla* grass-bundle upon the two separating-sticks (*vidhṛti*), the *prastara* on the *prastara*, and the *juhū* and other ladles on the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) with the formula, "These have sat down," and having then touched water, he takes the King [Soma] from the *brahman* priest and causes him to enter the *havirdhāna* shed by the eastern door with the verse: "Soma goes forth, the knower of the way; he goes to the appointed place of the gods, to sit in the womb of Truth. Then, in the interior of the southern *havirdhāna*, he spreads a black antelope skin with the formula, "Thou art the seat of Aditi," and places the King [Soma] upon the black antelope skin with the formula, "Sit upon the seat of Aditi."

Then he hands him over to the deities, saying: "O God Savitṛ, this Soma is yours; guard him so that he may not deceive you. Having handed him over, he stands worshipping, saying: "O Soma, as a god you have approached the gods; here I, a man, approach men, together with offspring and together with the increase of wealth.
Saying, "Homage to the gods," he makes a reverential salutation with his joined palms facing eastward.

With the words, "Svadhā to the ancestors," he pours [the water] down toward the south and then steps out, saying, "Here I am released from the noose of Varuṇa. Then he worships the Āhavanīya fire with, "May I behold the light of Vaiśvānara, the sun. Then he releases the sacrificer from the intermediate consecration (*avāntaradīkṣā*) with the formula: "O Agni, Lord of Vows, you are the lord of vows among vows. That body of mine which was in you, let it be here in me; that body of yours which was in me, let it be there in you. O Lord of Vows, let our vows be according to their respective places."

"O you two observers of vows, perform your vows! Then he instructs him: "Loosen your girdle; open your fists; hand over the staff to the Maitrāvaruṇa; let them call you by name, O sacrificer, mentioning your names along with those of your fathers, grandfathers, great-grandfathers, sons, and grandsons; let the Subrahmaṇya priest invoke the Subrahmaṇyā. He does all this accordingly. Then, having offered the oblation for the sacrificial post, he prepares the post with a Yajus formula and prepares the post-hole with a Yajus formula.
This [rite] concludes with the pit for the sacrificial post; then, according to the procedure for the sacrificial post, he raises the post,
and having set aside the post provided with a wooden cup (svaru), he dedicates the animal for Agni and Soma.

Having performed the ritual with its omentum in the established manner, and having cast the two omentum-spits into the fire and stepped out, they purify themselves at the *cātvāla* pit. Then, he asks for a sturdy jar;
taking it, they go out toward the north between the *cātvāla* and the rubbish-heap (*utkara*), and proceed to where there is water, but they do not cross over the innermost flowing stream.
He does not take [the water] from stationary [sources];

standing against the current, he takes it at the junction of shade and sunlight. He recites: "These waters are rich in oblation; the divine sacrifice is rich in oblation; he desires to win with oblation; may Sūrya be rich in oblation. Then, having taken them, having turned to the right, having placed them on his left shoulder, having returned by the same way he came, having gone around the north of the Āgnīdhrīya fire and around the north of the Sadas, and having entered the hall by the eastern door, he places them behind the Gārhapatya fire, touching the *aupasadā* altar, saying: "In the seat of Agni, whose house is secure..."
"I set down the gracious ones for the sake of grace; place me in grace"—thus he says. Then he offers the animal cake (paśupuroḍāśa).
The animal cake concludes with the *iḍā* offering; some say it concludes with the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings, while others say it concludes with the heart-spike (*hṛdayaśūla*).
Then, intending to carry around the *vasatīvarī* waters, he says: "Step aside; let me not pass over you."

The sacrificer sits down in the sacrificer’s station behind the Gārhapatya fire. Then, taking them [the vessels], having carried them out through the southern door, having placed them on his left shoulder, having gone around the south of the Sadas, and having carried them around the south of the Mārjālīya hearth, he sets them down to the south, touching the sacrificial post, with the formula: "Ye are the portions of Indra and Agni. Then, taking them, having turned toward the north, having placed them on his right shoulder, and having returned by the same way he came, he sets them down behind the Gārhapatya on the Aupasadā altar, touching it.

"Ye are the portion of Mitra and Varuṇa," he says. Then, taking them up, having carried them out by the eastern door, having placed them on the southern shoulder [of the altar], having gone around the north side of the *sadas*, and having carried them around the north side of the *āgnīdhrīya* hearth, he sets them down to the north, touching the sacrificial post, with the formula: "Ye are the portion of the Viśve Devas. Then, taking them up, turning to the right, placing them on the left shoulder, returning by the same way he came, he sets them down behind the *āgnīdhrīya* hearth, touching it, with the formula: "Be watchful at the sacrifice."

Then he assigns the milks: "Make curds for the *dadhigharma* from that which belongs to the Sovereign; make *āmikṣā* from that which belongs to the Sacrificer; make milk and parched grain for the *āśira* belonging to the wife; make curds for the boiled *ātaṅkya* for the Āditya cup; make the flour for the sacrificial cakes; make parched grains for the *hāriyojana* offering; prepare four *ambhṛṇa* vessels, three *udacana* vessels, odd-numbered *ekadhana* jars—the lowest being three and the highest eleven—four cords, and four [vessels]."

"Prepare the two omentum-spits, the sacrificial fuel and the grass, and the large enclosing-sticks of *udumbara* wood; let the Subrahmaṇya priest invoke the Subrahmaṇyā. They act according to these directions. Then he causes these *āmbhṛṇa* jars to be brought: the *ādhavanīya* in the interior of the northern *havirdhāna* cart, the *pūtabhṛt* on the front beam (*prauga*), and for both of them, a common water-vessel at the *āgnīdhra* shed; one single water-vessel at the *mārjālīya* shed, and another single water-vessel at the *āgnīdhra*. On this night, the sacrificer goes to sleep.
They guard the King (Soma) in the two Havirdhāna sheds;
then, at the very time of the great night, they wake them up.

The Adhvaryu wakes these officiating priests: the Hotṛ, the Brahman, the Udgātṛ, the Pratiprasthātṛ, the Prastotṛ, the Praśāstṛ, the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, the Acchāvāka, the Neṣṭṛ, the Potṛ, the Sadasya, the Unnetṛ, the Āgnīdhra, the Grāvastut, the Subrahmaṇya, the Pratihartṛ, and whoever other assistants there may be.

Having washed their hands and feet, they approach the sacrificer at the Āgnīdhra fire. Then the Adhvaryu touches his two hands, saying, "May I be able for you two to perform the work for the gods. Standing right there, he issues the call: "O Unnetṛ, having placed the pressing-stones and the Vāyavya cups along with the fringe-filters in the Droṇakalaśa, set them down in front of the axle of the southern Havirdhāna cart. O Āgnīdh, place the clarified butter on the fire. O Pratiprasthātṛ, cleanse the offering-spoons; bring the butter for the Pṛṣadājya; fetch the curds."

They act according to the directions. Then the Adhvaryu touches the Āgnīdhra shed with a verse addressed to Agni: "Agni is the head of heaven... He touches the *havirdhāna* shed with a verse addressed to Viṣṇu: "O Viṣṇu, you are our nearest... He touches the offering-spoons with a verse addressed to Agni: "This Agni is the giver of thousands... He touches the vessels for Vāyu with a verse addressed to Vāyu: "O Vāyu, a hundred bay steeds... He touches the *sadas* with a verse addressed to Indra: "All have made Indra grow... Then, having taken the portions of clarified butter mixed with speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*), he rises up with the sprinkling waters and sprinkles the fuel-wood.
He sprinkles the altar, he sprinkles the sacrificial grass (*barhis*).

Having sprinkled the sacrificial grass that has been laid down and having poured water over it, he takes the *prastara* bundle from the front. Having spread the sacrificial grass in a single layer, with the *prastara* in his hand, he moves forward to the east and lays down the large enclosing sticks made of *udumbara* wood, using the standard formula for laying them down; then he yokes them with the formula for yoking.

"I yoke for thee the earth together with light," he says as he touches the middle one; "I yoke Vāyu for thee together with the intermediate space," he says as he touches the southern one; "I yoke the three divergent paths of the sun for thee," he says. Then, having touched water, he says, "Come, O sacrificer! and, having caused him to enter the *havirdhāna* shed by the eastern door, he spreads out this skin upon the two planks with its neck toward the east and the hair upward, either with the formula, "O sacrifice, be established," or silently.

Having placed the pressing-stones facing him on that [spot], he brings down the King [Soma] between the two poles of the southern *havirdhāna* cart with two verses: "For the heart thee! For the mind thee! O King Soma, come hither, descend! Thus he says.

Then they announce him to the Udgātṛs; they perform therein what they know. Then, having sipped water, he says, "Come, O Sacrificer! Having run to the Āgnīdhra shed and taken four portions of clarified butter in the ladle, he recites the Pañcahotṛ formula mentally and offers it in the Āgnīdhra fire while the Sacrificer maintains contact with him, saying "Svāhā! Having taken another four portions, he offers them in the mouth of the Āgnīdhra, saying, "Protect me from the curse of the mouth, from every imprecation, Svāhā! Then he silently places a chip of wood smeared with clarified butter onto the Āhavanīya fire. Then, standing right there, he issues the summons.

"O Hotṛ, recite for the gods who come at dawn; O Brahman, restrain your speech; O Subrahmaṇya, invoke the Subrahmaṇyā; O Āgnīdh, pour out the sacrificial portions for the *savanīya* offerings; O Pratiprasthātṛ, arrange the vessels on the mound"—thus they act according to the directions. Then the Hotṛ begins the morning litany (*prātaranuvāka*), and the Brahman restrains his speech.
The Subrahmaṇya priest invokes the Subrahmaṇyā formula; when it has been invoked, the Brahman releases his speech.

The Āgnīdhra pours out the oblations for the Savanīya cakes dedicated to Indra on eleven potsherds; he causes the call to the preparer of the oblation (*haviṣkṛt*) to be raised over rice grains alone. Then they lift up as many [vessels] as there are; meanwhile, the Pratiprasthātṛ arranges the vessels upon the mound (*khara*).

In the eastern half of the mound, he places the *upāṃśusavana* stone with its head toward the south. To the south [of the stone] he places the *upāṃśu* cup, and to the north the *antaryāma* cup; these two are either touching or not touching, depending on whether the rite is for one practicing sorcery. Behind them, following in order, are the cups for the dual-deity offerings: the *aindravāyava* cup, the *maitrāvaruṇa* cup, and the *āśvina* cup. Behind those, the *śukra* and *manthin* cups are placed side by side, with the *śukra* cup to the south and the *manthin* cup to the north.
In front [of the *khara*], he places the *manthin* vessel; behind it, the *ṛtu* vessels; on the southern hip of the *khara*, the *āgrayaṇa* jar together with its supplementary cup (*upaśaya*);
and on the northern hip of the *khara*, the *ukthya* jar together with its supplementary cup.
In front of the northern *havirdhāna* cart, upon ground that has not been smeared with clay, he places the *dhruva* vessel;
between the *pūtabhṛt* and the *ādhavanīya*, the cups;

and behind the axle of the southern *havirdhāna* cart, the *droṇakalaśa* and the two *daśāpavitra* filters. Then he touches them with ten formulas: "Agni is the deity, the *gāyatrī* is the metre, you are the vessel of the *upāṃśu* [cup]," and so on for each of the ten. Then the Adhvaryu either enters the hall or remains watching over the ritual acts.

Then, when he recognizes the Hotṛ’s recitation: "The Dawn has appeared with her radiant cattle; Agni, the seasonal one, has been established. Your immortal chariot, O wonder-workers, rich in stallions, has been yoked—O lovers of sweetness, hear my call," then, having taken four portions of clarified butter in the *pracaraṇī* ladle, he offers it into the Āhavanīya fire while the sacrificer maintains contact with him, [reciting]: "May Agni hear my call with his fuel; may the Waters and the divine Dhiṣaṇās hear."

"Listen, O pressing-stones, to the sacrifice; may the wise one listen! May the god Savitṛ hear my call! Svāhā! Having thus taken another fourfold-drawn portion and having taken the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), he issues the command: "Send forth the waters, O Hotṛ! Camasādhvaryus of Maitrāvaruṇa, Ādruva, and Vaikadhanins, come hither! Neṣṭṛ, lead up the wife! Agnīdh, receive [the water] at the Cātvāla pit with the Hotṛ’s cup and the Vasatīvarī waters!
They act according to the command.

The Neṣṭṛ brings the wife, taking the *pānnejana* vessel; with the liturgical formula, "Go forth! Come up! he causes her to go out by the eastern door, leads her around the north side of the *sadas*, and leads her past the north side of the *āgnīdhrīya* hearth. Having gone out between the *cātvāla* and the rubbish-heap toward the north, they proceed to where there is water. Then, having thrown sacrificial grass (*barhis*) into the water, he makes an offering over it with the formula: "O divine waters, O Son of the Waters, that wave of yours which is fit for oblation, powerful, and most intoxicating—that do you bestow among the gods as a godly gift, pure for those who drink the pure, whose portion you are; svāhā!"

He causes the oblation to overflow with the cup of Mitrāvaruṇa, saying, "Thou art the plougher; drive away the evil, the adversary. Placing two blades of *barhis* grass between [the cup and the vessel], he draws [the water] up, saying, "I draw you up for the imperishability of the ocean. Then he takes the *ekadhana* waters, either saying, "I take you, who are pleasing to Indra," or silently. Then he takes the *pannejani* waters, saying, "I take you, the *pannejani* waters, for the Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas, and the Viśve Devas; I take you, the *pannejani* waters, for the sacrifice."

Having handed those [cups] over to his wife, they go out; while the sacrificer maintains contact [with her], having returned by the same way they came, he touches together the Hotṛ’s cup and the Maitrāvaruṇa’s cup at the Cātvāla pit and pours the Vasatīvarī waters into them, filling the Hotṛ’s cup.

He causes [the soma] to spill into the Maitrāvaruṇa cup for the sake of attainment. Then, having placed together three—the Hotṛ’s cup, the Vasatīvarī waters, and the Maitrāvaruṇa cup—he anoints them with the *pracaraṇī* spoon according to the stoma, saying: "May light be united with light; may the bright with the bright, the oblation with the oblation, and the lord of the sacrifice with his blessing. Then the wife, having returned by the same way she came, places them silently in contact on the *aupasadā* altar behind the Gārhapatya fire. Then the Adhvaryu goes to the signal-call of the Hotṛ.

The Hotṛ asks the Adhvaryu, "O Adhvaryu, have you seen the cattle? The other replies, "I have indeed seen them; they are here. Then, if it is an Agniṣṭoma, he offers with the formula: "O Agni, that mortal whom you protect in battles and whom you urge on in the contests for booty—he shall be the master of eternal nourishment, Svāhā!

If it is an Ukthya, he wipes [the vessel] upon the middle enclosing-stick with this very same Yajus. If it is an Atirātra, he enters while reciting this very Yajus, for the sake of distinguishing the sacrificial rites (yajñakratu), so says the Brāhmaṇa.

Then, having caused these vessels belonging to the *hotṛ*’s cup to pass between the two shafts of the southern *havirdhāna* cart, he sets them down in the interior. Then, having turned the *ādhavanīya* vessel upside down, he pours out all the contents of the *maitrāvaruṇa*’s cup;
he pours in a third part of the *vasatīvarī* waters and a third part of the *ekadhanā* waters. He places the *vasatīvarī* waters in front of the axle.

Then, having sat down between the two *havirdhāna* sheds, he asks for a four-cornered vessel made of *udumbara* wood. Having placed two blades of sacrificial grass (*barhis*) inside it, he draws the *dadhi-graha* belonging to Prajāpati with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, the luminous, for the luminous Prajāpati; for Dakṣa, the increaser of Dakṣa; offered to the gods whose tongue is Agni, who live by the Truth, who have Indra as their eldest, Varuṇa as their king, Vātāpi as their companion, and Parjanya as their soul."
Having removed the two blades of sacrificial grass and having taken up the vessel, he stands up with the formula: "For heaven thee, for the intermediate space thee, for the earth thee!"

He goes out by the eastern door [with the mantra]: "Away, O Indra, slay the mind of him who hates us, away the mind of him who seeks to conquer us; away slay him who acts as an enemy toward us. Having approached the Āhavanīya fire while the sacrificer maintains contact with him, he offers an oblation with: "For out-breath thee, for in-breath thee, for diffused breath thee; for what exists thee, for what does not exist thee; for the waters thee, for the plants thee; for all beings thee; from whom offspring were born unimpaired—for that Prajāpati, the wide-giving, the luminous, I offer thee, the luminous, svāhā! Then he pours its wash-water within the enclosing sticks.
"One should give either an excellent cow or an excellent bull," so said Baudhāyana; "twelve heifers," so said Āñjīgavi; "a bull," so said Kātya; "jewels and earrings," so said Rāthītara.
Then, having brought down these [vessels] belonging to the Hotṛ's cup between the two poles of the southern *havirdhāna* cart, he places them upon the hide.

Over those *nigrābhya* waters, he causes the sacrificer to recite: "You are the *nigrābhyās*, heard by the gods; satisfy my life-span," beginning with this and ending with, "May my groups not thirst. Having handed them over to the sacrificer, he then takes up that one among these pressing-stones which is like a *sujantu*. Having taken it with the formula, "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee," he consecrates it with: "Thou art a stone, a performer of the sacrifice for the gods; perform this deep sacrifice for Indra with thy highest rim."

[He measures out] the well-pressed Soma, honeyed, milky, and winning rain; then, having leaned it forward and loosened it, he measures out the King [Soma] over the pressing-stone used for the *upāṃśu* libation with the formula "O Indra, you who are the slayer of Vṛtra... O Indra, you who are the overcomer of Vṛtra... O Indra, you who are the slayer of adversaries... O Indra, you who are accompanied by the Ādityas... O Indra, you who are accompanied by all the gods," five times with the *yajus*.

Having measured five times silently and ten times while measuring, he measures half of the King [Soma]; then, having tied the remaining King [Soma] with a turban and brought it between the two poles of the southern *havirdhāna* cart, he places it in the interior. Then, he pours the measured King [Soma] together with the waters from the *hotṛ*-cup, saying: "You are invigorating, overcomers of Vṛtra, bestowers of wealth, wives of immortality; O goddesses, establish this sacrifice among the gods; being invited, drink of the Soma! Being invited, let the Soma drink of you!"

Then he mixes it, saying: "O Soma, with that light of yours which is in heaven, which is on earth, and which is in the wide mid-air—with that, make wide wealth for this sacrificer; speak in favor of the giver. He touches the two pressing-boards across the hide, saying: "O two Dhiṣaṇās, being firm, be firm; bestow strength upon us; bestow strength upon me; may I not harm you, and may you not harm me. Then he causes [the sacrificer] to recite the *vṛddhi* verses: "I have increased you with my mind, O well-born ones, born of the *ṛta*; may we be yours, O Goddesses, through Bhaga. May the divine plants, in agreement with Indra, consent to the Soma for the pressing."

When the King has been fully satiated, the Pratiprasthātṛ places six shoots (*aṃśu*) in his left hand; then with that same hand he takes up the Upāṃśu vessel. He then presses the King [Soma] eight times first while it is being approached. When a shoot has fallen, he makes him recite: "Do not strike me away, together with offspring, together with the increase of wealth; do not destroy my sensory power and vigor. Then he strikes [the shoots] with his joined palms silently;
the Pratiprasthātṛ holds [the shoots] between [his hands].
With the first two verses, the Adhvaryu brings [the soma] with the mantra, "O vigorous one, flow pure for Vācaspati";
he then places these two stalks together and presses the King [Soma] eleven times with the second [verse].
When the shoulder-blade has been dropped, he does not make [the sacrificer] recite;
likewise, he strikes with his joined palms and silently places it within.
The Pratiprasthātṛ brings the two middle shoulder-blades, while the Adhvaryu [recites]: "The bull [is purified] by the two shoulder-blades of the bull, cleansed by the hands."
They cleanse these stalks; likewise, having approached the King [Soma], he presses him for the third time twelve times.
He does not cause [the sacrificer] to recite the formula when the stalks have been scattered.

In the same manner, he strikes with his joined palms; silently, he places [the vessel] between. The Pratiprasthātṛ brings [the Soma] with the two last shoots. The Adhvaryu [takes it] with the formula: "Thou art the god, the purifier of the gods; for those whose portion thou art, for them thee! He touches these two shoots. Then, having wiped this Upāṃśu-pressing stone with the *daśāpavitra* filter, he places it on the eastern half of the *khara* mound, with its head toward the south. Then he takes the cup of the Pratiprasthātṛ with the formula: "Thou art self-made."

He hands [the vessel] over and then gazes at it, saying, "Make our nourishments honey-sweet. Then he wipes it upwards, saying, "For all thy powers, celestial and terrestrial. Then, taking it up, he stands up, saying, "May the mind attend thee. Having gone forward, saying, "Go through the wide atmosphere," he offers it in the Āhavanīya fire while the sacrificer maintains contact with him, saying, "Svāhā! To thee, O auspicious one, for Sūrya, Svāhā! Having offered, he breathes out.

He causes [the Adhvaryu] to recite: "Thou art the earth, the best of rays, the protector of breath; protect my breath. Then, having wiped him downward, he wipes him on the middle enclosing-stick with his hand turned toward him and downward, saying: "For the gods who drink the rays, thee! Then, having turned to the right, he pours the residue of the cup into the Āgrayaṇa vessel, saying: "This is thy womb. Then he throws the *aṃśu* stalk into this Upāṃśu cup, and places it to the south, touching it with the Upāṃśusavana stone, saying: "For out-breathing (*prāṇa*) thee! and "For through-breathing (*vyāna*) thee! He then touches the Upāṃśusavana stone in response.

While the Adhvaryu is occupied here, the Pratiprasthātṛ pours two by two stalks of the King [Soma] into the *aṃśu* cups with the formula: "O Soma, that which is thy inviolable, watchful name—for that, O Soma, to Soma, svāhā!"—[repeating] "O Soma, that which is thine, O Soma... Then, about to press the King, they sit down all around him;
the Adhvaryu sits behind him, facing east.

Following his right arm, the sacrificer stands on the south, the Pratiprasthātṛ on the north, and the Āgnīdhra between the Pratiprasthātṛ and the Āgnīdhra fire-altar; then the fourth person who presses [the Soma] speaks. Then he says to the Unnetṛ, "Bring water and pour it in! The Unnetṛ pours from the *adhavanīya* jar with water flowing out over the upper half of the *hotṛcamasa*. They cause the stalks (*aṃśu*) to overflow in the *hotṛcamasa* with the verse: "From the east, the west, the north, and the south—let the quarters run toward thee; O Mother, flow down. This is the *nigrābha*. They cause [the Soma] to swell, they separate [the stalks], they press, they perform the *nigrābha*, and they cause [the Soma] to swell again.
They separate [the soma],
they press it, they go to the *nigrābha* (the water for mixing), they cause it to swell, they separate it, and they press it.
They do not perform the *nigrābha* rite on the fourth day; then, having collected him well-prepared in the *saṃbharaṇī* vessel, he hands him over to the *unnetṛ*.
In this very same way the second turn is completed, and likewise the third. Finally, having wrapped the *ṛjīṣa* with the *daśāpavitra*, he hands it over to the *unnetṛ*.
The *unnetṛ*, having washed it in the *ādhavanīya* jar and squeezed it out, brings it down between the two poles of the southern *havirdhāna* cart and places it upon the hide.

Having placed the pressing stones directly in front of him, he distributes this *ṛjīṣa* in four parts from the mouths of the stones. Then either the Udgātṛ or the Prastotṛ, having crept behind the axle of the southern *havirdhāna* cart, places the *droṇakalaśa* facing eastward upon the stones;
over it they spread the *daśāpavitra* filter with its fringes pointing northward.

When he has performed it in that manner, they await the rising of the sun; once the sun has risen, he draws the Antaryāma cup from the King who is being purified, [reciting]: "Thou art taken with a support; O Maghavan, restrain within, protect the Soma, preserve our wealth, sacrifice for the sake of strength; I place thee between Heaven and Earth, between the wide mid-air; in harmony with the lower and higher gods, O Maghavan, rejoice in the Antaryāma!"

With the words, "Thou art made acceptable," he hands over the cup; then he gazes at it with the words, "Make our nourishments honey-sweet. Then he wipes it upwards with the words, "For all thy powers, celestial and terrestrial. Then, taking it up, he rises with the words, "May the mind attend thee. Having gone forward with the words, "Go through the wide atmosphere," he offers it in the Āhavanīya fire while the sacrificer maintains contact with him, saying, "Svāhā! To thee, O auspicious one, for Sūrya, Svāhā! Having offered, he breathes out.

He causes [the Adhvaryu] to recite: "Thou art the yoke-pole, the best of the reins; O protector of the out-breath, protect my out-breath. Then, having wiped him upward, he wipes him across the middle enclosing-stick with his palm turned upward from west to east, saying: "For the gods who drink the rays of light, thee! Then, turning to the right, he pours the residue from the Āgrayaṇa vessel into the cup, saying: "This is thy womb. Then he sets it down to the north, touching it with the Upāṃśusavana stone, saying: "For the out-breath, thee!"

With the formula, "For Vyāna thee," he touches the Upāṃśusavana stone. Then he says to the Unnetṛ, "Bring [the Soma] continuously and without negligence; I shall draw the Upāṃśu cups. He then takes the Aindravāyava vessel; it is made of *rāsnā* wood and has a neck (*grīvī*).

With that he draws [the Soma] from the King who is being purified, reciting the verse, "O Vāyu, come to the pure-drinker," and then the formula, "Thou art taken with a base; I take thee, acceptable to Vāyu. Having set it down, he again holds it over [the Soma], reciting the verse, "O Indra and Vāyu, these [Somas] are pressed," and then the formula, "Thou art taken with a base; I take thee, acceptable to Indra and Vāyu."
Having wiped it, he sets it down with the formula, "This is thy womb; for the two who are in harmony, thee. Then he takes up the Maitrāvaruṇa cup; it has a *pilaka* (a small knob) on it.

With that, he draws [the Soma] from the King who is being purified, reciting, "This is for you two, O Mitra and Varuṇa," and continuing, "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Mitra and Varuṇa. Having placed two blades of *barhis* grass between [the cup and the vessel], he mixes it with milk. Having removed the two blades of *barhis*, he wipes it with the fringed filter (*daśāpavitra*) and sets it down with the formula, "This is thy womb; for the two who live by Truth, thee. Then, passing over the Āśvina cup, he takes up the Śukra cup.
This [cup] is made of Bilva or Palāśa wood and is smooth;
with it he draws [the Soma], having run through the verse, "This Vena has impelled the King who is being purified," and says, "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Śaṇḍa.
Having wiped it, he sets it down, saying, "This is thy womb; protect heroism! Then he takes the Manthin vessel, which is made of Vikaṅkata wood and is smooth.

With that [ladle], he draws from the King who is being purified, running after it with the formula, "As of old... and saying, "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Marka. Having placed two blades of *barhis* grass between [the vessel and the Soma] and having mixed it with barley meal, he removes the two blades of *barhis*, wipes [the cup] with the *daśāpavitra* filter, and sets it down with, "This is thy womb; protect the offspring. Then he takes the *āgrayaṇa* vessel and draws from the King who is being purified with that [vessel], running after it with the formula, "O gods who are eleven in heaven... and saying, "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to the Viśve Devas. Then he utters the sound *hiṃ* over it three times.

Hiṃ hiṃ hiṃ! Soma purifies itself; Soma purifies itself; Soma purifies itself. For this *brahman* it purifies itself; for this *kṣatra* it purifies itself; for this *viś* it purifies itself. It purifies itself for food; it purifies itself for strength; it purifies itself for the waters; it purifies itself for the plants; it purifies itself for the trees; it purifies itself for heaven and earth; it purifies itself for well-being; it purifies itself for spiritual luster; it purifies itself for this pressing sacrificer; it purifies itself for me—having thus recited in a low voice, he then says aloud: "It purifies itself for preeminence."

Then he addresses it: "Thou art the Āgrayaṇa; thou art a good Āgrayaṇa; quicken the sacrifice, quicken the lord of the sacrifice; protect the pressings! May Viṣṇu protect thee; do thou protect the people with power.

Having wiped it all around, he sets it down with the formula: "This is thy womb; for the All-gods thee! From this point onward, he draws the cups with verses containing the word *upabdi*, such as: "Thirty and three are the troop-leaders who break [the enemy]. Regarding this, there is a Brāhmaṇa text stating: "One should draw the cup with a verse containing the word 'broken' (*rugṇavat*) when one has a rival."

Then he takes the Ukthya vessel; with it he draws from the King who is being purified, saying: "Thou art taken with a support; for Indra the great, the vigorous, the seeker of hymns—what vigor is thine, O Indra, for that I take thee as one beloved.

Having wiped it around, he sets it down, saying: "This is thy womb; for Indra the seeker of hymns. Then he takes the Dhruva vessel; he says: "Those who have entered by the eastern door, let them go out facing east; those by the western door, let them go out facing west; may I not pass you on the wrong side."

Having moved around behind the pressers and the *unnētṛ* from the rear, he receives [the cup] from the north with the verse, "The head of heaven, the messenger of earth... Having recited this, he says, "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Agni Vaiśvānara. Then he pronounces the consecration over it: "Thou art firm, a firm dwelling, the firmest of the firm, the most immovable of the immovable. Then, having carried it back as it was brought, he places it on the unpounded ground in front of the support of the northern *havirdhāna* cart, saying, "This is thy womb;
for Agni Vaiśvānara, thee!"

With the *dhruva* cup, he hands over the King [Soma]; then, having thrown the *pariplu* vessel into the upper half of the *droṇakalaśa*, he addresses the drops with the formulas: "The drop has fallen," "Thy drop," "The drop which," and "Thy drop. Then he says to the *unnetṛ*: "Make the *pūtabhṛt* full; I shall take the cups of the Pavamāna."

Having heard that, the Unnetṛ spreads the filter over the opening of the *pūtabhṛt* vessel and pours two or three ladlings of the King [Soma] into it. Then, while the *pūtabhṛt* is not yet empty, he draws the cups for the Pavamāna laud: "Thou art taken with a support; for Prajāpati thee!"—with this he touches the *droṇakalaśa*; "For Indra and Agni thee!"—[this for] the *ādhavanīya*; "For the All-gods thee!"—[this for] the *pūtabhṛt*. Then he says, "O Unnetṛ! Cause the King [Soma] to flow through from the *pūtabhṛt* towards the east; having wiped the *ādhavanīya* with the fringe, turn it upside down."
He does so; then, having touched water and taken two blades of sacrificial grass (*barhis*), he creeps out.
As he creeps out, the Udgātṛ touches him, the Prastotṛ touches the Udgātṛ, and the Pratihartṛ touches the Prastotṛ.
The sacrificer [approaches] the *pratihartṛ*, the *brahmán* the sacrificer,
and the *pratiprasthātṛ* is the seventh; while they are holding on to one another, he offers a spoonful (*sruva-āhuti*) into the *āhavanīya* fire.

"May Agni Vaiśvānara, who brings welfare to all, protect us at the morning pressing by his greatness; may he, the purifier, bestow wealth upon us, and may we, sharing the draught, be long-lived—Svāhā! With this verse the two Adhvaryus offer the oblation, while the others offer according to their respective Vedas; then they creep toward the north toward the Pavamāna graha.

The Adhvaryu, bowing low, first creeps forward while shaking the two *barhis* grass-blades, saying: "May Speech go at the head, going straight ahead; may she go before the gods, bestowing glory upon me, vital breaths upon the animals, and offspring upon me and the sacrificer. Then they sit down in their respective places in the *āstāva*. Then he hands the two *barhis* blades to either the Udgātṛ or the Prastotṛ, saying, "Thou art the under-layer for the Ṛc and the Sāman, for the procreation of the pair," or silently. Then he mutters the introductory formula: "Vāyu is the maker of the *hiṅ* sound, Agni is the Prastotṛ, Prajāpati is the Sāman."

"Bṛhaspati is the Udgātṛ, the Viśve Devas are the Upagātṛs, the Maruts are the Pratihartṛs, and Indra is the Nidhana. May those gods, the Prāṇabhṛts, bestow life-breath upon me; Om! Sing! This Bahiṣpavamāna becomes threefold (trivṛt).

When the fifth [verse] has been introduced, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "Thou art a falcon, having the Gāyatrī for thy metre; I take hold of thee; lead me safely across. At this point, he recites the Daśahotṛ formula. Once the Sāman has been chanted, he issues the direction: "O Āgnīdh, spread the fires; strew the sacrificial grass; prepare the sacrificial cakes; O Pratiprasthātṛ, let the animal sacrifice be near at hand."

They perform their duties according to the directions; then, having touched water and said, "Come, O Sacrificer," he leads him into the *havirdhāna* shed by the eastern door and stands in worship before the entire King Soma with the verse, "O Viṣṇu, you are our nearest [kinsman]. Then he takes the cup for the Aśvins; it is double-edged.

From the *droṇakalaśa*, he draws the juice into that cup using the *pariplu* ladle, reciting the verse, "Whatever [beverage] is yours, O Kaśā," followed by the formula: "You are taken with a support; I take you, acceptable to the Aśvins."

Having wiped [the ladle], he sets it down with the formula: "This is your womb; for the two Mādhvīs, you! Then, having touched water, he says, "Come, O sacrificer! Having run to the Āhavanīya fire and taken four portions into the offering-spoon (*sruk*), he recites the *Saptahotṛ* formula mentally and offers it into the Āhavanīya while the sacrificer maintains contact with him, saying "Svāhā! Then he proceeds with the *avakāśa* formulas: "Encompassing Agni, encompassing Indra," with this section (*anuvāka*). Then he takes nine portions into the *pracaraṇī* spoon; then this Āgnīdhra [priest] [takes portions] from the Āgnīdhrīya hearth in successive order.

He distributes the embers among the *dhiṣṇiya* hearths; then, sitting in front and facing west, he sprinkles clarified butter over the distributed *dhiṣṇiyas* with the same mantras as those used for their original placement. If he offers oblations according to the order of placement, he finally offers on the *Āgnīdhra* hearth with the mantra "Seven are yours. However, if he offers with the cry "Svāhā! Svāhā!", he finally offers on the *Āgnīdhrīya* hearth with the word "Svāhā" alone, so as to maintain the movement from left to right. Then, at the front corner of the northern *havirdhāna* cart, he places the *pracaraṇī* ladle; thereafter, along the visible path, he spreads the *pṛṣṭhya* grass-line continuously from the *Gārhapatya* fire to the *Āhavanīya* fire.

Then the Adhvaryu, with a rope in his hand, approaches the sacrificial post; having removed the previous rope, while winding it around at the height of the navel, he says, "Recite for the post being encircled.
Having released the post provided with a wooden chip (svaru), he dedicates the animal to Agni; the ritual procedure remains the same up to the invocation of the ancestors (pravara).

He chooses the well-known Hotṛ; then he causes the announcement to be made: "Ośrāvaya! Astu Śrauṣaṭ! The Aśvins are the Adhvaryus from the office of the Adhvaryu. He pronounces the name of the Pratiprasthātṛ: "And so-and-so is the human one. Then he causes the announcement to be made: "Ośrāvaya! Astu Śrauṣaṭ! Mitra and Varuṇa are the Praśāstṛs from the office of the Praśāstṛ. He pronounces the name of the Maitrāvaruṇa: "And so-and-so is the human one. Then he causes the announcement to be made: "Ośrāvaya! Astu Śrauṣaṭ! Indra is the Brahman from the office of the Brahman. "And so-and-so is the human one."

He pronounces the name of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin; then he causes the announcement to be made: "O announce! Let it be heard! From the office of the Potṛ, Marut is the human one"—thus he pronounces the name of the Potṛ. Then he causes the announcement to be made: "O announce! Let it be heard! From the office of the Neṣṭṛ, Agnāyu is the human one"—thus he pronounces the name of the Neṣṭṛ. Then he causes the announcement to be made: "O announce! Let it be heard! From the office of the Āgnīdhra, Agni is the human one"—thus he pronounces the name of the Āgnīdhra.
As soon as they have entered, he offers the *pravṛtāhuti* oblations with these [formulas]:

"May I be dear to speech; prosper the hymn with the Ṛg-verse; may the god Sūrya protect me from the gods. With these, the two Adhvaryus offer; the others offer according to their respective Vedas. Then he causes the announcement: "Ośrāvaya! Astu Śrauṣaṭ! Agni is the leader of the divine clans; this sacrificer, pressing the Soma, is the leader of men. May their household-fire shine undivided for a hundred winters. May the two of them, uniting their wealth and not separating their bodies, prosper."
The ritual procedure for the omentum is the same;

having performed the offering with the omentum and having cast the two omentum-spits into the fire, they step out and purify themselves at the *cātvāla* pit. Then he causes the sacrificer to stand upon the rubbish-heap (*utkara*) facing the wooden sword (*sphya*) and the beaters (*vighana*).

"The wooden sword (sphya) is well-being; the mallet (vighana) is well-being; the rib (parśu), the altar (vedi), and the axe (paraśu) are well-being for us. You are worthy of sacrifice and performers of sacrifice; do you invite me to this sacrifice! May Heaven and Earth invite me; may the place of praise (āstāva), the pitcher (kalaśa), Soma, and Agni invite me; may the gods and the sacrifice invite me; may the Hotṛ-offices invite me to the invitation! Then he stands near the Āhavanīya fire, saying: "Homage to Agni, the slayer of Makha; may the glory of Makha not depart from me."

"Obeisance to Rudra, the slayer of Makha; having been honored, protect me"—with these words he addresses the Āgnīdhra fire. "Obeisance to Indra, the slayer of Makha; do not destroy my power and vigor"—with these words he addresses the Hotrīya fire.

Then, having turned toward the east, he mutters: "You two are firm; you two are relaxed; being united, protect me from laughter! May the god Sūrya protect me from the sky from laughter; Vāyu from the intermediate space; Agni from the earth; Yama from the fathers; Sarasvatī from men. Then, having turned clockwise, he touches the two eastern doors of the *sadas* with the formula: "O divine doors, do not burn me! Then he enters the *sadas*, saying: "Homage to the *sadas*, homage to the lord of the *sadas*, homage to the eye of the friends who go before, homage!"

"Adoration to the sky, adoration to the earth"—with these words, he throws away a blade of grass from his seat outside the *sadas* with the formula: "O son of a remarried woman, depart; sit on the seat of another who is more foolish than we.

He then sits down with the formula: "May I go up from the lowlands and from the highlands. Then he looks at these two [the heaven and the earth] with the formula: "May Heaven and Earth protect me today. Then he gazes toward the southern half [of the *sadas*]: "Come, O Fathers; may I be rich in fathers through you; may you be rich in offspring through me. Then he gazes toward the northern half for the sake of moving in a counter-clockwise direction.
Then these two Adhvaryus, beginning with the Āhavanīya fire, worship the Āhavanīya in this very manner, likewise the Āgnīdhrīya,
and likewise the Hotrīya.
Having thus turned toward the east while muttering [the mantra], and having thus turned clockwise, they both touch the two eastern doors of the *sadas*. In this manner they enter the *sadas*.

In this manner, from their seats, they both cast out blades of grass outside the *sadas*; the Adhvaryu sits down leaning against the southern door-post, and the Pratiprasthātṛ leans against the northern one. In this manner these two look at each other; in this manner they gaze across toward the southern half and the northern half [of the *sadas*].

Regarding the state of being directed toward the north: then these *vaṣaṭ*-utterers, starting from the Āhavanīya fire, likewise pay homage to the Āhavanīya, likewise to the Āgnīdhrīya; they go around it to the north, and likewise to the Hotrīya.

Thus they turn toward the east and mutter; thus, having turned clockwise, they touch the two eastern doors of the *sadas*; thus they enter the *sadas* by the front, passing along the north of the *dhiṣṇiya*s and around the *dhiṣṇiya* of the *acchāvāka*; thus they cast out blades of grass from their seats outside the *sadas*; thus each sits down according to his own respective *dhiṣṇiya*; thus these two look at one another; thus they look across toward the southern half and the northern half for the sake of establishing the northward orientation; then all these—the Udgātṛs and the Brahman—[perform the same].

The *sadasyas*, those who do not utter the *vaṣaṭ* call, worship the Āhavanīya fire in this very manner, starting from the Āhavanīya; likewise they worship the Āgnīdhrīya fire. They pass around its north side, and likewise [they worship] the Hotrīya fire.
Having turned toward the east, they mutter [the prayers];

having turned clockwise and passed around the north of the *sadas*, they touch the two rear doors of the *sadas* in this manner. In this manner they enter the *sadas*; in this manner they cast out grass-blades from the seats outside the *sadas*. The Udgātṛ priests sit down around the Udumbara post itself.

To the south, the Brahman and the Sadasya sit facing north; thus they look at one another, and likewise they look toward the southern half and the northern half for the sake of their northward arrangement. Now, their path of movement is unconfused: between the *dhiṣṇiya* of the Hotṛ and that of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin—those who have no *dhiṣṇiya*—and then those who possess *dhiṣṇiyas* pass around each of their own respective *dhiṣṇiyas* to the north. When the pressing (*savana*) has concluded, they withdraw by the same route by which they entered.

Having recognized that they have all moved forward, the Adhvaryu asks for the *savanīya* sacrificial cakes. Then the Āgnīdhra, sitting behind the Gārhapatya fire, spreads out five portions in a vessel;
he places the sacrificial cake in the middle, having spread a base of butter and poured butter over it, the roasted grains to the east, the flour-mash to the south, and the parched grain to the west.

Having placed the *āmikṣā* to the north, he then takes hold of these [portions], carries them out by the eastern door, goes around the north of the *sadas*, and having carried them around the north of the *āgnīdhrīya* hearth, he sets them down within the altar. Then, spreading a base of ghee in the *juhū* and *upabhṛt* ladles, he says: "Recite for the morning *prātaḥsāva* of the Indra-related sacrificial cakes as they are being cut.
He cuts twice from the sacrificial cake, twice from the parched grains (*dhānā*), and twice from the flour-mash (*karambha*).
He pours clarified butter over the *parivāpa* twice and over the *āmikṣā* twice; he then anoints [the portions].
Then, for the *sviṣṭakṛt*, he cuts off a single portion from the northern half of each of all [the offerings] into the *upabhṛt* ladle.

He pours clarified butter over them twice, but does not anoint them back. Having stepped across and caused the announcement to be made, he says: "O Hotṛ, recite the *praisha* for the morning offerings of the *puroḍāśas* set forth for Indra.

At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering. Then, while pouring together [the portions], he says: "Recite the *anuvacana* for Agni. Having caused the announcement to be made, he says: "O Hotṛ, recite the *praisha* for Agni."

At the utterance of "vaṣaṭ," he makes the offering in the eastern part of the northern half, passing over the previous offerings; then, having stepped out toward the north and placed the two ladles in their proper places, and having put the *iḍā* into the vessel, he sends the sacrificial cakes westward. Some follow him, saying, "The cattle are the *iḍā*"; then, moving eastward, he says, "Recite for Vāyu and Indra-Vāyu!"

Having heard that, the Pratiprasthātṛ draws the *pratinirgrāhya* portion for Indra and Vāyu from the *droṇakalaśa* with the *pariplu* ladle into the auxiliary vessel belonging to the *ādityasthālī*, saying: "Thou art taken with a support; thou art seated in speech; I take thee for the two protectors of speech, for the two protectors of the ritual, for the two supervisors over the firmness of this sacrifice. Having taken the two vessels, he steps out. As soon as he has stepped out, the Adhvaryu takes the two vessels and hands the *pratinirgrāhya* portion to the Pratiprasthātṛ standing to the north. Now it is indeed said: "Having taken the [cup] for Indra and Vāyu, one should perform the *āghāra* libation."

Having taken a portion from the vessel of clarified butter with the *sruva* spoon and having taken the cup for Indra and Vāyu, he pours the *āghāra* libation, saying: "O gods, may this sacrifice be a peaceful rite (*adhvara*) for the plants, for our cattle, for our people, and for all beings; you are the peaceful rite, so swell with clarity, O divine Soma, svāhā! Then he causes the announcement to be made: "O Śrauṣaṭ! Let it be heard! For Vāyu, for Indra and Vāyu, give the command! When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, the Adhvaryu offers first.

At the second *vaṣaṭ*-call, both offer together. Having offered, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "O Indra and Vāyu, lords of splendor, whatever rival of mine seeks to harm me or overflows against me, here I cast him down beneath my feet, so that I may be exalted as the highest, like Indra.
Then the Pratiprasthātṛ pours the residue of the draught from the Adhvaryu’s cup into his own; the Adhvaryu pours half of it into the Pratiprasthātṛ’s cup.

The Pratiprasthātṛ pours it into the Āditya vessel with the formula, "For the gods thee! Then the Adhvaryu, having turned to the right and hastened westward, hands the cup to the Hotṛ and, moving eastward, says, "Recite for Mitra and Varuṇa! Having heard that, the Pratiprasthātṛ takes the portion to be drawn back for Mitra and Varuṇa from the Droṇakalaśa using the *pariplu* ladle into the reserve cup of the Āditya vessel, with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee for the two protectors of sight, the two protectors of the will, the two supervisors over this firm sacrifice."

Having taken the two cups, he goes out; once he has gone out, the Adhvaryu takes the two cups and hands the *pratinirgrāhya* (the secondary draught) to the Pratiprasthātṛ standing to the north. Then he calls for the *āśrāvaṇa*: "O Śrauṣaṭ! Let it be heard! Pronounce the *praisha* for Mitra and Varuṇa!"

When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, both offer together. Having offered, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "O Mitra and Varuṇa, lords of splendor, whoever attacks us or seeks to overwhelm us as an enemy—here I cast him down beneath my feet, so that I may be preeminent like Indra. Then the Pratiprasthātṛ pours the residue of the draught from the Adhvaryu’s cup into his own; the Adhvaryu pours half of the residue from both cups into the Pratiprasthātṛ’s cup.

The Pratiprasthātṛ pours it into the Āditya vessel with the formula, "For the Viśvedevas, thee! Then the Adhvaryu, having turned to the right and hastened westward, hands the cup to the Hotṛ; moving eastward, he says, "Recite for the Aśvins!

Having heard that, the Pratiprasthātṛ takes the *pratinirgrāhya* portion of the Aśvin draught from the Droṇakalaśa with the dipping-spoon into the reserve vessel of the Āditya vessel, with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; thou art seated in hearing, I take thee for the two hearers, for the two guardians of the rite, for the two supervisors of this firm sacrifice."
Having taken the two cups, he goes out;

once he has gone out, the Adhvaryu takes the two cups and hands the *pratinirgrāhya* (the portion to be added) to the Pratiprasthātṛ standing to the north. Then he causes the announcement to be made: "Ośrāvaya! Let it be heard! *Praṣya* for the Aśvins!"

When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, both offer together. Having offered, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "O Aśvins, lords of splendor, whoever assails us or seeks to overwhelm us as an enemy—here I cast him down beneath my feet, so that I may be preeminent like Indra. Then the Pratiprasthātṛ pours the residue of the cup from the Adhvaryu’s vessel into his own; the Adhvaryu pours half of it into the Pratiprasthātṛ’s vessel.
The Pratiprasthātṛ then pours that into the Āditya vessel with the formula: "For all the gods, thee!"
If, indeed, the vessel is more than half full with these residues, he covers it with this very lid.

If it does not have an upper half, having placed it so that it has an upper half over the *droṇakalaśa*, he covers it with this very vessel, saying: "O Viṣṇu of the wide stride, this is your Soma; guard it! Let no evil-eyed one look upon it! Then the Adhvaryu, having turned to the right, having run back toward the west, having handed the vessel to the Hotṛ, and having stepped forward to the east, says: "Recite for those being filled! Fill the cups following the Hotṛ’s cup; make them bright on both sides; O Acchāvāka’s cup-bearer, do not [fill] him..."

"O Pratiprasthātṛ, you shall draw [the Soma]; with four splinters, some sprinkled and some unsprinkled, receive [the Soma] back," they say; they act according to this direction. First they draw from the *droṇakalaśa*, then from the *pūtabhṛt*, then from the *droṇakalaśa*.

Since they are pure on both sides, they first draw the *hotṛ*’s cup; having drawn the others as they come, they set them down upon the *uttaravedi*. Then the *pratiprasthātṛ* sprinkles two of the four wooden chips.
Two [soma vessels] remain unsprinkled;
having covered them with two that have been sprinkled, they take up the two that are unsprinkled;
the Adhvaryu takes up the bright one.
The Pratiprasthātṛ, taking the two cups of the *manthin* [mixture], goes out; the Adhvaryu goes out leaning against the southern doorpost, and the Pratiprasthātṛ leans against the northern one.

Behind the northern altar, the two of them join the cups together, saying: "Join the life-span; quicken that for me! Join the out-breath; quicken that for me! Join the in-breath; quicken that for me! Join the diffused breath; quicken that for me! Join the eye; quicken that for me! Join the ear; quicken that for me!"

"You are praised, O sustainer of people; may the gods who drink the *śukra* lead you forward. Procreating offspring rich in heroes, go around as the bright one, O bright one with bright luster!"—with these words, the *adhvaryu* circumambulates the northern altar by the south.

"You are praised, O sustainer of people; may the gods who drink the *manthin* lead you forward. Procreating offspring rich in progeny, go around as the churning one, O churning one with churning luster!"—with these words, the *pratiprasthātṛ* circumambulates the northern altar by the north.

The two [Adhvaryus] run toward the northern altar from the east, facing westward: "With Indra as our ally, may we overcome those who attack us, slaying the Vṛtras without opposition. "O Agni, with that splendor (*tejas*) which is yours, may I become splendid; with that radiance (*varcas*) which is yours, O Agni, may I become radiant; with that heat (*haras*) which is yours, O Agni, may I become hot. Then, between the sacrificial post (*yūpa*) and the Āhavanīya fire, they join the two cups together: "You are life; bestow life upon me; bestow life upon the sacrifice; bestow life upon the lord of the sacrifice."

Abiding in the out-breath (*prāṇa*), bestow out-breath upon me; bestow out-breath upon the sacrifice; bestow out-breath upon the lord of the sacrifice. Abiding in the in-breath (*apāna*), bestow in-breath upon me; bestow in-breath upon the sacrifice; bestow in-breath upon the lord of the sacrifice. Abiding in the diffused breath (*vyāna*), bestow diffused breath upon me; bestow diffused breath upon the sacrifice; bestow diffused breath upon the lord of the sacrifice. Abiding in sight (*cakṣus*), bestow sight upon me; bestow sight upon the sacrifice; bestow sight upon the lord of the sacrifice. Abiding in hearing (*śrotra*), bestow hearing upon me.
With the six *saṃdhā* formulas—"Give ear for the sacrifice; give ear for the lord of the sacrifice"—they join together and step out.

They say: "May you two gods, Śukra and Manthin, arrange the divine subjects; arrange the human subjects; bestow food and vigor upon us; bestow breaths upon the cattle; bestow offspring upon me and the sacrificer. Then they throw two unanointed wood-shavings outside the altar, saying: "Śaṇḍa is cast out along with so-and-so," while the Adhvaryu meditates in his mind upon whomsoever the sacrificer hates.

"The monkey has been driven away along with him"—thus thinking, the Pratiprasthātṛ mentally contemplates whoever the sacrificer hates; then, having touched water, they both place the two sprinkled [pieces of wood] on the fire.

"O Śukra, this is your fuel-stick; with it may you be kindled, svāhā!"—thus says the Adhvaryu. "O Manthin, this is your fuel-stick; with it may you be kindled, svāhā!"—thus says the Pratiprasthātṛ. At this time, the Camasādhvaryus lift up the cups. Then the Adhvaryu, standing in front facing west, causes the announcement to be made: "O Śrauṣaṭ! Let it be heard! O Hotṛ, do you recite the offering prayer for the Soma juices of the morning pressing, accompanied by the Śukra and Manthin, dripping with sweetness—the Somas set forth for Indra!"

When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, both offer together: "He is the first creator, Viśvakarman; he is the first Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni; he is the first Bṛhaspati, the wise one. To him, O Indra, I offer the pressed [soma] with 'svāhā'!
At the *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *vaṣaṭ*, they both offer twice.

In the same manner, they offer the *camasa*s of all [the priests] twice each; then he issues the command: "Let the *camasa* of the Hotṛ go forward, that of the Brahman, that of the Udgātṛ, that of the Sacrificer, and that of the Sadasya! O *camasādhvaryu*s of the *hotrakas*, having drawn [Soma] once each from the *droṇakalaśa*, turn back! O *camasādhvaryu* of the Hotṛ, come hither! O Pratiprasthātṛ, offer the residue of the *manthin* cup upon the northern half of the Āhavanīya fire!"

They act according to the direction given. Then, having turned to the right, he pours the residue of the draught into the Hotṛ’s cup, either with the formula, "I pour thee, who art offered, into the offered; full of vigor for the gods, full of sweetness for men," or silently. Then the Pratiprasthātṛ offers the residue of the Manthin vessel on the northern half of the Āhavanīya fire with the formula: "O Rudra, this is thy portion which thou didst demand; enjoy it! May we obtain cattle-wealth, abundance of riches, and goodly heroes; may there be well-being for a year!"
Saying "svāhā," he then touches water and places the *śukra* cup and the *manthin* cup on the mound (*khara*) in their respective places.
These cups of the great officiating priests (*mahartvij*) are carried away; then the cup-bearers of the *hotraka*s return after having drawn [soma] once each from the *droṇakalaśa*.
Taking the cup of the *maitrāvaruṇa*, and having called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says, "O *praśāstṛ*, sacrifice! (*praśāstar yaja*).
At the *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *anuvaṣaṭ*, he makes two offerings.

Having performed the five *saṃyājya* oblations with the calls, "O Brahman, sacrifice! O Potṛ, sacrifice! O Neṣṭṛ, sacrifice! O Agnīdh, sacrifice!", he turns to the right, hastens back toward the west, and sits down in front of the Hotṛ. The Hotṛ says, "The Agnīdh has sacrificed," and the Adhvaryu replies, "May it be auspicious for him who will cause us to drink King Soma. Then the Hotṛ takes the cup for Indra and Vāyu.

The Adhvaryu takes hold of himself; when the Adhvaryu has taken hold of him, the Hotṛ, having sought permission (*upahava*), consumes [the portion] in the manner he knows. When the Hotṛ has taken hold of him, the Adhvaryu, having sought permission, consumes [it], saying: "In me is the Vasu, the Purovasu, the protector of speech; protect my speech. Then the Hotṛ consumes, then the Adhvaryu; he then attaches this [portion] to the Hotṛ.
The Hotṛ places it in its proper place. Then the Hotṛ takes the cup of Mitrāvaruṇa.

The Adhvaryu takes hold of himself; when the Adhvaryu has taken hold [of him], the Hotṛ, having sought permission, consumes [the cup] in the manner he knows. When the Hotṛ has taken hold [of him], the Adhvaryu, having sought permission, consumes [it], saying: "May I be a Vasu, a finder of wealth; O protector of the eye, protect my eye. Then he hands it over to the Hotṛ;
the Hotṛ places it in its proper place. Then the Hotṛ takes the Āśvina vessel.
The Adhvaryu takes hold of himself;

when the Adhvaryu has taken hold [of him], the Hotṛ, having sought permission, consumes [the portion] in the manner he knows. When the Hotṛ has taken hold [of him], the Adhvaryu, having sought permission, consumes [it], saying: "In me is wealth, the gatherer of wealth; protector of hearing, protect my hearing."

"He consumes the Āśvina cup with a complete circumambulation," so says the Brāhmaṇa. Then he hands it over to the Hotṛ; the Hotṛ places it in its proper position, and then, having touched water, they lift up the *iḍā* for the Hotṛ.

While the *iḍā* is being invoked, they hold the cups close; once the *iḍā* has been invoked, there remains an unplaced portion for the *āgnīdhra*. Then he makes these vessels dedicated to the dual deities non-empty:
he throws a fragment of the sacrificial cake into the cup for Indra and Vāyu, and the curd-mixture (*āmikṣā*) into the cup for Mitra and Varuṇa.

The parched grains are for the Āśvina cup; then, having taken them up together and brought them out by the eastern door, he causes them to enter the *havirdhāna* shed by the western door and places them on the northern track of the southern *havirdhāna*.
They remain there until the third pressing; then he places them in the *āgnīdhra* fire-pan, and they consume the portion consisting of six cuttings.

Having cleansed themselves, they consume the cups after the *iḍā* has been invoked, reciting the long *bhakṣa*-formula: "Consume! Enter me! Having recited this, [they say]: "O God Soma, of thee who belongest to the Vasu-group, who knowest the mind, who art drunk by Indra at the morning pressing, whose metre is the *gāyatrī*, who art full of sweetness, and who hast been invited—I, being invited, partake.
These three, having invited one another, consume the *hotṛ*'s cup; the others consume their respective cups according to their own vessels.
Touching themselves with the words, "Impel me," they cause the cups to swell with the mantra, "Swell up; let [the milk] come to you.

Having been made to swell, the Nārāśaṃsa goblets are placed one below the other along the rear support of the southern *havirdhāna* cart for the offering to Indra and Agni. Then this *acchāvāka* sits in front of the *sadas*; to him, placing a large piece of sacrificial cake, he says, "O *acchāvāka*, speak what is to be spoken by you."

When he recognizes the Acchāvāka’s [verse], "O Brahmins, call upon the Brahmins," then he says, "O Hotṛ, this Acchāvāka desires an invitation; invite him. The Hotṛ invites him with a ṛc-verse. Then, moving forward, he says, "Recite for the Soma being drawn; O Camasādhvaryu of the Acchāvāka, draw [the Soma]; make it bright on both sides. He does so accordingly. Then, having gone forward and taken the Acchāvāka’s cup, and having called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says, "O Acchāvāka, recite the offering prayer (*yajya*)."

Having offered at the *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *anu-vaṣaṭ*, he carries away the portion for consumption. If the Acchāvāka desires an invitation (*upahava*) from him, he indeed invites him; however, the two do not consume together.
The Nārāśaṃsa cup, having been replenished, sits down. Then he says: "Acchāvāka, sit down! Neṣṭṛ, lead the wife forward! Agnīdh, announce to me that the Acchāvāka has sat down!"
This Acchāvāka sits down behind his own Dhiṣṇiya hearth.

The Neṣṭṛ leads the wife forward, taking the *pannejani* waters, with this formula: "Go forth! Come up! Having caused her to go out by the eastern door and having led her into the Sadas by the western door, he sets down the *pannejani* waters behind the Neṣṭṛ’s Dhiṣṇiya, on a path not used for traffic, along the route of the Sāman, with the formula: "I set you down as *pannejani* waters for the Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas, and the Viśvedevas; I set you down as *pannejani* waters for the sacrifice. Then the Agnīdhra says: "The Acchāvāka has sat down; [approach] the Acchāvāka who has sat down."

At this time, while the water for washing the feet is being offered, the sacrificer eats of the sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa*) in the Āgnīdhra shed if he intends to eat; the wife eats them in the wife’s shed if she intends to eat. Then the two take up the seasonal cups: the Adhvaryu takes the southern one, and the Pratiprasthātṛ takes the northern one. The Adhvaryu first draws from the *droṇakalaśa* with the Vāyavya cup, saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Madhu. Then the Pratiprasthātṛ draws, saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Mādhava."

As they go out taking the cups, the Adhvaryu goes out leaning against the southern door-post, while the Pratiprasthātṛ stops leaning against the northern door-post. Then the Adhvaryu calls for the *śrauṣaṭ*: "Oṃ śrāvaya! Astu śrauṣaṭ! [O Hotṛ], give the command for the season!
At the *vaṣaṭ*-call, he makes the offering;
the Pratiprasthātṛ, meanwhile, simply goes out.

The Adhvaryu steps forward; he takes [the cup], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Śukra. Then the Pratiprasthātṛ causes [the Āgnīdhra] to announce: "O announce! "Let it be heard! "With the Season, give the command!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering.
The Adhvaryu steps out, and the Pratiprasthātṛ enters;

he takes [the cup] with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Śuci. Then the Adhvaryu causes the announcement: "O announce! Let it be heard! O Ṛtu, give the command!"
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he offers;
the Pratiprasthātṛ steps out,
and the Adhvaryu enters.

He draws [the cup], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Nabhas. Then the Pratiprasthātṛ causes the announcement to be made: "O announce! "Let it be heard! "For the Season, give the command!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers the oblation;
the Adhvaryu, however, steps out.
The Pratiprasthātṛ approaches;

he takes [the draught] with the formula, "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Nabhasya. Then the Adhvaryu causes the announcement to be made: "O announce! Let it be heard! With the Ṛtu, give the command!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering.

The Pratiprasthātṛ indeed steps out, while the Adhvaryu enters; having turned the vessel over, he draws [the draught] with the formula, "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, the beloved, for Īṣa. Then the Pratiprasthātṛ calls for the *śrauṣaṭ*—"O Śrauṣaṭ! Let it be heard! With the season, give the command!"—and at the *vaṣaṭ*-call, he makes the offering.
The Adhvaryu goes out, while the Pratiprasthātṛ enters; having turned the vessel upside down, he takes it up with the formula:
"Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable for strength. Then the Adhvaryu causes the announcement to be made: "O Śrauṣaṭ! Let it be heard! 'Prompt [the Hotṛ] by means of the seasons!'"
When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he offers the oblation; the Pratiprasthātṛ steps out,
and the Adhvaryu enters.

He takes [the draught] with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, the beloved one, for Sahas. Then the Pratiprasthātṛ causes [the Āgnīdhra] to announce: "O announce! "Let it be heard! "For the Seasons, give the command!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers the oblation;
the Adhvaryu then steps out.
The Pratiprasthātṛ steps forward;

he takes [the draught] with the formula, "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Sahasya. Then the Adhvaryu causes [the Āgnīdhra] to cry out, "O Śrauṣaṭ! Let it be heard! O Ṛtus, give the command!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers the oblation.

The Pratiprasthātṛ indeed goes out, while the Adhvaryu enters; turning the vessel upside down, he draws [the draught] with the formula: "Thou art taken with a base; I take thee, acceptable to Tapas. Then the Pratiprasthātṛ causes the announcement to be made: "O announce! "Let it be heard! "Oṁ śrauṣaṭ! Command for the Seasons!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers the oblation.

The Adhvaryu goes out, and the Pratiprasthātṛ enters, having turned his vessel upside down; the Adhvaryu says to him, "O Pratiprasthātṛ, rest with this vessel. Then the Adhvaryu calls for the announcement: "O Śrauṣaṭ! Let it be heard! Command for the season! The Praśāstṛ says, "O two Adhvaryus, sacrifice! The Adhvaryu says, "O Hotṛ, sacrifice this! At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, the Adhvaryu makes the offering.
He approaches the Pratiprasthātṛ who is seated right there.

First, the Pratiprasthātṛ draws [the cup], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Tapaḥ. Then the Adhvaryu draws [his], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; thou art Saṃsarpa; I take thee, acceptable to Aṅgirasvat and Bārhaspatya. Having taken hold of the two cups, they both go out. The Adhvaryu goes out leaning against the southern door-post, and the Pratiprasthātṛ leans against the northern one.
In this rite, the Pratiprasthātṛ causes [the announcement] to be heard: "Oṃ śrāvaya! Let it be heard! Oṣaṭ! With the season, give the command!
The Praśāstṛ says, "O Gṛhapati, sacrifice! and the Gṛhapati says, "O Hotṛ, sacrifice this!"
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, both offer together; then the Pratiprasthātṛ pours the residue of the draught from the Adhvaryu’s vessel into his own.
He says to him, "O Pratiprasthātṛ, take the draught for Indra and Agni with this vessel.

With that, the Pratiprasthātṛ takes the draught for Indra and Agni from the *droṇakalaśa* using the *pariplu* ladle, having recited the verse, "O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed juice," and then saying, "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Indra and Agni."

Having wiped it, he sets it down with the formula: "This is thy womb; for Indra and Agni, thee! Then the Adhvaryu, having turned to the right and hastened westward, causes the Hotṛ to consume this cup with the formula: "Of that which has been drunk by the Seasons," [adding] "by the Hotṛ, the Potṛ, the Neṣṭṛ, the Āgnīdh, the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, and the Maitrāvaruṇa. Then, having turned the cup over, the Hotṛ alone consumes it four times with the formula: "Of that which has been drunk by the Seasons," [adding] "by the Hotṛ, the Potṛ, the Neṣṭṛ, and the Acchāvāka. Then, having again turned the cup over, the Hotṛ alone consumes it twice with the formula: "Of that which has been drunk by the Season."
Then he asks the Hotṛ: "Will you recite the *praṇava* in a low voice, [recite] the *śaṃsa*, [recite] the *siṣya*, and [recite] with distinct pauses?

Having heard how the Hotṛ replies to him, and having grasped the vessel, he turns away. As long as it takes to complete this *yajus* formula—"The *iḍā* is the invocation of the gods"—he mutters it. The Hotṛ calls out to him, and the Adhvaryu responds.
When there is a *śaṃs*,
he responds with a *pratigara*; when it is in a low tone (*upāṃśu*), he responds in a low tone.
When [the Hotṛ] recites loudly, he responds loudly;
whether continuously or with pauses,
having responded to the well-known hymn (uktha), he goes forward facing east and lifts up this cup for Indra and Agni.
The Nārāśaṃsa cups are lifted up;
then he causes the announcement to be made: "Ośrāvaya! Astu śrauṣaṭ! O reciter of the hymn (ukthaśas), offer the oblation of Soma!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *anuvaṣaṭ*, he offers twice.
In the same way, they shake the *nārāśaṃsa* cups twice each;
