they follow this cup with the *nārāśaṃsa*s.

At each pressing, the Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu together consume this cup with the formula: "Of that which was drunk by Indra and Agni... [and] "O divine Soma, of thee who art drunk by the *Narāśaṃsa*, who knowest the mind, who belongest to the morning pressing, whose metre is the *Gāyatrī*, who art drunk by the Fathers, who art full of sweetness, and who hast been invited—I, being invited, partake."
These three, having invited one another, consume from the *hotṛ*’s cup alone;

they consume from their respective cups while touching themselves with the formula, "Impel me," and they cause the cups to swell with the formulas, "Swell up! Let [the draught] come to you! and so forth.

The Nārāśaṃsa cups, having been replenished, sink down below the support of the southern *havirdhāna* cart for the sake of the Vaiśvadeva draught. Then, having gone eastward while taking up the *śukra* cup, he says: "O Unnetṛ, when I take this Vaiśvadeva draught, then cause the King Soma to flow through the *pūtabhṛt* filter toward the north; O Droṇakalaśa, having wiped [the cup] with the fringed cloth (*daśā*), turn it face down.

He does so. With the *śukra* cup, he draws from the *kalaśa* the Vaiśvadeva draught, reciting: "Omāsaḥ carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ," and then: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to the Viśve Devas."

Having wiped [the ladle], he sets it down with the formula, "This is thy womb; for the Viśve Devas, thee! Then, having touched water and taken two blades of *barhis* grass, restraining his speech, he hastens westward and introduces the *stotra* for the Vaiśvadeva hymn.
When they announce to the Hotṛ, "The Vaiśvadeva is being chanted; this is the last [verse]," the Adhvaryu turns away from the Hotṛ's position, and the Hotṛ calls out to him.
The Adhvaryu calls back; he recites; he responds.
Having responded with the well-known *uktha*, he goes forward and lifts up this *vaiśvadeva* cup;
they lift up the *nārāśaṃsa* goblets in succession, and then he calls for the announcement: "O Śrauṣaṭ! Let it be heard! O reciter of the *uktha*, sacrifice to Soma!"
At the *vaṣaṭ* call and at the subsequent *anu-vaṣaṭ* call, he offers twice;

likewise, they shake the *nārāśaṃsa* cups twice each. They follow this cup with the *nārāśaṃsas*. The consumption [of the Soma] at each pressing is performed with the formula: "Of that which has been drunk by the All-gods. Both the Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu consume this cup together with the formula: "With the drinking of Narāśaṃsa. [The Hotṛ recites: "O divine Soma, of thee who art drunk by Narāśaṃsa, who knowest the mind, who belongest to the morning pressing, who hast the Gāyatrī metre, who art drunk by the Fathers, who art full of sweetness, and who art invited—I, being invited, partake."
Having invited one another, these three consume from the Hotṛ’s cup alone;
they touch themselves individually with the formula, "Impel the cups; impel me."
They do not fill the cups;

having consumed the entire contents, they perform the *mārjana* purification. Then he says, "O Pratiprasthātṛ, having purified these four vessels and this Śukra vessel at the Mārjālīya mound, pour them back into the [original] vessels.
He does so accordingly. Then, moving forward toward the east, he says:
"Fill the cups following the cup of the Maitrāvaruṇa; O Unnetṛ, prepare the Soma!
Thus they fill the cup of the Maitrāvaruṇa first, and the others as they come.

Having poured it out, they set it down on the Uttaravedi. Then he takes the secondary cup belonging to the Ukthya-vessel; in that [cup], he draws the third portion of this King [Soma] which remains in the Ukthya-vessel, with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, agreeable to Mitra and Varuna, for the gods, thee who art god-seeking, for the Ukthyas, thee who art Ukthya-seeking, for the life of the sacrifice.
With the words, "Thou art a repeated oblation," he touches the Ukthya-vessel again.

Having wiped it, he sets it down with the formula, "This is thy womb; for Mitra and Varuṇa, thee! Then, having touched water and taken two blades of *barhis* grass, restraining his speech, he hastens westward and introduces the chant.
They say, "The Maitrāvaruṇa's [turn] is the last; let him chant."
After the time of the Maitrāvaruṇa, the Adhvaryu turns away; the Maitrāvaruṇa calls out to him,
and the Adhvaryu responds with the call *śaṃsati*.
He responds with the well-known *uktha*; having responded, he goes forward and lifts up this cup;
the *camasa* vessels are lifted up after it.
Then he causes [the Āgnīdhra] to announce: "O announce! Let it be heard! *Oṣaṭ*! O reciter of the hymn (*ukthashā*), sacrifice the Soma-libations!

At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* and at the subsequent *anu-vaṣaṭ*, he makes two offerings. In the same manner, they offer each of their own goblets twice. Then, having turned to the right, he pours the residue of the draught into the goblet of the Maitrāvaruṇa, saying: "I pour thee, who hast been offered, into that which has been offered—full of vigor for the gods, full of sweetness for men. Or rather, having silently set down this very vessel right there, they come back toward the west with the portions for consumption. The formula for consumption at each pressing is: "Of what has been drunk by Mitra and Varuṇa..."
Having invited one another, these three consume the cup belonging to Mitrāvaruṇa alone;
they touch themselves individually with the formula, "Impel the cups according to their respective vessels; impel me."
They do not swell the cups;
having consumed all the portions, they perform the *mārjana* purification. Then he says, "O Pratiprasthātṛ, proceed with your two cups.
Having heard this, the Pratiprasthātṛ, moving forward, says:
"O Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, fill up your cup; O Unnetṛ, make the Soma increase!
Thus they first fill the cup of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, and the others as they come along.

Having drawn it up, they set it down on the *uttaravedi*. Then he takes the secondary cup (*aupasaya*) from the *ukthya-sthālī*; in it he takes a half-measure of this King [Soma] which remains in the *ukthya-sthālī*, saying: "Thou art taken with a support; for the gods thee, god-loving; for the *ukthyas* thee, *uktha*-loving; for the life of the sacrifice! O Indra, I take thee who art dear. He touches the *ukthya-sthālī* again, saying, "Thou art a renewed oblation.

Having wiped it, he sets it down, saying, "This is thy womb; O Indra, I take thee who art dear. Then, having touched water and taken two blades of *barhis* grass, restraining his speech, he hastens westward and introduces the chant (*stotra*).
They say, "This is the last [verse] for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin as he praises.
From the time of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, the Pratiprasthātṛ turns away; the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin calls out to him.
The Pratiprasthātṛ calls back, the Hotṛ recites, and the Adhvaryu responds.
Having responded with the well-known *mukha*, he goes forward and lifts up this cup;
they lift up the goblets after it.
Then he calls for the announcement: "O Śrauṣaṭ! Let it be heard! Recite the offering prayer for the Soma-pressings that possess the glory of the *uktha*!"

He offers twice—at the *vaṣaṭ* call and at the subsequent *anuvaṣaṭ* call—and likewise, they offer their respective cups twice each. Then, having turned to the right, he pours the residue of the draught into the cup of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, saying: "I pour thee, who art offered, into the already offered; full of vigor for the gods, full of sweetness for men. Or rather, having silently set down that vessel right there, they turn back with the portions for consumption. The formula for consuming at each pressing is: "Of what has been drunk by Indra... These three, having invited one another, consume the cup of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin itself.
With the words, "Impel the cups according to their respective vessels; impel me," they touch themselves,
but they do not cause the cups to swell.
When they have cleansed themselves after eating everything, he says, "O Prastotṛ, chant the *prastāva* for the Acchāvāka. Then, while moving forward, he says:

"Fill the cups following the cup of the Acchāvāka; O Unnetṛ, fill the King [Soma] entirely, do not leave any remainder. O Pratiprasthātṛ, come with this cup. Come, O Sacrificer! Having caused him to enter the *havirdhāna* shed by the eastern door, he then spreads out this skin upon the two boards, with its neck toward the east and the hair upward, either with the formula "O Sacrifice, be established" or silently.

Having placed stones face-to-face in front of it, he brings down the King (Soma) between the two poles of the southern *havirdhāna* cart with two verses: "For the heart thee! For the mind thee! O King Soma, come hither; descend! Then they announce him to the *udgātṛ*s, and they perform upon him whatever rites they know. Then, having turned the *ādhavanīya* vessel upside down, he pours half of the *vasatīvarī* waters into it and half of the *ekadhana* waters. He places the *vasatīvarī* waters in front of the axle and the *ekadhana* waters behind the axle.
They first draw out the cup of the Acchāvāka; they draw out the others as they arise;
having drawn out the King [Soma] entirely, they place them together on the Uttaravedi.

Then he takes the secondary cup from the Ukthya vessel; into it he draws the entire King Soma that remains in the Ukthya vessel, with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, agreeable to the gods, the god-loving, for the Ukthyas, the hymn-loving, for the life of the sacrifice, for Indra and Agni.
Here he does not touch the Ukthya vessel again with the words "Thou art the oblation"; rather, having wiped it with the fringes of the cloth, he turns it upside down.

Having wiped it, he sets it down with the formula, "This is thy womb; for Indra and Agni, thee! Then, having touched water and taken two blades of *barhis* grass, restraining his speech, he hastens westward and introduces the chant.
They say to the Acchāvāka, "This is the last [verse]. From the time of the Acchāvāka, the Pratiprasthātṛ turns away from him. The Acchāvāka calls out to him, and the Pratiprasthātṛ responds.
When there is the word "śam," he responds; having responded with the well-known *uktha*, he goes forward and lifts up this cup.
The goblets are lifted up;
then he causes the announcement to be made: "Ośrāvaya! Astu śrauṣaṭ! O reciter of the hymn (ukthaśas), sacrifice the Soma-libations!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* and at the subsequent *anuvaṣaṭ*, he makes two offerings.

In the same manner, they offer the *soma* from all the cups twice each; then, having turned to the right, he pours the residue of the draught into the *acchāvāka’s* cup, either with the formula, "I pour thee, who hast been offered, into what has been offered—full of vigor for the gods, full of sweetness for men," or silently. Having set this vessel down right there, they move westward with the portions for consumption (*bhakṣa*). The portion for consumption is according to the libation, with the formula, "Of that which was drunk by Indra and Agni. These three, having invited one another, consume the *acchāvāka’s* cup alone.
Then they touch themselves, cup by cup, with the formula, "Impel me! and so forth.
They do not swell the cups;
having consumed the entire contents, they perform the *mārjana* purification. Then he says, "O reciter of the *uktha*, having responded to the morning pressing, O *praśāstṛ*, give the command!"
"Creep forward," says the Praśāstṛ;
the morning pressing concludes;
they proceed to the midday pressing with the [verse] "O divine doors," from this very point upwards.
Having recognized that they have all moved forward, the Adhvaryu, stepping forward toward the east, calls out: "O pressers, come! O Grāvastut, come! O Sacrificer, come!

Having caused the Sacrificer to enter the Havirdhāna shed by the eastern door, and having poured water from the Vasatīvarī waters into the Hotṛ’s cup, he makes the Sacrificer recite over those same *nigrābhya* waters as before. Having handed those over to the Sacrificer in the same manner, he takes up a pressing stone other than the one used for the silent pressing (*upāṃśusavana*).
Having fixed it facing eastward in the same way and loosened it, he measures the King Soma over the pressing stone with the formula: "For Indra thee! For Indra thee!"

Measuring five times with the *yajus* formula and five times silently, he measures the King [Soma] in its entirety ten times. Having sprinkled it with water, he hands the turban to the *grāvastut*. Having likewise sprinkled it with water, they carry the garment to the residence of the *adhvaryu*. He then mixes the measured King [Soma] with the waters contained in the *hotṛ*-cup; thus he stirs it together.
In the same manner he touches the skin and the wooden board; in the same manner he causes the *vṛddhi* verses to be recited; he does not touch the *nāntra* and the *aṃśu*.
They press [the Soma] here, there, and here, making it resound with "ihā, ihā, ihā";

they discipline it well, saying "ihā, ihā, ihā, ihā, ihā, ihā. Then, at the time of gathering, they play about, saying "ihā, ihā, ihā. Having gathered it well into the gathering-vessel, he hands it over to the Unnetṛ; the Unnetṛ pours it out into the Adhvaniya vessel. In this very manner the second turn is completed, and likewise the third.

On the third day of the third [pressing], they approach with the *bṛhat* chant, saying "The great, the great, the great! Finally, having wrapped the *ṛjīṣa* in a fringe of the *daśāpavitra*, he hands it to the *unnetṛ*.
The *unnetṛ*, having rinsed it in the *ādhavanīya* jar and squeezed it out, brings it down between the two poles of the southern *havirdhāna* cart and places it upon the hide.
Having arranged the pressing-stones facing each other upon that [hide] in the same manner as before, he distributes this *ṛjīṣa* in four parts from the mouths of the stones.
Likewise, either the Udgātṛ or the Prastotṛ, having approached the axle behind the southern *havirdhāna* cart, places the *droṇakalaśa* upon the pressing-stones facing eastward.

Having spread over it the *daśāpavitra* filter with its fringes pointing northward, he draws the *śukra* and *manthin* cups in the established manner; then, with the two seasonal vessels (*ṛtupātra*), he draws the two *marutvatīya* cups with the two verses:
"O Indra, the bull accompanied by the Maruts, the one who has grown great... O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, drink the Soma here."
Then, having drawn the Āgrayaṇa from above, he draws it up from below;
having likewise uttered the *abhihiṅkāra* over it three times and wiped it around, he sets it down.
In the same manner he draws the Ukthya cup, and with the Ukthya he concludes the King [Soma].

Likewise, having thrown the *pariplu* vessel into the *droṇakalaśa* which is half-full, he consecrates the drops with the formulas: "The drop has fallen," "Thy drop," "The drop," and "Thy drop. Then he says to the *unnetṛ*: "Make the *pūtabhṛt* empty; I shall draw the cups of the *pavamāna*. Thereupon, when the *pūtabhṛt* is empty, he draws the cups of the *pavamāna*, touching the *droṇakalaśa* with "Thou art taken with a support; for Indra thee! and the *ādhavanīya* with "For Indra thee!"
"O Unnetṛ, [with the words] 'Indrāya tvā' (For Indra thee), pour the King [Soma] forward into the *pūtabhṛt* vessel; having wiped the *ādhavanīya* with the fringes, turn it upside down.
He does so.
Then, having touched water and taken two blades of *barhis* grass, he steps out.
When they have likewise taken hold of those [vessels], he offers a spoonful (sruvāhuti) into the Āhavanīya fire with this [verse]:

"May the Viśve Devas, the Maruts, and Indra not abandon us at this second pressing; may we, long-lived and speaking what is pleasing to them, abide in the good favor of the gods, Svāhā! With this verse, the two Adhvaryus offer, while the others offer according to their respective Vedas. Then, having turned to the right, they proceed toward the Sadas for the Pavamāna laud; thus they sit down in the Sadas, each in his proper place.

In the same way, he gives two blades of sacrificial grass (*barhis*) to either the Udgātṛ or the Prastotṛ, either with the formula, "Thou art the under-layer for the Ṛc and the Sāman; for the procreation of the pair," or silently.
Likewise, he mutters the introductory prayer: "Vāyu is the utterer of *hiṃ*. This constitutes the fifteenfold midday Pavamāna-stotra.

When that eighth [offering] has been introduced, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "Thou art Suparṇa, having the Triṣṭubh metre; I take hold of thee; lead me safely across. At this point, he recites the Caturhotṛ formula. When the Sāman has been chanted, he issues the direction: "O Āgnīdh, spread the fires; strew the sacrificial grass; prepare the sacrificial cakes; O Pratiprasthātṛ, bring curds for the Dadhigharma.
The two of them perform according to the direction. Then, having touched water, he says: "Come, O sacrificer!"

Having caused [the sacrificer] to enter the *havirdhāna* shed by the eastern door, he worships the King Soma in his entirety; he proceeds with the ritual in the same manner as the *avakāśa* offerings,
and likewise draws [the butter] nine times into the *pracaraṇī* ladle.

In the same manner, this Āgnīdhra priest distributes the embers from the Āgnīdhrīya hearth onto the other Dhiṣṇiya hearths in successive order; likewise, sitting in front facing westward, he sprinkles clarified butter over the distributed Dhiṣṇiyas; and likewise, he places the Pracaraṇī ladle on the front corner of the northern Havirdhāna cart.
In the same way, he spreads the *pṛṣṭhya* grass-blades along the path leading from the Gārhapatya fire to the Āhavanīya fire so that they form a continuous line.
Then, sitting between the two *havirdhāna* carts, he asks for the curds for the *dadhigharma* offering;
when it has been brought, he gazes upon it, saying: "Thou art light, belonging to Vaiśvānara, the milk of the speckled cow."

Having placed two blades of *barhis* grass between [the vessel and the soma], he draws [the draught] into a bronze cup or a wooden goblet with the formula: "As great as heaven and earth are in magnitude, and as far as the seven rivers extend—so great a draught of yours, O Indra, do I draw with strength, unsubdued. Having removed the two blades of *barhis*, he then mixes it with curds, saying: "May speech and mind mix you; may out-breath and in-breath mix you; may sight and hearing mix you; may skill and strength mix you; may vigor and power mix you; and may life-span [mix you]."

"May old age and glory blend with you; may the self and the body blend with you. You are cooked; you have been made cooked. For the cooked one, for the cooked ones, for you who have been made cooked—thus saying, 'Make [it] cooked,' he then says, 'O Hotṛ, speak what is to be spoken by you. Then, taking it up and rising, he says, 'The oblation is cooked. Having stepped across and called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says, 'Recite the offering prayer (*yajya*) for the Dadhigharma.'"

When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he offers [the oblation] with: "O Indra, whom they call Varuṇa, whom they call Mitra, whom they call Truth; he who is the most divine among the gods, born of fervor (*tapas*)—to him, to thee, to them, *svāhā*! Having offered it when the *anu-vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he carries away the portion for consumption. Having sought permission from as many priests as there are of the *pravargya*, the sacrificer alone consumes it directly, [reciting]: "In me be that great power (*indriya*), in me skill, in me resolve; in me has been placed heroic vigor; may the three-fold *gharma* shine upon me."

"With intention and with mind, with sovereign power and with light, with sacrifice and with milk, with sacred formulation and with brilliance, with dominion and with glory, with truth and with austerity—may we partake of its milking; may we partake of its favor; may we partake of its consumption. Of that which has been drunk by Indra, which is honey-sweet, and of which [I] have been invited, being myself invited, I consume.
Having rinsed the vessel, he hands it over.
In the same manner, he calls for the sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa*) belonging to the *savana* offerings.
Cutting portions from them in the same manner, he says, "Recite for the sacrificial cakes being cut for Indra at the midday pressing.
Having cut from the front half, he cuts from the rear half, pours clarified butter over it, and anoints the place from which the portion was taken.
Similarly, for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering in the *upabhṛt* ladle, he cuts portions once each from the northern half of all [the cakes];

he pours clarified butter over them twice; he does not re-anoint [the cakes]; having stepped across and called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says: "O Hotṛ, announce the cake-offerings set forth for Indra at the midday pressing."
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering; likewise, while pouring together [the portions], he says, "Recite for Agni," and having called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says, "Prompt for Agni.
When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the offering in the eastern part of the northern half, passing over the previous offerings.

Having stepped out toward the north and placed the two *sruva*-ladles in their respective places, and having likewise gathered the *iḍā* in the vessel, he sends the sacrificial cakes westward. Some follow him, saying, "The cattle are the *iḍā*. Then, moving eastward, he says: "Recite for the cups being filled!

Fill the *camasa* of the Hotṛ after [his own]; make them bright on both sides; O *camasādhvaryu* of the Acchāvāka, you too fill yours! O Pratiprasthātṛ, support me with four splinters, some sprinkled and some unsprinkled!
They act according to these directions.

The ritual action is the same up until the call for the *āśrāvaṇa*; at the *āśrāvaṇa* itself it ceases. Then the Adhvaryu, standing in front and facing west, calls for the announcement: "Ośrāvaya! Astu Śrauṣaṭ! For the portion belonging exclusively to the midday pressing, accompanied by the *śukra* and *manthin* cups, dripping with honey—to Indra, the Soma juices that have been set forth—proclaim!
At the *vaṣaṭ* call, both offer together. With the formula, "He is the first creator, Viśvakarman," they both offer twice, at the *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *anuvaṣaṭ* calls.
In the same manner, they offer all the *camasa*s twice each;
likewise, he issues the direction: "Let the *camasa* of the Hotṛ go forward, let that of the Brahman go forward.

Then, having turned to the right, he pours the residue of the *graha* into the Hotṛ’s *camasa*, either with the formula, "I pour thee, who hast been offered, into what has been offered—full of vigor for the gods, full of sweetness for men," or silently.
In the same manner, the Pratiprasthātṛ offers the residue of the Manthin cup upon the northern half of the Āhavanīya fire;
likewise, having touched water, he places both the Śukra vessel and the Manthin vessel on the mound (khara) in their respective places,
while these goblets of the great officiating priests proceed.
In the same way, these cup-attendants (camasādhvaryu) of the Hotrakas, having drawn [Soma] once each from the Droṇakalaśa vessel, return;

for them, in that very manner, having taken up the Maitrāvaruṇa's cup and called for the *āśrāvaṇa* (the call for assent), he says: "O Praśāstṛ, sacrifice! O Brahman, sacrifice! O Potṛ, sacrifice! O Neṣṭṛ, sacrifice! O Acchāvāka, sacrifice! O Agnīdh, sacrifice!"
Having performed the *ṣaḍḍhotṛ* offerings and having turned clockwise, he hastens back toward the west and sits down in front of the *hotṛ*, saying, "The *āgnīdh* has sacrificed.
The *hotṛ* says, "May he who will cause us to drink King Soma have good fortune.
Then, having touched water, while they are lifting the *iḍā* for the *hotṛ*, they hold up their cups as the *iḍā* is being invoked.

When the *iḍā* has been invoked, he places the sixfold portion for the *āgnīdh*. They consume it and perform the ritual purification (*mārjana*). Having invoked the *iḍā*, they consume the cups (*camasa*), reciting the long consumption formula (*dīrghabhakṣa*): "O Soma, come hither, enter me! Having recited this, [he continues]: "O Rudra, of the troop, O divine Soma, knower of the mind, of thee who art drunk by Indra at the midday pressing, of the *triṣṭubh* metre, of the honeyed, of thee who art invited—I, being invited, consume.
These three, having mutually invited one another, consume the Hotṛ’s cup alone.
Touching themselves with the formula, "Impel the cups according to their respective vessels for me," they cause the cups to swell with the formula, "Swell up; may [the draught] come to you."

The Nārāśaṃsa cups, having been replenished, remain sitting below the rear support of the southern *havirdhāna* cart for the third *marutvatīya* offering. At this time, in the *āgnīdhra* shed, the sacrificer eats of the sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa*) if he intends to eat; the wife eats them in the *patnīśālā*.

Then, about to offer the oblations pertaining to the sacrificial gifts (*dākṣiṇa*), he causes [the necessary items] to be brought: a vessel of clarified butter (*ājyasthālī*) together with a dipping-spoon (*sruva*), a large ladle (*sruk*), and a garment.

When the fringe of this garment has reached its end, a piece of gold is tied to it; taking this, he says, "Come, O sacrificer! Having gone around to the north of the Āgnīdhrīya fire and having gone around to the north of the Sadas, and having entered the hall by the eastern door, while the participants have taken hold of one another and are covered over, he melts the clarified butter over the Gārhapatya fire, purifies it, takes four portions into the ladle, and holding the end of the garment against the handle of the ladle, he offers it into the Gārhapatya fire with two verses addressed to Sūrya: "Up..."

"The rays bear that god Jātavedas so that everyone may behold the Sun; Svāhā! Having taken another fourfold portion, he offers it in the Gārhapatya fire itself with the mantra: "The brilliant face of the gods has risen—the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni."

"May Sūrya, the soul of all that moves and stands, fill the heavens, the earth, and the mid-space—Svāhā! Having run to the Āgnīdhra shed and taken four spoonfuls into the offering-ladle, he holds the end of the garment against the handle of the ladle and offers it into the Āgnīdhra fire with the verse containing the word "lead": "O Agni, lead us by a good path to wealth, O God, you who know all ways. Keep away from us the crooked sin; we offer to you the most abundant speech of homage—Svāhā! Then, having offered a piece of gold with the words, "Go to heaven, fly to the light," he draws it back up.

The sacrificial gifts are distributed by way of the southern path, between the *sadas* and the *gārhapatya*, between the *sadas* and the *āgnīdhra*, and between the *cātvāla* and the rubbish-heap (*utkara*); thus they proceed toward the north.

Having circumambulated them clockwise, he approaches them with the verse: "I approach your form with my form, your age with my age. Then he distributes them with the formula: "May Tutha, the all-knowing, distribute you in the highest heaven. Then he approaches the *sadas* hall with the verses: "This is your gift, O Agni; it comes from Soma; lead it by the path of Mitra, by the path of Ṛta. "Go forth, O bright sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), leading us to well-being by the path of the sacrifice. Now, this descendant of Atri sits in front of the *sadas*.

He approaches that Brahmin, saying, "Today I shall succeed with this seer, the descendant of seers, who has a father and a grandfather, and who is accompanied by a gift of gold. Then, stepping aside from him, he asks, "Who is the Ātreya? The other replies, "I am he.

Stepping aside from him in the same manner, he asks for a second time, "Who is the Ātreya? The other replies, "I am he. Stepping aside from him in the same manner, he asks for a third time, "Who is the Ātreya? The other replies, "I am he."

He places gold in his hand with the formula, "O Moon, thou art a weapon. Whatever else has been prepared, he goes to the Āgnīdhra shed and gives it to the Āgnīdhra with gold at its head; then, having come to the Sadas, he gives it to the Brahman, the Hotṛ, and the Udgātṛ. Then, having gone to the Havirdhāna shed, he gives it to the Adhvaryu and to those others who are around him. Then, having come to the Sadas, he gives it to the Prastotṛ, the Praśāstṛ, the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, the Acchāvāka, the Sadasya, the Āgnīdhra, the Potṛ, the Neṣṭṛ, and the Grāvastut.

[The duties] of the Unnetṛ, the Subrahmaṇya, and the Pratihartṛ [are performed]; finally, according to the traditional instruction, [the offerings] are for the Prasarpakas. Then he says, "Come, O Sacrificer! Having run to the Āgnīdhra shed and having taken four portions of clarified butter in the ladle, he offers five Vaiśvakarman oblations in the Āgnīdhra fire with the verse, "The Rishis have seized the Lord of the Sacrifice with sin.
Then he steps across and proceeds with the Atimokṣa formulas by means of these two Anuvākas: "With the god Agni... and "Those gods who are destroyers of the sacrifice... and so forth.

Then he causes the sacrificer to look toward the east, saying, "Behold the light; behold the mid-air. Then he seats him in the *sadas*, saying, "Exert yourself with those in the *sadas*. Then he points out the sacrificial gifts (*dakṣiṇās*), saying: "Given by us, go to the gods, full of sweetness; enter the giver. Without leaving us, sit in the world of the doers of good by the path leading to the gods; may that be prepared for us.
Then, as he goes forward, he says, "Recite the invitatory verse for Indra accompanied by the Maruts."

Having heard that, the Pratiprasthātṛ takes up the two cups and steps out. As soon as he has stepped out, the Adhvaryu takes up the two cups; he hands one to the Pratiprasthātṛ who stands to the north. Then he calls for the *āśrāvaṇa*: "O Śrauṣaṭ! Let it be heard! Pronounce the *praisha* for Indra accompanied by the Maruts! At the utterance of the *vaṣaṭ*, they both offer together. Then the Pratiprasthātṛ pours the residue of the cup into the Adhvaryu’s vessel. He says to him: "O Pratiprasthātṛ, take the third Marutvatīya cup with this vessel."

Thereupon, the Pratiprasthātṛ draws the third Marutvatīya cup from the Droṇakalaśa with the *pariplu* ladle, having run forward [with the formula]: "O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, a bull for the battle! Having recited this, he says: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, who art dear to Indra accompanied by the Maruts. Having wiped it around, he deposits it with: "This is thy womb; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, thee. Then the Adhvaryu, having turned to the right and run back toward the west, causes the Hotṛ to consume that cup with: "Of what has been drunk by Indra accompanied by the Maruts... Then, holding the cup, he turns away with: "The *iḍā* is the invoker of the gods."
As soon as he has mastered this Yajus formula, he mutters it; the Hotṛ calls out to him,
and the Adhvaryu responds, saying "Śaṃsati."
He responds with the well-known *uktha*. Having responded, he goes forward and lifts up this third *marutvatīya* cup;
they lift up the *nārāśaṃsa* vessels after it.
Then, having caused [the announcement] to be heard with "Ośrāvaya," and [the response] "Astu śrauṣaṭ," [the Adhvaryu says] "O Ukthashā, recite the offering-verse for the Soma!
At the *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *anuvaṣaṭ*, he offers twice;

likewise, twice each time they do not shake the Nārāśaṃsa cups. These Nārāśaṃsa cups follow this vessel; the consumption [of the Soma] at each pressing is performed with the formula: "Of that which was drunk by Indra accompanied by the Maruts..."

The Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu consume this cup with that which has been drunk by Narāśaṃsa. [The formula is: "O divine Soma, of thee who art drunk by Narāśaṃsa, who knowest the mind, who belongest to the midday pressing, whose metre is the Triṣṭubh, who art drunk by the Fathers, who art full of sweetness, and who art invited—I, being invited, partake.
Having thus invited one another, these three consume the Hotṛ’s cup; they consume the other cups according to their respective vessels.
Touching themselves with the words, "Impel me," they cause the cups to swell;
they settle the *nārāśaṃsa* goblets that have been made to swell beneath the rear support of the southern *havirdhāna* cart, below the *māhendra* cup.

Then, having gone eastward while taking up the *śukra* vessel, he says: "O Unnetṛ, when I take this *māhendra* draught, then cause the King [Soma] to flow through the filter toward the *pūtabhṛt* jar; O Droṇakalaśa-washer, having wiped it with the fringed cloth, turn it upside down."
He acts accordingly:

with a vessel for the *śukra* juice, he draws the *māhendra* cup from the *droṇakalaśa*, reciting "Great is Indra who [is great] by might," and following it with "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Mahendra.

Having wiped it around, he sets it down with "This is thy womb; [I set thee down] acceptable to Mahendra. Then, having touched water and taken two blades of *barhis* grass, restraining his speech, he hastens westward and introduces the *stotra*.

When the *māhendra* cup has been praised and the *sāman* has been introduced, he issues the direction: "O pressers, press the Soma! O Āgnīdh, pour out the milk-mixture! Make the mortar resound! O Pratiprasthātṛ, offer the cake on one potsherd for Varuṇa; attend to the offering for Soma!
They act according to these directions.
"This is the best oblation," they say; at the time of the Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu turns away, the Hotṛ calls him,
and the Adhvaryu responds as he utters "śaṃsati."
He responds with the well-known *uktha*. Having responded, he goes forward and lifts up this cup for Mahendra;
they lift up the *nārāśaṃsa* goblets after it.
Then, having caused the announcement to be made with "Ośrāvaya," [the response is] "Astu śrauṣaṭ. [The Hotṛ says] "O Ukthashā, recite the offering-verse for the Soma!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *anuvaṣaṭ*, he offers twice.

In the same manner, twice each time, they do not shake the Nārāśaṃsa cups. They follow this cup, the Nārāśaṃsas; the consumption at each pressing is performed with the formula: "Of that which was drunk by Mahendra..."

The Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu consume this cup together with what has been drunk by Narāśaṃsa, [reciting]: "O divine Soma, of thee who art drunk by Narāśaṃsa, who knowest the mind, who belongest to the midday pressing, who hast the Triṣṭubh metre, who art drunk by the Pitṛs, who art full of sweetness, and who art invited—I, being invited, partake.
Having thus invited one another, these three consume the Hotṛ’s cup; they consume the other cups according to their respective vessels.
With the verse "hinva me," they touch themselves, but they do not cause the cups to swell;
having consumed the entire contents, they perform the purification rites. Then he proceeds with the three Ukthya rounds, beginning with "indrā yāhi" and "indrā yāhi."

He says to him who is standing there in the same manner at the *uttama* [cup]: "Fill the cups following the *ācchāvāka*'s cup; O *unnētṛ*, draw out the entire *rājā* [Soma], do not let it overflow! O *pratiprasthātṛ*, rejoice with this cup!

Come, O sacrificer! Having caused him to enter the *havirdhāna* shed by the eastern door, he then turns the *ādhavanīya* vessel upside down and pours all the *vasatīvarī* waters into it, and likewise all the *ekadhana* waters.
Having wiped the *vasatīvarī* pitcher in front of the axle, he turns it upside down;
behind the axle, they first draw the *ekadhanā* waters into the *acchāvāka*'s cup.

Having raised the King [Soma] from all sides as they arise, they deposit him upon the high altar (uttaravedi). Then he takes the secondary cup (aupaśaya-pātra) belonging to the Ukthya-vessel; into that he draws the entire King [Soma] which remains in the Ukthya-vessel. That [Soma] indeed belongs to Indra alone. Then, having responded to the midday pressing with "The Uktha has been spoken," he says, "O Praśāstṛ, give the command!"
"Creep forward! says the Praśāstṛ;
the midday pressing is concluded, and they proceed toward the third pressing with the [verse] "O divine doors," from this very point upward.
"O Prasthātṛ, bring the head of the horse; bring the curd for the Āditya cup from the boiled milk; come, O sacrificer!

Having thus caused the sacrificer to enter the Havirdhāna shed by the eastern door, he pours that stalk which has been placed in the Upāṃśu vessel into the *ṛjīṣa* of the midday pressing. Then, taking any pressing-stone whatsoever, he says to the Unnetṛ, "Bring it; pour [the Soma] over it. The Unnetṛ pours an unlimited amount, pressing from the *ādhavanīya* trough with water added to it. Then, having collected it well-prepared in the collecting-vessel (*saṃbharaṇī*), he hands it over to the Unnetṛ.

The Unnetṛ pours that into the Ādhavanīya vessel; in this very manner the second round is completed, and likewise the third. Finally, having wrapped the *ṛjīṣa* with the fringe of the *daśāpavitra*, he hands it to the Unnetṛ. The Unnetṛ, having rinsed it in the Ādhavanīya and squeezed it out, brings it between the two poles of the southern *havirdhāna* cart and deposits it in the interior. They enclose it, closing both the eastern and the western doors. Then he takes the vessel that rests upon the *ādityasthālī*.

At that [third] time, he draws this third draught for the king [Soma], which is in the Aditya vessel, having recited "Never art thou barren," and then [reciting] "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to the Ādityas."

Having placed two blades of *barhis* grass in between, he mixes [the draught] with the *śrītātaṅkya* [mixture]. Having recited "Never indeed do you neglect... and "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to the Ādityas," and having removed the two blades of *barhis*, he draws from the King [Soma] at the half-mark. Having recited "The sacrifice of the gods goes toward favor," and "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to the Ādityas," he then mixes it with the *upāṃśusavana* stone from the largest [part] of the press, saying: "O Vivasvat, son of Aditi, this is thy Soma-drink; rejoice in it, be satisfied by it."

"May we, the offerers of libations, be satisfied by thee; with that divine rain which is thine, I mix thee"—with these words he then draws it up. At this point, a sign is perceived: if it spills out quickly, Parjanya will be rainy;
if for a long time, he will be dry. "He does not set it down," so says the Brāhmaṇa.
Then, having wrapped the *daśāpavitra* around the *upāṃśusavana* stone, he scoops the vessel from below with it, forming a wave-like shape without spilling.

"From the ocean and from the mid-region, may Prajāpati cause the sea to flow; may Indra sprinkle it, may the Maruts cause it to rain. Make the earth swell, cleave this celestial cloud! Give us of the celestial water; O Lord, release the leather bag! Having thus wiped the Upāṃśusavana stone with the *daśāpavitra* filter, he places it among the pressing-stones.

They open the eastern door and the western one; then, covering this cup with his hand on the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), while rising up, he says: "Recite the invitatory verse for the Adityas, who are beloved, whose abodes are beloved, whose vows are beloved, the lords of the great dwelling, the overseers of the wide mid-region.

Having stepped across and called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says: "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for the Adityas, who are beloved, whose abodes are beloved, whose vows are beloved, the lords of the great dwelling, the overseers of the wide mid-region.
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, having cast the plants into the fire, he offers the oblation to the Aditya only once.
Having offered, he does not look back;

the Pratiprasthātṛ takes the vessel from him as he turns away. At this time, the Pratihartṛ, having spread the filter over the opening of the *pūtabhṛt* vessel, pours two or three ladlings of the King [Soma] into it. The Adhvaryu takes the Āgrayaṇa vessel, and the Pratiprasthātṛ takes the Āditya bowl together with its secondary cup (*sopaśaya*).
Of those three or four streams, he pours the Āgrayaṇa on top and catches it from below.

Having uttered the *abhihiṅkāra* over it three times in that same manner and wiped it around, he sets it down; having removed the filter and placed two blades of *barhis* grass in between, he pours in the milk-mixture while the wife holds on to him, with the four verses according to their meter beginning, "O gods, look upon us for beauty.
Having removed the two blades of *barhis*, he consecrates the drops in the cavity of the *pūtabhṛt* vessel;
he takes two cups of the *pavamāna* soma.
"Therefore, he says, 'Let him cause the king [Soma] to flow forward toward the *pūtabhṛt* vessel; having cleansed the *ādhavanīya* with the fringes of the filter, let him turn it upside down.
He does so.
Then, having touched water and taken two blades of *barhis* grass, he steps out."
When they have likewise taken hold of them, he offers a spoonful (sruvāhuti) into the Āhavanīya fire with this verse:

"This is the third pressing of the seers (*kavīn*), those who by means of Truth (*ṛta*) set the chalice in motion; may those sons of Sudhanvan, having attained heaven, lead our well-offered sacrifice toward greater prosperity, Svāhā! With this verse, the two Adhvaryus offer; the others offer according to their respective Veda.
Then, having turned to the right, they proceed toward the *Sadas* and the *Āpavamāna* chant.

Just as they sit in the assembly according to their respective positions, he gives two blades of *barhis* grass to either the *udgātṛ* or the *prastotṛ*, saying, "Thou art the under-layer for the Ṛc and the Sāman, for the procreation of the couple," or silently;
likewise, he mutters the introductory formula: "Vāyu is the utterer of *hiṃ*."

This Ārbhava Pavamāna consists of seventeen verses. When the ninth verse has been introduced, he makes [the sacrificer] recite: "Thou art a companion, having the Jagatī for thy metre; I take hold of thee; lead me safely across. At this point, he recites the Pañcahotṛ formula. Once the Sāman has been chanted, he issues the direction: "O Āgnīdh, distribute the fire-sticks; strew the sacrificial grass; prepare the sacrificial cakes; O Pratiprasthātṛ, converse with the animal victim. They both act according to the direction.
Having likewise touched water and said, "Come, O sacrificer," he leads him into the *havirdhāna* shed by the eastern door; then he worships the entire King Soma,
and he does not proceed with the *avakāśa* formulas here.
In the same manner, he takes [the butter] nine times with the *pracaraṇī* ladle;

likewise, this *Āgnīdhra* priest distributes the fire-sticks (*śālākā*) from the *Āgnīdhrīya* hearth onto the other hearths (*dhiṣṇiya*) in successive order; likewise, sitting in the east facing west, he sprinkles the distributed fire-sticks with clarified butter.

In the same manner, he places the *pracaraṇī* ladle on the chin of the northern *havirdhāna* cart; likewise, he spreads the *pṛṣṭhyā* grass along the path that is visible from both ends, continuously from the *gārhapatya* fire to the *āhavanīya* fire.
Then he proceeds with the animal sacrifice, beginning with the *manotā* hymn and ending with the *iḍā*.
Likewise, he asks for the *savanīya* sacrificial cakes;
taking portions from them in the same manner, he says, "Recite for the sacrificial cakes being portioned out for Indra at the third pressing.
Having taken a portion from the eastern half, he takes a portion from the western half and pours clarified butter over it.
He anoints [the butter] in the upabhṛt for the Sviṣṭakṛt; he cuts off portions from the northern half of each [oblation] once each,
and he pours clarified butter over them twice.
Without stepping across, he does not sprinkle [the butter]; having called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says, "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for the cakes set forth for Indra at the third pressing.
At the *vaṣaṭ*-call, he makes the offering. Likewise, while pouring together [the portions], he says, "Recite for Agni"; having called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says, "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for Agni."

At the utterance of "vaṣaṭ," he makes an offering in the eastern part of the northern half, passing over the previous offerings. Then, having stepped out toward the north and placed the two ladles in their respective places, and having likewise placed the *iḍā* portion into the vessel, he sends the sacrificial cakes westward. Some follow him, saying, "The cattle are the *iḍā*. Then, moving eastward, he says, "Recite for the cups being filled! Fill the Hotṛ’s cup after [the others]; make them strong and full of flavor; O Unnetṛ, make the Soma swell!
They fill the Hotṛ’s cup first, and the others as they come.

Having lifted it up, they set it down on the *uttaravedi*. Then, having gone forward to the east and taken the *hotṛ*’s cup, he calls for the *āśrāvaṇa* and says: "For Indra, the Soma-draughts that have been set forth—belonging to the third pressing, full of vigor, all-pervading, powerful, rich in food, accompanied by Savitṛ, Bṛhaspati, and the Viśvedevas, and possessing the sharp *āṃśu* stalk—send forth the call!

At the *vaṣaṭ*-utterance, he offers with: "Svāhā to the flying falcon! At the subsequent *vaṣaṭ*-utterance, he offers twice with: "May the officiating priests be satisfied with the honeyed ghee; Svāhā!
At both the *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *vaṣaṭ*, he makes two offerings.
In the same manner, they offer all the *camasa* cups twice each;

likewise, he issues the command: "Let the *camasa* of the Hotṛ go forward, that of the Brahman, that of the Udgātṛ, that of the Sacrificer, and that of the Sadasya! O *camasādhvaryus* of the *hotraka*s, having drawn [the soma] once each with the *āśīr*, return!
These *camasa*s of the great officiants then proceed.
In the same manner, these cup-officiants (camasādhvaryus) of the Hotrakas, having drawn [the soma] once for each with the *āśīrvat* formula, withdraw.
For them, likewise taking up the cup of the Maitrāvaruṇa and having called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says, "O Praśāstṛ, recite the offering-verse (*yajya*).
At the utterance of the *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering with the formula: "To the support, to the law, svāhā!"
"To the enclosing-stick, the one renowned among people"—this for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin; "for the strength of the Hotrās"—this for the Potṛ;

"for the milk of the Hotrās"—this for the Neṣṭṛ; "to Prajāpati, for Manu"—this for the Acchāvāka; "to Ṛta, O guardians of Ṛta, winner of heaven"—this for the Agnīdh. He utters the *anuvaṣaṭ* for each cup individually: "May the Hotrās be satiated with the honey and the ghee—*svāhā*!"

Having performed the *saṃyāja* for the seven *hotṛ*s, having turned to the right and hastened back facing west, he sits down in front of the *hotṛ*. The *hotṛ* says, "The *āgnīdh* has sacrificed," and [the *adhvaryu*] replies, "May it be auspicious for him who will cause us to drink King Soma. Then, having touched water, while they lift the *iḍā* for the *hotṛ*, they hold up the cups as the *iḍā* is being invoked.

When the *iḍā* has been invoked, he places the sixfold portion for the *āgnīdhra*; they consume it and perform the ritual purification (*mārjana*). Having invoked the *iḍā*, they consume the goblets with the long *bhakṣa*-formula, reciting: "O Soma, come hither, enter me! followed by: "Of thee, O divine Soma, who belongest to the troop of Aditi, who art mindful, of the third pressing, whose metre is the *jagatī*, who art drunk by Indra, who art full of sweetness, and who hast been invited—I, being invited, partake. These three, having invited one another, consume the *hotṛ*'s goblet alone.
Saying, "Impel the cups according to their respective vessels;
impel me," they touch themselves. They cause the cups to swell with the formula, "Swell up; let [the draught] come to thee.
The *nārāśaṃsa* goblets, having been made to swell, are placed one below the other along the rear support of the southern *havirdhāna* cart for the *vaiśvadeva* offering.
For each *camasa* cup, he throws three pieces of the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) into it; there are nine such pieces in the Hotṛ’s cup, and he consecrates them with that very formula:
"O Fathers, rejoice here according to your respective portions. At this moment, the sacrificer eats the sacrificial cakes in the Āgnīdhra shed.
When the wife has eaten in the wife’s hall, then, moving eastward, [the Adhvaryu] says:
"Recite for the god Savitṛ; O Pratiprasthātṛ, having drawn the Sāvitra cup from the Āgrayaṇa vessel with the Antaryāma cup, wait upon it, saying 'Do not let it settle'.

Having heard that, the Pratiprasthātṛ draws the Sāvitra cup from the Āgrayaṇa vessel with the Antaryāma cup, reciting: "O Savitṛ, the lovely [gift] today... and then: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, agreeable to the god Savitṛ."
"He does not set it down," so says the Brāhmaṇa.
Without setting it down, having gone out and called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says, "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for the god Savitṛ!
At the *vaṣaṭ*-call, he makes the offering. Now, indeed, it is said:
With the *savitṛ* cup, he draws the *vaiśvadeva* [libation] from the *kalaśa*; "he draws Soma into Soma," so it is said.

He draws the *vaiśvadeva* with the *savitṛ* cup from the *kalaśa*, drawing Soma into Soma, [reciting]: "Thou art taken with a support; thou art a good refuge, a firm foundation. O Great Ox, homage! I take thee, acceptable to the All-Gods (*viśve devāḥ*). Having wiped it around, he deposits it, [reciting]: "This is thy womb; for the All-Gods thee! Then the Adhvaryu, having turned to the right and facing west, looks toward the Hotṛ and turns away, [reciting]: "The *iḍā* is the invoker of the gods."
As soon as he has mastered this Yajus formula, he mutters it; the Hotṛ calls out to him,
and the Adhvaryu responds, saying "Śaṃsati."

He responds. Then, when he recognizes the Hotṛ’s recitation, "With one and with ten, as they have become," the Pratiprasthātṛ, having cleansed the cups for the dual deities at the Mārjālīya mound, pours them back into the vessels. Then, when he recognizes the Hotṛ’s recitation, "O Heaven and Earth, increase the sacrifice through the Ṛta," he responds to the *anyatomada* chant: "Othā moda iva, madā moda iva," continuing until the *vyāhāva*. Then, when he recognizes the Hotṛ’s recitation, "That desirable gift of Savitṛ today..."
He responds to both of those with the very word "intoxication" (*mada*), saying "Intoxication, as if from joy; intoxication, as if from joy," up until the call for the response.
Having responded with the well-known hymn (*uktha*), he goes forward and lifts up this cup for the Viśvedevas;
they lift up the Nārāśaṃsa cups after it.
Then, having caused the announcement to be made with "Ośrāvaya," [the response is] "Astu śrauṣaṭ"; [the Adhvaryu says] "O Ukthashā, recite the offering-verse for the Soma!
At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* and at the subsequent *anuvaṣaṭ*, he offers twice.

In the same manner, twice each time they do not shake the Nārāśaṃsa cups. They follow this cup; the consumption [of the Soma] at each pressing is performed with the formula: "Of that which has been drunk by all the gods..."

The Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu consume this cup together with the Nārāśaṃsa-drink. [The formula is: "O divine Soma, of thee who art drunk by the Nārāśaṃsas, who art drunk by the fathers, who art possessed of the *mativi* (insight), who belong to the third pressing, whose metre is the Jagatī, who art full of sweetness, and who art invited—I, being invited, partake.
Having thus invited one another, these three consume the Hotṛ’s cup; they consume the other cups according to their respective vessels.
With the words "Impel me," they touch themselves; they do not cause the cups to swell;
having consumed the entire contents, they perform the ritual purification.

Then he asks the Hotṛ: "Will you sacrifice the *saumya* [oblation], or will you not? Having heard how the Hotṛ replies to him, he approaches the prepared *saumya*. Then, having taken four portions into the ladle (*sruk*), having stepped across and called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says, "Recite the offering prayer for the clarified butter" (*ghṛtasya yaja*).
When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the offering. Then, having spread an underlayer of butter, he cuts off two portions from the *caru*.
Having cut a portion from the eastern half, he cuts a portion from the western half, sprinkles it with clarified butter, and does not re-anoint it.
Having stepped across and called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says, "Recite the offering prayer for the Soma-oblation.

When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, wearing the sacrificial cord over his right shoulder (*prācīnāvītī*), he offers the Soma-oblation in the eastern part of the southern half. Then he makes a libation over it with a spoonful using the verse addressed to Viṣṇu: "O Viṣṇu, you are our nearest [kinsman]."
If, however, the Hotṛ performs the *pariyajana* with a verse addressed to Agni and Viṣṇu, one should not take heed of whether it is "complete";
rather, while the butter is being poured out, he gazes upon it, for that which belongs to Soma is a purifier; they thus purify themselves.
"One who does not perceive himself would be lifeless; therefore, having made an offering, he should look [at the clarified butter].
Having poured more clarified butter into it, he looks at it, saying: "That mind of mine which has gone away, or that which has not gone away—by means of King Soma, we maintain that within us.
Thus he places the mind back in himself; his mind does not depart. So says the Brāhmaṇa.

Then they carry him to the Udgātṛs; they perform upon him those rites which they know. Then, as he goes forward, he says: "O Pratiprasthātṛ, having taken a draught for the Patnīvats from the Āgrayaṇa vessel with the Upāṃśu cup, wait near me; do not sit down.

Having heard that, the Pratiprasthātṛ takes a draught for the Patnīvats from the Āgrayaṇa vessel with the Upāṃśu cup, saying: "Thou art taken with a support; O Indu, of thee pressed by Bṛhaspati, as much as is powerful, I take the draught for the Patnīvats, O Agni, thou who hast a wife!"

Having placed two blades of *barhis* grass in between, he mixes [the oblation] with clarified butter, saying: "I am above, I am below; by means of light, I have dispelled the darkness. That which is the intermediate space—that has become my father. I have seen the sun on both sides. May I become the highest among my equals. Having removed the two blades of *barhis*, he does not set [the vessel] down—so says the Brāhmaṇa.
Without setting it down, having gone out and called for the *śrauṣaṭ* response, he says: "O Āgnīdh, recite the offering prayer for the Pātnīvata [cup]."

When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he offers with the formula: "In unison with the god Tvaṣṭṛ, drink the Soma, Svāhā! Having offered in a low voice when the subsequent *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he carries away the portion for consumption. If someone desires an invitation (*upahava*) from him at the Āgnīdhra fire, he indeed invites that person.

But he does not eat together with him. Then he says: "O Agnīdh, sit in the lap of the Neṣṭṛ; O Neṣṭṛ, lead up the wife; have her looked at by the Udgātṛ; cause the water to flow forward; cause it to flow forward with the thigh; having uncovered the thigh, cause it to flow forward; fill the Hotṛ’s cup after [the others]; O Unnetṛ, draw up the entire King Soma, do not leave any remainder; O Pratiprasthātṛ, make a space for the Dhruvā in the Hotṛ’s cup; come, O Sacrificer!"

Having caused [the sacrificer] to enter the Havirdhāna shed by the eastern door, he makes him stand near the Dhruva vessel with the formula: "Thou art being; place me in being; thou art the mouth; may I become the mouth.
They fill the Hotṛ’s cup first, and the others as they come along.

Having raised the king (the Soma) from every side, they place him upon the *uttaravedi*. Then, having touched water and taken two blades of *barhis* grass, he restrains his speech, runs westward, and introduces the *stotra*;
they chant the *yajñāyajñiya* hymn, at which point he recites the *saptahotṛ* formula.

When the *sāman* has been introduced, the *neṣṭṛ*, having caused the wife to be looked at by the *udgātṛ*, makes her recite: "O Agni, may all the desirable things of yours, who are all-pervading and full of virility, be mine in your sight; may I obtain all seeds. May the sacrifice direct the gods; may the goddesses bestow blessings upon the gods for this pressing sacrificer; may the blessings consecrated with *svāhā* [be established] in the ocean. Stand near the Gandharva; in the flight of the wind, you are praised as the *iḍā*.
At the very moment the *udgātṛ* approaches her, the wife causes the washing-waters (*pannejana*) to flow forward over her thigh;
she causes them to flow over her thigh after having uncovered it.
"This is the supreme oblation," they say; at the time of the Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu turns away, the Hotṛ calls to him,
and the Adhvaryu responds as he utters "śaṃ."

He responds; then, when he recognizes the Hotṛ’s recitation, "Sweet indeed is this, and honeyed is this," he responds with joy from both sides, saying, "Joy! Like joy! Rapture! Like rapture! until the call for the Vyāhāva. Then, when he recognizes the Hotṛ’s recitation, "Stretching the thread, follow the light of the mid-region," the Pratiprasthātṛ takes hold of the Dhruva vessel, saying, "I take hold of thee for Heaven and Earth," and then he moves it forward, saying, "May all the gods, common to all men, move thee forward."

Then he brings it forward with the verse: "In heaven support the gods; in the intermediate space, the birds; on earth, the earthly beings. Then he pours it into the Hotṛ’s goblet with the formula: "We lead the firm Soma with the firm oblation, so that this entire world may be free from disease and full of goodwill for us; so that Indra may make all the people ours alone and of one mind; so that all the quarters may be ours alone. Having responded to the hymn in the established manner, he goes eastward and lifts up this Hotṛ’s goblet;
the other goblets are lifted up after it.
Then he causes [the Hotṛ] to announce: "O Śrauṣaṭ! Let it be heard! O Ukthashā, recite the offering-verse for the Soma-libations!

At the *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *anuvaṣaṭ*, he offers twice. In the same manner, they offer their respective goblets twice each. Then they turn back with the portions for consumption (*bhakṣa*). The formula for consuming at each pressing is: "Invited by Agni Vaiśvānara and the Maruts, I, being invited, consume the sweet, offered [Soma]."
Having invited one another, these three consume from the Hotṛ’s cup alone;
they touch themselves individually with the formula, "Impel the cups; impel me."
They do not replenish the cups;

having consumed all [the soma], they perform the *mārjana* purification. Then, having filled these cups with water, he causes them to be carried forward to the north of the Āhavanīya fire, either toward the east or toward the north.
Into them he throws three knots of *dūrvā* grass and a single tuft of *darbha* grass each.
Then, having responded to the third pressing with "O Indra, come to the speech," he says, "Praśāstṛ, give the command!
The Praśāstṛ says, "Crawl forward!
Thus the third pressing is concluded.

Then he issues the command: "O Āgnīdh, bring the embers for the *aupayaja* offerings; O *Upayaṣṭṛ*, sit down; O Brahman, we shall set forth; having placed the fuel-stick, O Āgnīdh, cleanse the fires once each. They bring those embers for the *aupayaja* offerings from the *āgnīdhra* shed; the Hotṛ pours them down in front of himself, and the *Upayaṣṭṛ* sits down with the third portion of the rectum. Then the Adhvaryu, having divided the clotted butter (*pṛṣadājya*) and poured it into the *juhū* ladle, steps across, calls for the *śrauṣaṭ*, and says, "Prompt for the gods! (*devebhyaḥ preṣya*).

When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering. Having performed eleven after-offerings (*anuyāja*) with the calls "Prompt! Prompt!", he steps out toward the north, places the two ladles in their respective places, and separates the two ladles with the two *vājavatī* verses.

Having scattered the *prastara* and the enclosing sticks together with the *śaṃyu* formula and having poured out the remnants from the ladles, he releases the ladles and says to the Unnetṛ: "O Unnetṛ, the cup is yours; proceed!"

Having heard that, the Unnetṛ draws the third draught from the Droṇakalaśa for the Āgrayaṇa vessel with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; thou art the bay one, the yoker of bays, the rider of the bays, the bearer of the thunderbolt, the lover of Pṛśni. O divine Soma, for thee whose sacrificial formulas have been offered, whose Stomas have been chanted, and whose Ukthas have been recited, I draw the draught accompanied by the bays. Having placed two blades of *barhis* grass between [the vessel and the grains], he mixes it with roasted grains (*dhānā*) with the formula: "Ye two are the bays; ye are the roasted grains for the two bays. Having removed the two blades of *barhis*, he takes hold of it and, rising up, says: "O Hotṛ, recite the invitatory verses for Indra, the possessor of bays, for the roasted grains and Somas!"

Having placed [the vessel] upon his head and stepped forward, he calls out without making it heard: "O Hotṛ, give the command for Indra, the possessor of the Soma, for the parched grains and the Soma-pressings that have been set forth!

At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers the oblation with the formula: "To Indra, accompanied by the Soma, Svāhā! Having offered at the subsequent *vaṣaṭ*-utterance, he carries away the portion for consumption. The Unnetṛ distributes the parched grains among as many officiating priests as there are; having sought permission from the Unnetṛ, they consume them one by one.

"O divine Soma, I, being invited, partake of thee who art invited—of thee who art pressed with the mind, whose *yajus* has been offered, whose *stoma* has been praised, whose *uktha* has been recited, who art accompanied by the *hari* horses, who art drunk by Indra, who art honey-sweet. Then, having washed them, they pour them together upon the northern altar (*uttaravedi*) with the formula: "Ye are full; fill me with offspring and wealth.

While pouring them out, the sacrificer keeps three grains of parched grain. Then he calls for the wooden sword (*sphya*), a vessel of water, and sacrificial grass (*barhis*); having taken these, he says: "Come, O sacrificer!"

Having gone around the two *havirdhāna* sheds by the south and the rear, he digs up the ground to the south of the *mārjālīya* hearth with the wooden sword (*sphya*), sprinkles it with water, and spreads sacrificial grass (*barhis*) with its tips pointing southward. He purifies [the ancestors] with water, saying: "May the fathers be purified; may the grandfathers be purified; may the great-grandfathers be purified. Then he gives three parched grains (*dhānā*), saying: "This for you, O father, N.N., and those who follow you; this for you, O grandfather, N.N., and those who follow you; this for you, O great-grandfather, N.N., and those who follow you. Here, O fathers, partake according to your respective portions.

Having said, "Be quiet," and having turned toward the north, he recites the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ formula there; then, having turned back and likewise sprinkled himself with water, he returns by the same way he came and offers two spoonfuls of oblation on the Āgnīdhrīya fire with the two verses: "Whatever deficiency has occurred in my self, Agni has restored my sight" and [the second verse].

Then they perform the rite with wood-shavings in the Āhavanīya fire, saying: "Thou art the expiation for the sin committed against the gods, svāhā! Thou art the expiation for the sin committed against men, svāhā! Thou art the expiation for the sin committed against the ancestors, svāhā! Then, having sat down around the Soma-vessels in the water, they consume it from the front [of the cups] with the formula: "O divine Soma, of thee who art washed in the waters, pressed by men, whose sacrifice is performed, whose Stomas are praised, and whose Ukthas are recited—of that portion which wins horses and which wins cattle, of thee who hast been made into food by the ancestors and invited, I, being invited, partake. Then, having poured out the remnants, they rise and worship the sun.
"We have drunk Soma; we have become immortal; we have beheld the light; we have found the gods. What can hostility do to us? And what, O Immortal One, can the malice of a mortal?

If the sun has already set, they worship the Āhavanīya fire with this *yajus* formula. Then, having run to the Āgnīdhra, they consume curds and drops at the Āgnīdhra fire with the verse: "I have celebrated Dadhikrāvan..."

Then they mutter the *sakhyavaisarjana* formula: "Both are young poets, those two are true lords of the law; O lord of the law of truth, we release our bonds of friendship. Then the Adhvaryu, having turned to the right, having run back facing west, having performed the offerings for the wives (*patnīsaṃyāja*), and having gone eastward and replenished the *dhruvā* ladle, offers six verses: "May Dhātṛ, Rāti, and Savitṛ enjoy this."

There are three *yajus* formulas: "O sacrifice, go to the sacrifice! This is your sacrifice, O Lord of the Sacrifice! O gods, you who know the way! Then, having taken four portions of clarified butter into the *sruva*-ladle, he offers the tenth oblation with the verse, "O Agni, giver of life, enjoying the oblation... At this time, the sacrificer throws his black antelope horn into the *cātvāla* pit, either with the formula, "Thou art the womb of Indra; I set thee in the womb of the sacrifice," or silently. Then the *pratiprasthātṛ* leads the wife forward; she throws a peg into the *cātvāla* pit silently.
They deposit this Avabhṛtha vessel in front of the Āgnīdhra shed, either on a raised mound or upon a hide.

From the *patnīśālā* they take the [cake] for Varuṇa, which has been spread with a base of ghee and sprinkled over; the vessel of clarified butter together with the dipping-spoon (*sruc*) and the pouring-spoon (*sruva*); the sacrificial grass (*barhis*); two garments for wearing at night; the king’s throne-seat made of Udumbara wood; the Udumbara pillar from the *sadas*; the staff of the Maitrāvaruṇa; the *pūtabhṛt* and *ādhavanīya* vessels from the two *havirdhāna* sheds; the cups; the pressing-skin; the two pressing-boards; six pegs; the pressing-stones; the *vāyavya* cups; the *sthālī* and *droṇakalaśa* jars; the two *daśāpavitra* filters; and the dregs (*ṛjīṣa*). All this, along with whatever else is smeared with Soma, is placed upon a black antelope skin. Now, indeed, it is said: [The text continues: "They take the *vāruṇa* [cake], which has been spread with a base of ghee and sprinkled over, the vessel of clarified butter together with the *sruva* and *sruc*, the *barhis*, the two garments for wearing at night, the Udumbara royal throne-seat, the Udumbara pillar from the *sadas*, the staff of the Maitrāvaruṇa, the *pūtabhṛt* and *ādhavanīya* from the two *havirdhānas*, the cups, the pressing-skin, the two pressing-boards, the six pegs, the pressing-stones, the *vāyavya* cups, the *sthālī* and *droṇakalaśa*, the two *daśāpavitra* filters, and the *ṛjīṣa*. All this, together with whatever is smeared with Soma, is placed upon a black antelope skin. Now, indeed, it is said:"
They throw away the other vessels and carry away the *vāyavya* cups; having taken up these, he says to the *prastotṛ*, "O *prastotṛ*, chant the *sāman*.
The *prastotṛ* follows along with the *sāman* and reaches the finale (*nidhana*) three times.
"Man after man goes to his end," so says the Brāhmaṇa.

Then, between the *cātvāla* and the *utkara*, they go out toward the north, [reciting]: "For King Varuṇa has made wide a path for Sūrya to follow; he has made feet to be set down where there was no place to stand, he who speaks away even that which pierces the heart."

At the equinox, they perform the second *nidhana* chant; having looked away from the water, he makes them recite: "A hundred are your remedies, O King, a thousand; may your benevolence be wide and deep. Drive away hatred and destruction far off; release us from whatever sin we have committed. At the edge of the water, they perform the third *nidhana* chant; then they step upon the limit of the waters with the words, "The noose of Varuṇa is stepped upon. Then he throws sacrificial grass (*barhis*) into the water with the verse: "The face of Agni has entered the waters."

"O Son of the Waters, protecting the divine power, may you worship the fuel-stick in every house, O Agni!"—saying this, he makes an offering over it with a spoonful of clarified butter, saying, "May your tongue rise up toward the ghee, Svāhā! Then, having taken four portions into the *sruk* ladle, he performs four *prayāja* offerings excluding the *barhis*. Then he proceeds with the two *ājyabhāga* portions for Agni and Soma. Then, having spread an under-layer of butter, while cutting from the eastern half of the sacrificial cake, he says, "Recite the invitatory verse for Varuṇa!
Having cut from the eastern half, he cuts from the western half and pours clarified butter over it.
Having stepped across and anointed [the butter], and having called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says, "Recite the offering-verse for Varuṇa.

At the *vaṣaṭ*-call, he makes the oblation. Then, having spread an underlayer of butter and taking up the entire portion of the offering for Varuṇa, he says, "Recite the invitatory verse for Agni and Varuṇa, the *Sviṣṭakṛt*s.
He pours butter over it twice. Having called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says, "Recite the offering-verse for Agni and Varuṇa, the *Sviṣṭakṛt*s."

Having uttered the *vaṣaṭ* call, he makes the offering in the eastern part of the northern half, passing over the previous offerings. Then, having taken four portions in the *sruk* ladle, he performs two after-offerings (*anūyāja*s) without the *barhis* grass. Then he places the *sruk* into the water with the formula, "In the ocean is thy heart; enter into the waters. Then he fills it with water with the formula, "May the plants and the waters enter into thee. Thus he offers water into the very waters with the formula, "O Lord of the Sacrifice, [I offer] thee with the oblations of the sacrifice."

At the *sūktavāka* and the *namovāka*, saying "We shall worship; Svāhā!", they pour out this *avabhṛtha* (purificatory bath) whatever has been smeared with Soma. [He says: "O *avabhṛtha*, *nicaṃkuṇa*; thou art a gliding one, *nicaṃkuṇa*. Thou hast wiped away by means of the gods the sin committed against the gods; thou hast wiped away by means of mortals the sin committed against mortals. O God, protect us from wide-reaching harm! Then, with his joined palms, he takes water, saying: "May the waters and the plants be friendly to us."

He sprinkles toward that direction in which he has someone whom he hates, saying: "May they be ill-disposed to him who hates us and whom we hate. Then, having touched water, they cause this *ṛjīṣa* to float away along with the black antelope skin, saying: "O divine waters, this is your embryo; we have made it well-pleased and well-nourished for you. Declare us as doers of good deeds among the gods. He merely touches the drops.

They do not eat; then, having loosened their girdles (*mekhalā*) and their lower garments (*prativasanīya*), they run over each other's backs while immersing themselves. Having put on their upper garments, they rise up with the three verses beginning with "Upward" (*udvatī*): "Upward from the darkness," "Upward that [sun]," and "The bright one. Then he steps toward the edge of the water, saying: "The noose of Varuṇa is cast off; the noose of Varuṇa is thrown away. Then they return without looking back, for the sake of escaping the reach of Varuṇa.
While on the journey, he prepares fuel sticks, saying, "Thou art fuel; may we prosper through thee.

Having arrived, he places them on the Āhavanīya fire with the formula, "Thou art a fuel stick; thou art brilliance; bestow brilliance upon me. Then they worship the Āhavanīya, saying, "I have followed the waters; we have united with their essence. Rich in milk, O Agni, I have come; unite me with splendor. Thereupon, they remove the enclosures.
They turn the two *havirdhāna* sheds around, the southern one to the south and the northern one to the north.

While the Adhvaryu is occupied here, the Pratiprasthātṛ prepares the *udayanīya* offering from the scrapings of the *prāyaṇīya*. This very same Veda, this same stirring-spoon, and this same sacrificial grass are used; then, having lifted up that pot for the cooked rice (*caru*) together with its scorched crust and having washed it, he cooks the *udayanīya* in it.

While that is being cooked in the same manner, he carries the *stambayajus* from behind the *gārhapatya* fire on the *aupasada* altar. This is the well-known procedure for the cake-offering (*pauroḍāśika*): three times with the sacrificial formula (*yajus*) and a fourth time silently. He performs the first tracing of the altar; he mutters the *karaṇa* formula; he digs up [the earth]; from what has been dug up, the *āgnīdhra* carries it away three times. The ritual procedure is the same as that of the *prāyaṇīya* sacrifice; only this much is different.

He offers the *pathyā svasti* first there [in the Soma sacrifice], and he offers it as the penultimate oblation here [in the Agnicayana]. Thus the quarters do not shift. Then, before the *sviṣṭakṛt*, he offers an oblation with the dipping-spoon (*sruva*), saying: "O Agni, those fuel-sticks of thine which exist in all [directions]. By means of this under-layering and over-sprinkling, they indeed sever the continuity of the *dhruvā* offering.
Some, however, offer the *samiṣṭayajus* [at this point].

The concluding rite (udayanīya) concludes with the *śaṃyu*-formula. At this point, he pours out the full vessel within the altar. Then, having taken portions of clarified butter mixed with speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*), he dedicates a barren cow to Mitra and Varuṇa.
Having performed the well-known ritual procedure with its omentum, he has his hair and beard shaved and his nails clipped at the southern edge of the altar.

They perform all the rites for the victim; however, if he does not obtain a barren cow, he cooks *āmikṣā* dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa on the *gārhapatya* fire and proceeds with it on the *āhavanīya*.
This sacrifice concludes with the *ājyabhāga* offerings and the *iḍā* portion.

Then, having consigned the fires into the two kindling woods, having moved away, having churned out the fires, and having spread them out, he offers the *udavasānīyā* sacrifice, an oblation of cake on eight potsherds dedicated to Agni.
Having cooked [the oblation], he sets it down;

for this [offering], there are fifteen *sāmidhenī* verses, five *prayāja* offerings, two *ājyabhāga* portions dedicated to Vṛtrahan, and then the oblation with the verses "O Agni, today... and "For you, O Agni... (RV 6.16.34 and 7.15.1).
The two *saṃyājyā* verses are in the *triṣṭubh* metre.
Having placed the *anvāhārya* rice, he gives a bull as a gift;

thus the sacrifice is completed in its well-known manner. Then, having consigned the fires into the two kindling woods (*araṇī*), having descended from the sacrificial ground, having churned out the fire, and having spread the fires, he offers the former *devikā* oblations: a pap for Anumati, a pap for Rākā, and a cake on twelve potsherds for Dhātṛ.

Having placed the *anvāhārya* rice, he gives a heifer as a gift; that sacrifice concludes in the well-known manner. Then, at that very time, having strewn the *pṛṣṭhyā* lines and having carried forward the waters, he offers the subsequent *devikā* oblations: a pap for Sinīvālī, a pap for Kuhū, and a cake on twelve potsherds for Dhātṛ. Having placed the *anvāhārya* rice, he gives a young bull as a gift; that sacrifice concludes in the well-known manner. Then, having consigned the fires into the two kindling woods, having settled upon his own fire-places, having churned out the fires and spread them out, he performs the evening and morning *agnihotra* offerings.
The Agniṣṭoma is concluded; the Agniṣṵoma is concluded.

Intending to collect the materials for the Pravargya rite, he prepares a wooden spade made of Khadira, Udumbara, Vaiṇava, or Vikaṅkata wood, measuring one fathom (vyāma) or one cubit (aratni) in length, sharpened at both ends. He also prepares prepared clay ready for working, a black antelope skin, earth dug up by a boar, a mound of anthills, a clump of *ūtīka* grass or a clump of wild millet (*vādāra*), goat’s milk, potsherds from a broken vessel, pebbles ground with collyrium, wool from a black sheep, hair from a black antelope skin, a slaughter-stool, a skilled craftsman, and a bamboo stalk.

Having prepared the boiling waters, and having performed either the New Moon sacrifice or a sacrifice under an auspicious constellation, they enter upon the first pacification with the words, "Homage to speech! Then, in front of the hall, he causes a pit to be dug for the altar measuring one bow's length;
he coats that with moistened clay and makes it level with the hollow.

He places these materials nearby: a piece of earth dug up by a boar, an ant-hill, a clump of *ūtīka* grass, or a clump of wild millet, as well as goat’s milk in a shallow vessel. Then, having strewn grass with tips pointing eastward upon the northern side of the equipment, he spreads a black antelope skin over them with the neck pointing east and the hair facing upward. Next, having dug up the ground in front of the northern part of the shed with the wooden sword (*sphya*) and sprinkled it with water, he pours sand thereon;
he makes that mound circular and covers it with sand so that it is shining.
Having covered it with young *kuśa* shoots and knots of *dūrvā* grass, they then enclose it;
they make its door face north.

He places near it shards of pottery, pebbles, powdered collyrium, hair from a ram, hair from a black antelope skin, a slaughter-stool, a skilled worker, and a bamboo stalk. Then, he places the boiling water on the Gārhapatya fire and sets down the wooden sword (*abhri*) within the altar.
They enclose the doors;
they enclose the wife in the *patnīśālā* and strew [grass] around it.

The Brahman and the sacrificer sit down to the south; they perform the first *praśānti* (appeasement) for those for whom it has not yet been performed. Having melted the clarified butter over the *gārhapatya* fire and purified it, and having taken four portions (*caturgṛhīta*) into the ladle (*sruva*), he offers the *sāvitra* oblation into the *āhavanīya* fire while the sacrificer maintains contact with him, reciting:

"The wise ones yoke their minds and yoke their thoughts—the inspired singers of the great, inspired sage. He alone, the knower of the ways, ordains the priestly offices. Great is the praise of the god Savitṛ. He offers the oblation with the words "Svāhā! for one who has not been consecrated (*adīkṣita*).

He mutters [the mantra]. Then he takes up the spade (abhri) with the formula: "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee.
