Regarding this, the Sūtra of the two Teachers says that Upamanyu stated: "Indeed, his potsherds are placed according to the traditional injunction; one should first apply the mantra that is used for turning the embers over the potsherds, and then turn the ember over silently.
This applies whether there is one potsherd or two potsherds.

Baudhāyana used to say: "Whether it be a cake on one potsherd or one on two potsherds, one should set it down using all the mantras for the potsherds. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should set down the potsherds according to their respective positions, but one should not imply the addition of further formulas; and in this case, one should recite the mantra for heating: 'Be heated by the heat of the Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases! Be heated! Be heated! (tapyasva, tapyethām, tapyadhvam)."
The yoga of the skull-bones.

Regarding this, the Sūtra says that Ācārya Aupamanyava used to say: "These [bricks] of his are joined with those very same mantras by which they were laid; then the other [mantra] should be merely the mantra for unloosing."
Regarding the placing over the fire of the boiling waters (madantī).
"One should pour the water across the filter and then place it over the fire," says Baudhāyana; "as the occasion arises," says Śālīki.
Regarding the term "saṃyavana" (the act of kneading).

Regarding the *sūtra*, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana [stated]: "Having drawn water from the *praṇītā* waters with the *sruva* ladle, one should bring it; likewise from the *madantī* waters. One should address both kinds of water as they are being brought with the mantra: 'The waters have united with the waters.'"
Regarding "sexual assault": [it refers to] the act of violating another through sexual contact.

Baudhāyana used to say: "One should indeed touch [the grains] separately for a single oblation, and likewise for various seeds. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Separate touching arises from the act of mixing;
one should not touch oblations that are not being mixed. There is no separate touching for a single oblation—for what [separate touching] could there be for various seeds?"
"Pouring out of the clarified butter," he says.
The Sūtra has been explained by Śālīki; regarding this, Baudhāyana says, and Aupamanyava indeed said, that one should pour out the clarified butter after having completed all the oblations.
Regarding the pouring of water for the consecration.

Regarding the disposal of the water for the Āpyas, Baudhāyana says one should pour it out behind the Gārhapatya fire; Śālīki says one should pass along the front of it; Aupamanyava says one may do so either in front or behind, at the point where the wooden sword (sphyā) is sharpened.

Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "One should perform first that mantra which is for the throwing up of the wooden sword (sphya), and then one should throw up the wooden sword silently."
Regarding the taking possession of the altar.

Regarding the Sūtra, Śālīki said that one should first enclose the buttock, then the southern shoulder, and then the northern; Baudhāyana said that one should enclose it from the front in a clockwise direction; Aupamyava said that one should enclose it from the front in a clockwise direction.
"Yoyupana" means "binding."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should level it with the fourth [line] and raise it up with the fifth.
Regarding the placing of the *prokṣaṇī* waters.
Baudhāyana says that one should pour [the water] along the track of the wooden sword (sphyavartman) and then set it down; Śālīki says that one should set it down without pouring [it].
Regarding the placing of the fuel and the sacrificial grass.
The Sūtra [is] that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says it is the uppermost fuel-stick, regarding the trimming of the Veda-grass.

"One should cleanse the *sruva* and *sruk* ladles after dividing [the water] into five parts," says Baudhāyana; "one should do so with all the water together, pouring it over them repeatedly," says Śālīki.
Regarding the wiping of the *prāśitraharaṇa* vessel.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana, who says one should sweep silently; Śālīki says one should not sweep at all; Aupamanyava [says] one should not sweep.
Regarding the disposal of the *sruva* ladle and the *saṃmārjana* grasses: they are to be thrown into the fire.

Regarding the *sūtra*, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "Having sprinkled them with water, one should throw them away in a place where there is no passage, or on the rubbish-heap; likewise with the firewood-bundles."
"The girding of the wives."

Baudhāyana used to say: "One should gird each of them individually; one should have each look at the Gārhapatya fire; one should have each look at the clarified butter. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should gird all of them together at once; one should have each look at the Gārhapatya fire; one should have each look at the clarified butter. Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "One should gird all of them together at once; one should have them look at the Gārhapatya fire together at once; one should have each look at the clarified butter. Aupamanyavīputra said: "One should complete the entire ritual procedure for each of them individually."
Regarding the term "granthikaraṇa" (the act of tying a knot).

"Releasing the upper noose while the lower one remains," so say the two teachers; "releasing the lower noose while the upper one remains," so says Dīrghavātsya, for it is in this very way that creatures are born.
"When the wife is not present."

Baudhāyana used to say that, while seated in the sacrificer’s place, the sacrificer himself should recite these formulas; regarding this, Śālīki used to say that these formulas are indeed seen to be connected with the wife, and if she is not present, one should not pay any heed to them at all.
Then he causes her to look at the clarified butter.

Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: one should take up what has been looked upon by the wife with the formula, "Thou art brilliance"; then, having taken it up with a chip of wood, he should carry it forward with the formula, "Follow after the brilliance"; then he should place it over the Āhavanīya fire with the formula, "May Agni not take away thy brilliance"; then, having lifted it and placed it to the north of the *prokṣaṇī* waters, he should look at it and purify the *prokṣaṇī* waters with the two [spoons] containing clarified butter.
Regarding the inspection of the clarified butter: |||
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana:
"One should purify the clarified butter after it has been inspected by all. Śālīki says it should be done [after inspection] by anyone at all.
Regarding the taking of the butter-offerings.

Baudhāyana used to say that the Adhvaryu alone should take [the portions] with both sets of formulas—those belonging to the *pauroḍāśika* (cake-offering) and those belonging to the sacrificer—and the sacrificer should follow along with the formulas belonging to the sacrificer. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that the Adhvaryu alone should take [the portions] with both sets of formulas—those belonging to the *pauroḍāśika* and those belonging to the sacrificer—but the sacrificer should not follow along with the formulas belonging to the sacrificer. Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that just as the *pauroḍāśika* formulas do not recur, even so the formulas belonging to the sacrificer should not recur.
Regarding the sprinkling of the fuel and the sacrificial grass.
Regarding the sprinkling of the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), Baudhāyana says one should sprinkle each [blade] three times,
while Śālīki says one should do so once each.

Regarding this, Śālīki said: Baudhāyana used to say that one should sprinkle the tips while standing with "To the sky, svāhā!"; the middle parts while stooping with "To the intermediate space, svāhā!"; and the roots while sitting down with "To the earth, svāhā!

Having sprinkled the knot from the front toward the west together with the offering-ladle, one should pour out the remaining sprinkling water from the southern hip to the northern hip with the formula: "Svadhā to the fathers who sit upon the sacrificial grass; become strength; go to the earth with strength."
"The ladles and the lifting-up."
"One should carry it northward in front of oneself," says Baudhāyana; "one should carry it northward behind oneself," says Śālīki.
He inserts the two strainers into the grass-bundle, either with the formula, "I place out-breath and in-breath in the sacrificer," or silently.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
He hands it over either to the sacrificer or to the Brahman priest.
The former ritual procedure belongs to Śālīki, the latter to Baudhāyana.
"In the place of the cord."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should spread [the grass] after loosening the cord at the southern edge of the altar.
"For the altar, for the strewing."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; however, Śālīki says that one should spread it from this very point toward the east, layer by layer.
Regarding the laying down of the enclosing-sticks.

Baudhāyana used to say that one should place the southern [fire] on top and cover the northern; Śālīki, however, says that one should enclose them so that they are merely touching at their front edges.
Then [the teacher] says, "Now he shall put on [the garment] from the front by means of the sun."
The Sūtra [states] that according to Baudhāyana, one should worship the Āhavanīya fire alone with this Yajus; Śālīki says [one should worship all three].
"He places two fuel-sticks upright," so says the Sūtra of Baudhāyana; "having placed these two upright, he should not let them fall," so says Śālīki.
Regarding the use of the two separating blades (*vidhṛtī*).
Regarding this, the Sūtra of the two teachers states that Dakṣiṇākāra Rāthītara said, "These two should extend across the altar, interlocking.
Aupamanyava says they should be from the middle part [of the altar] and without an inner womb.
The placing of the milking-strainer.
Baudhāyana says that one should set down the *prastara* after untying it; Śālīki says that one should do so without untying it at all.
Regarding the placing of the offering-spoons: thus it is said.

Baudhāyana used to say that one should set down the upabhṛt as if it were slightly tilted back and should support it with the two vidhṛtis; regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one should set them down in their proper sequence and should not support the upabhṛt with the two vidhṛtis.
Regarding the removal of the oblations: [the rule is as follows].

"Baudhāyana says that those which have not been removed from the front are to be removed from the rear; Śālīki says that those which have not been removed from the rear are to be removed from the front; Aupamanyava says [this applies] according to the cutting-off."
Regarding the term "pratyañjana": it means a counter-collyrium.
Baudhāyana used to say that one should anoint both [the vessels], namely the bowls for the cooked rice (caru) and the potsherds; Śālīki says that one should anoint only the potsherds.
The ritual release of the skull-bowls occurs in the office of the Adhvaryu.
Having uttered "udvāsya havīm̐ṣi," the two teachers release [the implements]; Aupamanyava says that one should release the potsherds at the end of the portions while still consuming them.
"The two libations," so it is said.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that the two cords should be interlaced like reins, as for the formal command.
"Baudhāyana says [the call is] 'O Agnīdh, the fires!'; Śālīki says 'O Agnīdh, the fire!'; Aupamanyava says 'O Agnīdh, the enclosing-sticks and the fire!'"
Regarding "transgressing": [it refers to] stepping across.

Regarding the call for the *āśrāvaṇa*: Baudhāyana says that one who is about to offer with the left hand should step across [the altar] from here after having offered there; Śālīki says that one who is about to offer with the right hand should step across from there after having offered here.
"Bauḍhāyana says 'o śrāvaya', Śālīki says 'ā śrāvaya', and Aupamanyava says 'śrāvaya'."
"Excellent! he said.

Regarding this, Śālīke said that Baudhāyana used to say: "Having struck the wooden sword (sphya) with its point upward into the rubbish-heap (utkara), one should choose the ancestral invocation (pravara); then one should cast the wooden sword aside right there and touch it afterwards."
Regarding the selection of the Hotṛ priest.

Baudhāyana used to say: "If his father, or his teacher, or an elder should be the Hotṛ, one should whisper the names of these elders; however, one should utter the name of the Hotṛ loudly," says Śālīki.
[Regarding the manner of offering: "He offers while stepping forward."
Baudhāyana used to say: "One should step forward with the whole body—with both feet, with the oblations, and with the tone—and one should offer each subsequent oblation higher and higher.
Śālīki said: "While stepping forward with the feet alone, one should offer all the oblations in the same place.
Aupamanyava said: "Standing in the same place, one should step forward by means of the oblations alone."

Āñjīgavi says that while standing in the very same place, one should offer oblations to each of the directions in clockwise order and then make an offering with the utterance of "svāhā" in the center.
The oblation of the two portions of clarified butter.
Baudhāyana says that one should offer in the eastern half, facing each other and with arms extended; Śālīki says that one should offer in the eastern half alone, with arms extended.
Regarding the portioning of the sacrificial oblations.

Baudhāyana used to say: "One should first take a portion from the eastern half of the principal oblation, and then from the western half; in this way, the portions of the oblations are taken in a clockwise direction. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should first take a portion from the western half of the principal oblation, and then from the eastern half; in this way, the oblations stand facing eastward. Aupamanyava says: "For those who offer five-fold portions, [the portions] are taken from the middle, the eastern half, and the western half."
"The abode of oblations."

Baudhāyana used to say: "These three alone have their places prescribed—the two Ājyabhāgas and the Sviṣṭakṛt; as for the others, one should offer them according to available space. Śālīki says: "While offering the two *praṣṭī* oblations, one should offer the Sviṣṭakṛt in the eastern part [of the fire].
Aupamanyava says: "One should offer it over the path of the Āghāra-offering, using the ladle. Rāthītara says: "In the middle, moving clockwise in a circular form."
Regarding the performance of the *upāṃśu-yāja* offering.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana says that one should perform the *upāṃśuyāja* with vegetable food (*oṣadha*), offering to Agni-Soma at the full moon and to Viṣṇu at the new moon; regarding this, Śālīki says that one should perform the *upāṃśuyāja* with clarified butter (*ājya*), offering to Soma at the full moon and to Viṣṇu at the new moon; regarding this, Aupamanyava says that one should perform the *upāṃśuyāja* with vegetable food alone, offering to Sarasvant at the full moon and to Sarasvatī at the new moon, while in both cases the offering to Viṣṇu is with clarified butter.
Regarding this, Rāthītara, the son of Kauṇapatañci, used to say: "There should be both a caru-oblation for Viṣṇu and [an offering] for Vaiśvānara; and the sacrificer himself should consume it."
"By the increase of the fifth avadāna."
"One should increase the amount of the medicinal herb," says Baudhāyana; "only that of the clarified butter," says Śālīki.
Regarding the throwing into the fire of the stirring-spoon: |||
Regarding this, Śālīke said that one should not throw the two omentum-spits into the fire according to the principle applied to the stirring-stick; so says Baudhāyana.
Regarding the cutting of the *prāśitra* portion.
Śālīki says that one should cut off the *prāśitra* portion even while still intending to set aside the *sūtra* of Baudhāyana.
Regarding the performance of the *anvāhārya* [rice] offering with clarified butter as the oblation.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
Regarding the placing of the *anvāhārya* rice.

"Having carried [the rice] around both the sacrificer and the Brahman priest from the front, one should set it down on the southern hip," says Baudhāyana; "from that very same place, on the southern hip," says Śālīki, regarding the removal of the *anvāhārya* rice.
"One should carry it out toward the north in front of the ladles," says Baudhāyana; "one should carry it out toward the north behind the ladles," says Śālīki.
Regarding the removal of the remnants of the sacrificial oblation.
"One should remove the offering-ladle northward in front of it," says Baudhāyana; "one should remove it northward behind the ladle," says Śālīki.
The offering of the after-offerings (anūyāja).
According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, one should conclude these oblations facing westward; so says Śālīki.
Regarding the spreading out [of the altar] with the two *vājavatī* verses.

Baudhāyana used to say that one should move the upabhṛt spoon crosswise toward the west and touch it with water; regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one should drag those two [spoons] with their bowls facing eastward, and one should not touch the upabhṛt with water.
Regarding the anointing of the sacrificial grass-bundle (prastara).
"One should anoint each [part] three times," says Baudhāyana;
"once each," says Śālīki.
Regarding the throwing-in of the grass-bundle (prastara).

Baudhāyana used to say: "The Adhvaryu alone should throw [the oblation] into the fire with both sets of formulas, those belonging to the *pauroḍāśika* (cake-offering) and those belonging to the sacrificer; the sacrificer should recite the formulas following the sacrificer’s portion. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "The Adhvaryu alone should throw [the oblation] into the fire with both sets of formulas, those belonging to the *pauroḍāśika* and those belonging to the sacrificer;

the sacrificer should not recite the formulas following the sacrificer’s portion. Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "Just as the *pauroḍāśika* formulas do not recur, even so the sacrificer’s formulas should not recur."
Regarding the placing of the enclosing-sticks (paridhi) upon the fire.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should place these very implements at the commencement itself.
Then he makes an oblation over them with the residue of the offering.
The Sūtra of Baudhāyana is that one should offer oblations over both the prastara and the enclosing sticks; Śālīki says [one should do so only over the prastara].
Regarding the release of the two offering-spoons (*sruc*).
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the circumambulation of the officiating priests during the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana:
"All should circumambulate to the north of the Gārhapatya," says Śālīki,
regarding the joint sacrifice of the wives.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should perform the offerings to the wives with the *dhruva* butter alone, accompanied by the sound of blowing.
"One should perform the Saṃyāja offerings after concealing the wives of the gods," says Baudhāyana; "without concealing them at all," says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of the *śamyuvāka* during the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
"The swelling of Dhruvā," so it is said.
Baudhāyana used to say that both the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer should replenish the *dhruvā* vessel;
Śālīki, however, says that the Adhvaryu alone, having replenished the *dhruvā*, should offer the *samiṣṭayajus*.
The offering of the *samiṣṭayajus* oblation.

Regarding this, the two teachers state in the Sūtra; here Gautama says: having offered with "Svāhā! To Speech!", and having torn off portions from the layers of the sacrificial grass (barhis), having smeared them together and cast them into the *dhruvā* ladle, he should offer over them with "Svāhā! Place [it] in the wind! Svāhā!
Now, therefore, we shall explain the establishment of the sacred fires (*agnyādheya*).
Regarding the phrase "in the provisions" (saṃbhāreṣu):
Regarding the *rāthītara* texts,

Baudhāyana used to say here that one should not perform the rite for a tree struck by lightning, as it is of a terrible form; Śālīki says that one should indeed perform the rite for a tree struck by lightning, but not for one with a nest of *muñja* grass, for its specific ritual application is not known.
Regarding the making of bowls.

Baudhāyana used to say that one should have the pouring-holes made at the tips; thus his offering-ladles (sruk) come to be placed with their bowls facing eastward. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one should have the pouring-holes made at the bases; thus his offering-ladles come to be placed with their bowls facing eastward. It is known from scripture: "Therefore, trees dwell upon the earth with their tops turned downwards."
Regarding the measurement of the *sruc* ladles:
"They should be the length of an arm," says Baudhāyana; "the length of a cubit," says Śālīki; "the length of a span," says Aupamanyava.
"The modification of the form of the *srucaḥ* ladles."
"They should have the lips of an elephant," says Baudhāyana; "the tails of crows," says Śālīki; "the faces of frogs with pouring mouths," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the performance of Ambarīṣa.
"One should construct the ambarīṣa hearth to the north of the fire-hall," says Baudhāyana; "one should go to wherever the ambarīṣa may already be," says Śālīki.
"On a red hide," [it is said].
According to Baudhāyana, the Sūtra states that it should be reddish-brown; according to Śālīki, it should be red.
Regarding the *brahmaudana* (the sacrificial porridge for the Brahmins), there is the view that it is both with and without mantras.
Baudhāyana says that it should be accompanied by a mantra, while Śālīki says it should be performed silently.
Regarding the offering of the Brahma-rice.
Baudhāyana says it should be with a vessel provided with a strainer and accompanied by a mantra; Śālīki says it should be without a strainer and silently.
Regarding the cooking of the Brahmaudana: [the rule is as follows].
"One should cook it in milk," says Baudhāyana; "in water," says Śālīki.

"One should neither pour into it nor pour out from it," says Baudhāyana; "one may at will pour into it but not pour out from it," says Śālīki; "having drained it, [it should be] with broth," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the under-layering of the *brahmaudana* rice porridge.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should not spread [the underlayer].
Regarding the ritual for emerging from the water after the Brahmaudana.
According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, they should sit around right here; according to Śālīki, they should sit around at this very spot.
"The pushing away of the brahmaudana."
"May the sacrifice approach me," or silently; the former alternative is Baudhāyana's, the latter is Śālīki's.
Regarding the consumption of the Brahmaudana: thus it is said.

"Brahmins of ṛṣi lineage alone should consume the *brahmaudana*," says Baudhāyana; "whosoever are restricted in their diet," says Kātya. Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "Only the great officiating priests (*mahartvijas*) should consume the *brahmaudana*, for it is here that they become possessed of the *anūnaptrīya* offerings."
Regarding the placing of the fuel-sticks upon the fire.

Regarding this, Śālīke’s son Baudhāyana used to say: "Once [the priests] have eaten and have not wiped their mouths, one should anoint the fuel-sticks and place them on the fire. Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "One should anoint these [sticks] right there on the side and set them down.

When they have all finished eating, then, having washed that vessel and spread an underlayer of ghee, one should pour out whatever ghee remains in the pot all at once; having anointed the fuel-sticks with that, one should place them on the fire."
"Of the cow, the instrument."

"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki; furthermore, Kātya says that one may perform many [such rites], for there would be a meritorious and auspicious recitation for him.
Regarding the gift of two fire-drills.

Regarding this, the Sūtra of the two Teachers says that Upamanyu used to say: "At the very end of the night, one should hand over the two kindling woods (araṇīs) to him and release the speech with the words, 'I grant you a boon.'"
The smearing of the fire-places.
Regarding this, the Sūtra of the two teachers states that Upamanyu said: "One should smear only the site of the Gārhapatya fire; for that is what becomes burnt."
It is the sowing of the provisions.

Regarding this, the two teachers say in the Sūtra; thereupon Upamanyu said: "Having completed these [sacrificial implements] at the very site of the Gārhapatya fire with all the mantras, one should pour them out in three parts during the carrying of the fuel.
This refers to the carrying of the fuel.
Baudhāyana used to say: "One should first carry [the earth] knee-deep, then navel-deep, and then neck-deep;

one should not carry it beyond the level of the breaths. One should achieve these measures while actually taking up [the earth], but one must certainly not carry it beyond the level of the breaths—so says Śālīki.
The progression of the accumulations.

Regarding this, Śālīke said; however, Baudhāyana said that one should have him step forward with his right forefoot, turning from east to west, so that the embers of the fire already established might fall upon the ritual materials.
"Of the horse's gift," [it is said].
"O Adhvaryus, one should give this horse at the footprint of Agni, and another to the Brahman," says Baudhāyana; "this [horse] to the Brahman, and another to the Adhvaryus," says Śālīki.
Regarding the laying down of the fuel.
According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, one should place the fuel silently; thus says Śālīki.
Regarding the establishment of the Sabhya and Āvasathya fires.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
Regarding the carrying forth of the Sabhya and Āvasathya fires.

"One should carry these two fires away from the *āhavanīya* fire," says Baudhāyana; "from the village fire," says Śālīki; "they should be produced by friction (*nirmanthya*)," says Aupamanyava. Regarding this, Aupamanyavīputra used to say: "One should designate the *sabhya* fire as being in the assembly hall (*sabhā*) and the *āvasathīya* fire as being in the dwelling (*āvasatha*); and on the festival days (*parvan*), having cooked *sthālīpāka* offerings for these two, one should offer them to the Brahman. Āñjīgavi, however, says that one should not even do this.
Regarding the construction of a chariot wheel.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki. Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "One should cause this chariot, already yoked, to move forward;
one should give it to the officiating priests. Āñjīgavi, however, said that even this one should not do.
"The enumeration of the bodies."
"One should recite [the mantra] for each [victim] and then assign it," says Baudhāyana; "one should simply say, 'O Agni, those fierce forms of yours, with them go to so-and-so,'" says Śālīki.
Regarding the phrase "in the sequences of Virāja":
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should simply say, "O manly one, protect my offspring."
Regarding the offering of the full oblation.
According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, one should offer the full-offering (pūrṇāhuti) only after the enclosure has been completed; Śālīki,
however, says that the Agnihotra should be performed silently during the full-offering.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana says that for the Rathītara lineage one should offer only the *pūrṇāhuti* and not the silent *agnihotra*;
Śālīki says that one should offer only the silent *agnihotra* and not the *pūrṇāhuti*.
This is the explanation of the Daśahotuḥ.
Baudhāyana used to say: "Whenever one is about to pour out the oblation or is about to recite the *sāmidhenī* verses, one should indeed recite the *daśahotṛ* formula there;
this is seen [as the rule] in these very *agnyādheya* rituals," says Śālīki; whereas Aupamanyava says: "This is seen [as the rule] in this very *āgneya* cake on eight potsherds."
Regarding the phrase "tantrakaraṇa": it means the act of composing a tantra.

Baudhāyana used to say: "There should be fifteen *sāmidhenī* verses; the two *ājyabhāga* offerings should have the *vārtraghna* verses; the deities should be recited loudly. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "There should be seventeen *sāmidhenī* verses; the two *ājyabhāga* offerings should have the *vṛdhanvat* verses; the deities should be recited in a low voice. Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "In the cake on eight potsherds for Agni, there should be the two *ājyabhāga* offerings with the *vārtraghna* verses; those with the *vṛdhanvat* verses for Indra-Agni and Aditi; those containing the words 'rayimat' (possessing wealth) and 'puṣṭimat' (possessing nourishment) in the oblations to Pavamāna; and those containing the word 'vīta' (enjoyed) in the *anvārambheṣṭi*."
"It is the performance by the sacrificer."
"One should perform the sacrifice using the name [of the sacrificer]," says Baudhāyana.
One should perform the duties of the sacrificer according to the available opportunity; thus says Śālīki.
Regarding the giving of sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*).
Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīke said that Baudhāyana stated: "One should perform all these offerings with sacrificial fees;
one should give three [cows] for each [offering], and a pair at the last one."
Thus ends the *Tantarasamāsa*.

"There is no compendium of ritual procedures (tantra-samāsa) for these two teachers; regarding this, Aupamanyava said: 'A cake on eight potsherds for Agni Pavamāna—this should be the first tantra; then [cakes] for Agni Pāvaka and Agni Śuci—this is the second; then a pap for Indra-Agni and a pap for Aditi should proceed to the end.'"
Regarding the giving of sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā).

This has been declared in the Sūtra by Śālīki; regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that Upamanyava [held] that one should perform all these sacrifices as being accompanied by sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā), giving four [cows] at each [of the first three], and a pair at the last one.
Regarding the performance of an expiation by one who has not performed the Darśapūrṇamāsa sacrifices in their proper sequence.
Baudhāyana says that one should perform it; Śālīki says that one should not perform it.
Regarding the Anvārambheṣṭi sacrifice: thus [it is said].

Regarding the Caturhotṛ, the two Sārasvata oblations, and the Anvārambheṣṭi: Baudhāyana says that one should perform these on the day of preparation (upavasatha), while the others should be performed on the day of the sacrifice (iṣṭi). Śālīki says that one should perform the Caturhotṛ and the two Sārasvata oblations on the day of preparation, while the others should be performed on the day of the sacrifice. Aupamanyava says that one should perform only the Caturhotṛ on the day of preparation, while the others should be performed on the day of the sacrifice. Aupamanyavīputra says that all of this should be performed on the day of the sacrifice. Now, therefore, we shall explain the re-establishment of the sacred fires (punarādheya).
Regarding the words "in the *sarparājñī* verses":

Regarding this, Śālīkei said that Baudhāyana stated: "One lays the Gārhapatya fire with the verses of the Serpent Queen (sarpārājñī); having laid it with six [verses], one should worship it with the seventh."
Regarding the performance of the final oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*).
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
Regarding the phrase "tantrakaraṇa": [it means] "the making of a thread."

Regarding this, Śālīke said, "Baudhāyana used to say that one should perform both sets of ritual procedures—those pertaining to the re-establishment of the fires (*punarādheya*) and those pertaining to the original establishment of the fires (*agnyādheya*). One should offer a cake on eight potsherds for Agni; before the [regular] sacrificial fees for the *agnyādheya* have been given, one should give the fees for the *punarādheya*. Then, one should offer a cake on five potsherds for Agni; before the fees for the *punarādheya* have been given, one should give the fees for the *agnyādheya*. Then there is the oblation of cooked rice for Indra-Agni and for Aditi, and finally the offering to Agni-Varuṇa at the conclusion of the twelve-day period."
The term *dhāna* refers to the case endings (*vibhakti*).

Regarding the *sūtra*, Śālīke said that one should sacrifice after reciting the entire verse; Baudhāyana said that one should add dual-syllabled case-endings (*vibhakti*) belonging to the fire-god (*Āgneyī*); while Aupamanyava said that one should add dual-syllabled case-endings for all [verses].
This is the supplementary oblation for the sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa).
"One should offer the oblation to the deity," says Baudhāyana; "including the sviṣṭakṛt offering," says Śālīki.
This is the etymological explanation of *sviṣṭakṛt*.
"One should recite [the *nigadas*] in their own respective places," says Baudhāyana;
"having recited them in their own places, one may then recite them at will thereafter," says Śālīki; regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say, "There are these five places for the *sviṣṭakṛt*;
one should recite [the *nigadas*] in all of them."
Now, [the rule applies] also to one whose fires have been carried away and to one whose fire-drills are lost.
Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "If the fires are lost or carried away, one need not concern oneself with the re-establishment of the fires (*āgnyādheya*).
From the moment of their original installation (*ādhāna*), the fires are indeed the sacrificer himself;
his out-breath (*prāṇa*) is the Gārhapatya, his in-breath (*apāna*) is the Anvāhāryapacana, and his diffused breath (*vyāna*) is the Āhavanīya."
"One should offer the oblation after having descended to the Kāma [fire]."
Regarding the "spreading out" (viharaṇa) of the fires.
According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, these fires should remain perpetually maintained from the time of their installation; according to Śālīki, they should be so from that very point.
Regarding the placing of the vessels: thus it is said.

Regarding the Sūtra, Śālīkeira said that Baudhāyana stated: "One should set down the vessels either on a grass mat or upon blades of grass; [the offering] proceeds counter-clockwise (apasavya), for wood is joined with wood."
"The oblation is for two."

Baudhāyana used to say: "If the first [offering] should fall into error, one should perform the expiation with the second; but if the second should fall into error, both would be rendered faulty by the error, and one should perform the expiation with yet another. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Whichever of the two should fall into error, both would be rendered faulty by the error; therefore, one should perform the expiation with yet another [offering]. This concerns the kindling of the fire.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should kindle it with a coal from the Gārhapatya fire and carry the fire around it three times.
"Making a path, he carries it out toward the north."
Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana used to say: "In that very place, one should take it down as if establishing it three times;
these are the three worlds, and thus one becomes established in these very worlds."
Regarding the term "unnayana" (the lifting up).
"Either with the *pūrṇāhuti* or with the *anūcya* formulas"— the former alternative belongs to Baudhāyana, the latter to Śālīki.
"Reflection."
Baudhāyana used to say that one should touch both—that which is in the pot and that which has gone into the ladle; Śālīki says that one should touch only that which has gone into the ladle.
Then he places it down behind the Gārhapatya fire.
Baudhāyana says that one should recite the Sūtra before the *atihāya* [formula], while Śālīki says it should be after.
Regarding the term "havana": [it refers to] the act of offering oblations.

"One should offer the oblation after having understood it oneself," says Baudhāyana; "if he has a son or a pupil who is capable of performing the ritual, that person, sitting to the south, should offer it," says Śālīki.
The oblation consists of two offerings.
"One should offer in the front and the back," says Baudhāyana; "in the two flanks," says Śālīki.
Baudhāyana says that one should wipe upwards twice and wipe downwards twice; Śālīki says that one should wipe upwards once and wipe downwards twice.
Having sipped water twice with two fingers and turned toward the north, he consumes [the remnant] with the ladle whose handle points eastward.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should consume [the remnant] with the handle pointing northward.

Having washed the *sruva* ladle, heated it, and filled it with water, he pours it out toward the north behind the *gārhapatya* fire, saying: "Here I offer immortality into Agni Vaiśvānara, svāhā! or "An imperishable offering into the imperishable."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"The worship with the Āgnipāvamānī verses."

Baudhāyana used to say: "Having performed the *upasthāna* (reverential salutation) for the Āhavanīya fire as it presents itself throughout the year, one should then perform the *upasthāna* for the Gārhapatya fire with the *Āgnipāvamānī* verses, then with the *Gāyatrī* verses, then with the *Dvipadā* verses; then, on the following day, [one should proceed] according to the regular order. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Whatever [verses] are prior to and subsequent to the *Āgnipāvamānī* verses—with those, having performed the *upasthāna* for the Āhavanīya fire as it presents itself throughout the year, one should then perform the *upasthāna* for the Gārhapatya fire with the *Āgnipāvamānī* verses, then with the *Gāyatrī* verses..."

"On the next day, [he should recite] the *dvipadā* verses according to their respective order; thus says Aupamanyava. Furthermore, after this point, neither the *āgnipāvamānī* verses nor the *āhavanīya* fire should come into his possession, nor the *gārhapatya* fire. From this point onward, they should serve only for the purpose of private study (*svādhyāya*).
Having performed the worship with the *vyāhṛtis*, he should simply say: 'May I be able to maintain you; may my faith not depart. Thus says Āñjīgavi.
Regarding the phrase "in blessings" (āśiḥṣu):
Baudhāyana used to say that one should first make a wish for oneself, then for those already born, and then for the progeny;

regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one should first make a wish for those already born, then for oneself, and then for the progeny; regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that for one who has no children yet, one should make a wish both for oneself and for the progeny, and that one may make such a wish at will both in the evening and in the morning—so said the son of Aupamanyavī.
Regarding the performance of the Piṇḍapitṛyajña.

Baudhāyana used to say: "From the very beginning one should wear the sacred thread over the right shoulder (prācīnāvīta); he should remain wearing it thus until the offering of the oblations. When about to offer the oblations, he should wear the sacrificial thread over the left shoulder (yajñopavīta);
he should remain wearing it thus until the spreading of the *sakṛdācchinna* grass."

When about to spread the *sakṛdācchinna* grass, he should arrange his sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvīta*); he should remain with the thread in that position until the verse addressed to Prajāpati. However, for the verse addressed to Prajāpati, he should stand facing the Gārhapatya fire with the thread arranged over the left shoulder (*yajñopavītin*). Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one should arrange the thread over the right shoulder from the very beginning.

He should wear the sacred thread over the right shoulder (prācīnāvītī) until the verse addressed to Prajāpati; for the verse addressed to Prajāpati, he should wear it over the left shoulder (yajñopavītī) and go toward the north.
Baudhāyana says that one should silently purify [the grains] once, sprinkle them once, and once form the shape of the *haviskṛt* (the call to the preparer of the oblation).

Śālīki says that one should simply make them well-purified once, pour them into a pot provided with strainers, cook the *sthālīpāka*, pour clarified butter over it, and remove it from the fire toward the north.
The offering of oblations.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should not offer a middle oblation here, and that the wooden spoon itself should be the third.
Regarding the spreading of the grass that has been cut once.

Having gone out from the fire-hall, one should spread the *sakṛdācchinna* grass in the intermediate space between the south and the east, and place the fire-brand (*ulmuka*) to the south; thus says Baudhāyana. Śālīki says that it should be done within [the hall] toward that same direction, and that one should not place the fire-brand here.
Regarding the giving of alms-food: |||
Regarding this, Śālīke said that Baudhāyana used to say: "One should offer the rice-balls from beyond [the boundary] toward this side, moving away from oneself."
The application of collyrium and ointment is the concealment of the mind.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"The offering of the rice-balls," so it is said.
Regarding this, Śālīke said; however, Baudhāyana said that these rice-balls should remain right here, for they have become the remains of food consumed by the ancestors.
"The consumption of what remains."
Baudhāyana says that the sacrificer himself should consume [the portion];
Śālīki says that he should give it to his son or to a pupil,
or have his wife consume it.

"Auspicious offspring will be born to her," says Aupamanyava; "having smelled as much as fits on a finger, one should then throw the rest into the fire," says Aupamanyavīputra; "having removed it to a heap of ashes, one should cover it completely," says Āñjīgavi; "one should cast it into the water," says Maudgalya;
[this concludes] the summary of the ritual procedure for the Āgrayaṇa sacrifice.

"There is no compendium of the Tantras for these two teachers. On this point, Aupamanyava used to say: "Having offered the Soma-oblation, one should then offer the other oblations; thus his oblations have the *caru* as their opening. On this point, Aupamanyavīputra used to say: "The Soma-oblation should be an addition because it is omitted [in the standard sequence]; one should offer it between the Vaiśvadeva and the cake on one potsherd. On this point, Āñjīgavi used to say: "These are three oblations;
there are these three worlds, and thus he finds firm footing in these very worlds. By means of the *śyāmāka* grass for his *prastara*, this requirement is fulfilled."
"The offering of the *ajyāni* oblations."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should offer the *ājyānī* oblations before the *sviṣṭakṛt*.
The cooking of the oblations for the Āgrayaṇa sacrifice.
"One should cook it in milk," says Baudhāyana; "in water," says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of the cake on one potsherd at the Āgrayaṇa sacrifice.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
Regarding the phrase "tantrakaraṇa": [it means] the making of a loom.

Baudhāyana used to say that there should be fifteen *sāmidhenī* verses, the two *ājyabhāga* offerings should be the *vārtraghna* formulas, and one should perform the recitation for the deities and the duties of the sacrificer (*yājamāna*) loudly. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that there should be seventeen *sāmidhenī* verses, the two *ājyabhāga* offerings should be the *vṛdhanvant* formulas, and one should perform the recitation for the deities and the duties of the sacrificer in a low voice (*upāṃśu*).
Regarding the term "viparidhāna": it means "putting on" or "donning."
Baudhāyana used to say that one should set out on a journey after enclosing oneself with the Āhavanīya fire alone;

having returned from his journey, he should worship the Āhavanīya with all the mantras. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one should set out on a journey after enclosing oneself with the fires as they happen to be present;
having returned from his journey, he should worship each one [of the fires] with all the mantras.
"Of one who has gone forth without having attended [to his teacher]."

Regarding the rule that one should worship with the regular [nitya] rite from the place where one remembers [the deity] while away, Baudhāyana says this applies if one remembers; however, Śālīki says that if one does not remember, then upon returning from the journey, one should perform only the regular rite.
Regarding the phrase "at the offering of the journey":

Baudhāyana used to say: "If an expiation has already been performed, one need not pay attention to it for the purpose of offering; however, if it has not been performed, one should offer this [oblation] there. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "In the case of those errors for which specific expiations have been prescribed, those very expiations should be performed there; but in the case of those errors for which no specific expiations have been prescribed, one need not pay any attention to them at all. Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "Whether the expiation has been performed or whether it has not been performed, one should simply offer the *pravasathāhuti* (the journey-oblation) there."
"In the sequences of Virāja."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the sipping of water (ācamana): it is as follows.
Baudhāyana says that one should sip water twice with the mantra and once silently; Śālīki says that one should sip water once with the mantra and twice silently.
Regarding "realization":

Baudhāyana used to say: "One should make all these deities witnesses [by saying], 'O Agni, Lord of Vows, I shall perform the vow'; for Agni is indeed the Lord of Vows among the gods; one should not disregard this. Śālīki says: "One should do exactly that [without making them witnesses]."
"When the skull is lost or broken," it is said.

Regarding this, the two teachers [have spoken]; here Upamanyu said: "Having offered these two spoonfuls with the formulas, 'May the mind delight in the light' and 'The thirty-three threads,' one should then release the other [substance] with the formula, 'May the Gharma go to the gods.
This is the mantra: 'I pour you together with the Yajus. Whether it be milk or clarified butter that has been poured out, one should pour it together with this very mantra."
Regarding the taking of the portions of clarified butter.

Baudhāyana used to say that the Adhvaryu alone should take [the portions] with both sets of formulas—the Pauroḍāśika and the Yājamāna—and the sacrificer should follow along with the Yājamāna formulas. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that the Adhvaryu alone should take [the portions] with both sets of formulas—the Pauroḍāśika and the Yājamāna—but the sacrificer should not follow along with the Yājamāna formulas. Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that just as the Pauroḍāśika formulas do not recur, even so the Yājamāna formulas should not recur.
Regarding the laying down of the enclosing-sticks.

Baudhāyana used to say that the Adhvaryu alone should perform the *paridhāna* (covering) with both sets of formulas—those belonging to the *Pauroḍāśika* section and those belonging to the sacrificer—and that the sacrificer should follow along with the formulas belonging to the sacrificer.

Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that the Adhvaryu alone should perform the *paridhāna* with both sets of formulas—the *Pauroḍāśika* and the *Yājamāna*—but the sacrificer should not follow along with the formulas belonging to the sacrificer. Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that just as the *Pauroḍāśika* formulas do not recur, even so the *Yājamāna* formulas should not recur.
He mutters [the formula] while the two fuel-sticks are being placed upon the fire.

According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, this entire mantra for the yoking of the fire should be used; however, Śālīki says that one should set down the Agnihotra with these vyāhṛtis: "bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ."

Regarding the rule "year after year," Śālīki says that one should set it down on the very night in which one first sets it down; once the year has elapsed, having set it down on that [same] night, one need not pay further attention to it beyond that. On this point Baudhāyana used to say: "The year indeed becomes fully completed for him on the night in which he first sets it down; once the year has elapsed, having set it down on whichever night was prior to that, one need not pay further attention to it beyond that. On this point Aupamanyava used to say: "The year is indeed ascended by him on the night in which he first sets it down; once the year has elapsed, having set it down on whichever night was prior to that, one need not pay further attention to it beyond that."
"One who is performing the New and Full Moon sacrifices should set down the oblations with these sacred utterances (vyāhṛtis)."

Regarding the rule "year after year," Śālīki says that one should place [the sacrificial implements] on whichever full moon day they were first placed at the beginning; when the year has elapsed, having placed them on that same day, one need not concern oneself with anything beyond that. Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that the year indeed becomes "ascended" for him on whichever full moon day they were first placed; when the year has elapsed, having placed them on whichever full moon day occurs prior to that, one need not concern oneself with anything beyond that. Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that the year is truly "ascended" for him on whichever full moon day they were first placed; when the year has elapsed, having placed them on whichever full moon day occurs prior to that, one need not concern oneself with anything beyond that.
"One performing the Cāturmāsya sacrifices should set out the oblations with these vyāhṛtis."

Regarding the rule "year by year," Śālīki says this; however, Baudhāyana used to say that on whichever full moon day one should set out the Vaiśvadeva oblations, when the year has elapsed, having set out the Vaiśvadeva oblations on that [same] day, one need not pay further attention to it beyond that.
On this point, Upamanyu used to say: "Indeed, for him, the year itself becomes repeatedly ascended."

"On whichever full moon day one should set out the Vaiśvadeva oblations, when the year has elapsed, on the full moon day that precedes it, one should set out the Śunāsīrīya oblations; one need not pay further heed beyond that."
The Dhāna is for the Vyāhṛtis.
The former alternative belongs to Baudhāyana; the latter, to Śālīki.
He mutters [the formula] while the *prāśitra* portion is being cut off.

Then, while the *prāśitra* portion is being cut off, he mutters the *sūtra* of Maitreya and the two teachers: "May Agni protect me from ill-performed sacrifice; may Savitṛ [protect me] from the malevolent."
"Regarding the sacrificer's portion: 'May I conquer by means of this whoever acts as an enemy to me, whether he be near or far.'"
Aupamanyava maintains that this entire mantra should be used for the consecration of the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.
He causes the sacrificer to recite the Veda.
Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana recites the formula "Vedaḥ asi, vittiḥ asi, videya" to the sacrificer over the Veda-grass bundle.
Whatever one might covet from an enemy, one should utter that person's name; thus one seizes all of it from him.
Now, if the sacrificer is either a drinker of *surā* liquor or is away on a journey.

Baudhāyana used to say that for one who is away on a journey, one should throw the sacrificer’s portion into the fire together with the *prastara* bundle; having spread a layer of clarified butter around the *dhruvā* ladle and having placed [the portion] therein, one should offer it, for thus the sacrificer’s portion attains the status of the *prastara*. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "From the very beginning, one should not associate with a drinker of *surā*; but if he should associate, one should have him recite the mantras. Why should he not consume the portions? Aupamanyava, however, said: "And he should indeed consume the portions."
This is the worship of the Āditya.
Having gone out from the fire-hall, one should worship the sun; thus says Baudhāyana. Śālīki says that one should do so while remaining right there.
"The making of the upaveṣa [spoon] on the full moon day."
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
Regarding the "conclusion of the vow":
"Baudhāyana says that one should sip water with a mantra and release the vow with a mantra;
Śālīki says that one should sip water silently and release the vow with a mantra; Aupamanyava says that one should release the vow after having performed the rite with the *upaveṣa*."
He mutters the formula for the re-seizing of the sacrifice.

The Sūtra says that one should worship the Āhavanīya fire itself with this Yajus formula; thus says Baudhāyana. Śālīki says that one should worship the Gārhapatya. Now, therefore, we shall explain the animal sacrifice (Paśubandha).
Baudhāyana used to say that the *iṣṭi* and *paśubandha* sacrifices are accompanied by the *upavasatha* day;
Śālīki, however, says they may be either accompanied by the *upavasatha* or performed on the same day (*sadyoyajña*).
Regarding the phrase "iṣṭikaraṇa" (the performance of the sacrifice):

"One should sacrifice with an eight-potherd cake dedicated to Agni for both the animal and the victim," says Baudhāyana; "This is seen in the case of both the brown-eared cow and the goat-ewe," says Śālīki, "and it is more extensive."
"The wooden sword becomes the sacrificial post."

Baudhāyana says that this sacrificial post (yūpa) for the fire-hall attendant is like a wooden sword (sphyaprakāra), being provided with a top-ring (caṣāla); Śālīki says that it should be a wooden sword itself, without a top-ring.
"The sacrificial post is to be forked."

Baudhāyana says that above the time of the girdling, there should be two branches, both four-cornered, and the *caṣāla* should also be four-cornered; whereas the other sacrificial post (*yūpa*) should be eight-cornered.
Śālīki says that this [first] branch should be without a *caṣāla*, while the other sacrificial post should be eight-cornered.
Regarding the phrase "saktukaraṇa" (the making of groats):
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one may also use rice grains.
"The oblation of the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ."
The Sūtra says that Baudhāyana holds that one should offer the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ formula on the very day of the Upavasatha; Śālīki [holds this same view].
"At the invocation for the oblation to the sacrificial post."

Regarding this, Śālīkei said that Baudhāyana used to say: "Having taken clarified butter and the two fire-drills, one should churn the fire near the sacrificial post and offer the oblation for the post."
This is the supplementary oblation for the Āvraścana [sacrifice].

Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana used to say: "In this very manner, having placed gold within the *juhū* ladle, one should make an offering over it with the formula, 'O Tree, grow with a hundred shoots, svāhā! Then, with the formula, 'May we grow with a thousand shoots,' he should touch himself, and thereafter he should touch water."
Regarding the invocation of the sacrificial post (yūpa).
"One should invite him who falls toward the east or the north," says Baudhāyana; "one should indeed invite him in whichever direction he may fall, provided he is not impaired," says Śālīki.
"For the sake of making the object of knowledge known."

Regarding the measurement of the Sūtra according to Aupamanyavīputra, Baudhāyana used to say that it should be commensurate with a chariot: transversely at the back by the axle of a chariot, eastward by the shafts of a chariot, transversely in front by the yoke of a chariot, and the northern *nābhi* by the northern yoke-piece;
or it may be measured by the eye (the distance between the eyes). Śālīki says it should be ten paces on all sides, as the *virāj* is complete in ten.
This concerns the tracing around the *cātvāla*.
Regarding the sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "While tracing the outline in this very manner, one should draw [the lines] on the outside, both to the east and to the north."
Regarding the carrying away of the world-fires.

Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana used to say: "Having seated the Āgnīdhra on the Uttaravedi, one should then carry forth the Lokāgnis"; however, Aupamanyava says that one should carry forth the Lokāgnis from their very designated locations.
Regarding the measurement of the *uttaravedi*:
Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīke said that Baudhāyana stated one should measure [the altar] with the pin of the yoke-horse of a chariot;
in this case, there is no middle altar.
The tracing around of the sacrificial post's pit has been explained.
Regarding the decoration of the *uttaravedi*.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should complete the northern navel on the very day before.
The Agnīdhra follows, striking with the wooden sword at the footprints of the Hotṛ.
Regarding the *sūtra*, Śālīkīra said that Baudhāyana stated: "Having struck them down step by step from the footprints, one should scatter them to the north of the northern *nābhi*."
Regarding the sprinkling of the *uttaravedi*: [the view is that] it is for the sake of purification.
Regarding this, Śālīke said; however, Baudhāyana said that one should sprinkle it with the mantras according to direction and according to the sequence of the mantras.
Regarding the pouring out of what remains.

"One should pour [the water] on the southern shoulder of the altar," says Baudhāyana; "on the high altar (uttaravedi)," says Śālīki; "one should pour it on the southern shoulder only after it has been measured by a chariot," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the sprinkling of the Uttaravedi.

The Sūtra of Baudhāyana is that one should pour the libation over the opposing sides; Śālīki says that while pouring with the *akṣṇayā* (diagonally), having offered in the middle, one should then offer upon the northern part; [this is] the view of Aupamanyava.
Regarding the laying down of the fuel.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should simply place the fuel silently.
The oblation of the sacrificial offerings of the *adhvara*.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should offer four portions of ghee taken four times each.
The taking of the speckled butter, the cleansing, and the placing [of the ladles].
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana:
"One should obtain [the grass] for the wiping and the placing of the *aupabhṛta* ladle. Śālīki says one should not wipe it; Aupamanyava says one should not wipe it.
Regarding the taking of the speckled butter.
"One should take [the portion] up to the end of the *hṛdaya* formula," says Śālīki;

"one should mix the clarified butter and the curds and take [the portion] with these five formulas," says Aupamanyava; regarding this, Aupamanyavīputra used to say: "Having silently spread [the base] twice, having brought the curds while reciting all the formulas, one should silently pour [butter] over it twice."
Regarding the performance of the expiation for the speckled butter (pṛṣadājya).
Baudhāyana says that one should perform the expiation for this very act at the moment of seizing or at the moment of moving forward;
Śālīki says it is at the moment of setting down or at the moment of moving forward; but Aupamanyava says it is not merely upon the appearance of a drop of milk.
Regarding the washing of the sacrificial post.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
however, Śālīki says that one should wash the sacrificial post (yūpa) silently.
Regarding the sprinkling of the sacrificial post.

Baudhāyana used to say: "Having placed near [the sacrificial post] the *svaru*, the rope, the staff for the Maitrāvaruṇa, a chip of the sacrificial post, gold, and a vessel of water, one should sprinkle the sacrificial post; in this way, one should sprinkle those things connected with the post by means of the post, and those things connected with the animal by means of the animal," so says Śālīki.
Regarding the circumambulation of the sacrificial post (yūpa).
"To the south," says Baudhāyana;
"to the north," says Śālīki.
Regarding the anointing of the sacrificial post.
The Sūtra [is] that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says it should be on the Agniṣṭhā pillar alone.
Regarding the pouring of water from a water-pot.
"One should pour it out while moving clockwise," says Baudhāyana; "according to what is convenient," says Śālīki.
Regarding the encircling of the sacrificial post.
"One should recite the mantra three times and repeat the ritual action three times," says Baudhāyana;
"one should recite the mantra only once and perform the ritual action only once," says Śālīki.
"He girds it at the height of the navel."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says it is the Middle Country, regarding the covering over of the *svaru*.
The Sūtra [prescribes] the Agniṣṭoma according to Baudhāyana; Śālīki says it is according to the [other] Śālīka school.
Regarding the ritual preparation of the sacrificial animal.
Regarding this, Aupamanyavīputra’s Sūtra says that Baudhāyana used to say: "One should perform the *upākaraṇa* in this very manner, but one should not approve [the victim].

Śālīki says: "One should both approve it and offer the oblation for the sake of the *upākaraṇa*. Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "In this very manner, one should strike it from the front while it is turned westward with two blades of sacrificial grass (*barhis*) and a branch of the *plakṣa* tree; and having placed the heart upon that *plakṣa* branch, one should cut the portions."
"The smearing together of the two kindling woods."
Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: one should take up a fire-chip with the formula, "Thou art the birthplace of Agni";

he should place either a blade of *dūrvā* grass or another chip down with the formula, "Ye two are the stallions"; he should take up the lower friction-wood (*adharāraṇi*) with the formula, "Thou art Urvaśī"; and the upper friction-wood (*uttarāraṇi*) with the formula, "Purūravas."
Then, having anointed these two in the vessel of clarified butter, he should place them together with the formula: "Anointed with ghee, may you two bestow virility."
"The animal is the grasping of hunger."
Baudhāyana says that one should take it with a mantra, while Śālīki says silently.
Regarding the term "designation of the sacrificial animal":
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should instead place it on the neck.
Regarding the tethering of the sacrificial animal.
According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, one should tie the animal to the sacrificial post itself; thus says Śālīki.
Regarding the sprinkling of the sacrificial animal.
"One should sprinkle with water consecrated silently," says Baudhāyana; "with water from water-pots," says Śālīki.
"The anointing of the animal."
Regarding this sūtra, Śālīke said, but Baudhāyana said that one should place the offering-ladle against the forehead and draw it across without breaking the line as far as the southern hip.
Regarding the production of the *svaruraśana* (the sacrificial post-girdle).
Baudhāyana says that one should produce the sacrificial post (*yūpa*), the *svaru* chip, and the *raśanā* cord; Śālīki says it is the animal (*paśu*);
Aupamanyava says it is the ritual procedure (*tantra*); Aupamanyavīputra says it is the deity (*devatā*);
[and] Atyāśrāvaṇa says it is the call for assent (*atyāśrāvaṇa*).
According to Baudhāyana, one should cause the *atyāśrāvaṇa* call to be made only during the Soma sacrifice; according to Śālīki, [it may be done at other times as well].
The anointing of the sacrificial animal.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana said: "One should not cut from the same part with which one has anointed; rather, one should cut from the cooked portion with this [ladle].
Śālīki says: "It should be according to what is available."
Regarding the carrying of fire around the sacrificial animal.
"One should carry fire around the *śāmitra* [fire]," says Baudhāyana; "whatever is other than the *śāmitra*," says Śālīki;
"both the animal and the clarified butter," says Rāthītara; "the animal alone," says Aupamanyava.
The offering of the Apāvyas.
Baudhāyana used to say that one should offer one oblation in the first round, two in the middle, and two in the last; Śālīki says it should be according to what is available.
Regarding the *upapraiṣa* and the *āśrāvaṇa*: [the former is] the command for the subsequent action, and [the latter is] the call for attention.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should not cause the announcement to be made.
Regarding the slaughter of the sacrificial animal:

"Baudhāyana says it should have its head toward the west and its feet toward the north; Śālīki says it should have its head toward the north and its feet toward the west; Aupamanyava says it should have its head toward the east and its feet toward the north."
"The animal is the casting away of hunger."
Baudhāyana says that one should throw the cord into the *cātvāla* pit; Śālīki says that one should sprinkle it with water in a place where there is no passage.
Regarding the leading forth of the wife.

Regarding this, Śālīke said; however, Baudhāyana used to say that one should lead it forward with the formula "Go, unhindered," and then, having made it look up at the sun, one should lead it forward with the formula "Go, unhindered."
Regarding the inspection of the waters: |||
"One should look down from above the *cātvāla* pit," says Baudhāyana;
"from the side of the animal," says Śālīki.
Regarding the smearing of the sacrificial grass (barhis).

Regarding the offering of the omentum, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "The rest should be as previously described; having smeared it on the other side, one should discard it with the formula, 'Thou art the portion of the Rakṣases,' and then touch water.
This is the rule for the offering of the omentum.

The ladles for the clarified butter may be either made of gold or [ordinary wood]; regarding the second and fourth [ladles], the former option is that of Baudhāyana, while the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the offering of the sacrificial cake for Paśu.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that after having immolated the animal, one should offer the sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa).
Regarding the displacement of the sacrificial animal.
"One should cause the heart and the tongue to move," says Baudhāyana; "the heart alone," says Śālīki.
"The cooking of the heart," it is said.
Regarding this, Śālīke said that Baudhāyana stated: "One should cook it on a spit; one should finish the heart-spit right there, and afterwards one should touch it with the mantra."
"The portioning of the iḍā from the sacrificial cake of the animal sacrifice."

Regarding this, Śālīke said that one should cut the *iḍā* portion for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering after having already made the [initial] portions; Baudhāyana says that it should be done in this same manner for the *savanīya* offerings.
Regarding the performance of the *iḍā-sūna*.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana: "Having placed the heart upon the Plakṣa branch on the sacrificial grass itself, one should cut the portions," says Śālīki.
Regarding the dialogue of the animal victim.
Regarding the *sūtra* of Śālīki, Baudhāyana used to say: having asked [the first question], he should step forward with the words, "May Pūṣan, the guardian of cattle, protect me";

having asked the second time, he should step forward with the words, "May Pūṣan protect me on the path"; and having asked the third time, he should step forward with the words, "May Pūṣan, the overlord, protect me."
Regarding the sprinkling of the animal victim.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana:
"Having sprinkled the heart with speckled butter (pṛṣadājya), one should sprinkle the other organs with clarified butter (ājya)," so says Śālīki.
Regarding the placing of the sacrificial animal.
Baudhāyana says that one should set down the five *hotṛ*s with the formula, while Śālīki says silently.
Regarding the "cutting-off" (avadāna) of the sacrificial animal:

Baudhāyana used to say: "One should take the portions in sequence from the heart, the tongue, and the chest; and here, for those who offer five-fold portions (*pañcāvattin*), one should make a third cutting.

Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should take the portions from all [the organs] in sequence, but one should not make a third cutting here for those who offer five-fold portions," concerning the touching of the animal victim.
Baudhāyana used to say that one should touch both [the portions], those from which he cuts and those contained in the ladle;
Śālīki, however, says that it should be only those contained in the ladle.
"He heats it from the pitcher."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should mix the fat-oblation with the entire side [of the liver].
Regarding the leading back of the animal from the sacrifice.
"One should exchange it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not exchange it," says Śālīki.
Regarding "transgressing": [it refers to] stepping over [the boundary].
Śālīki says that one should cause the announcement (āśrāvaya) after walking around the northern altar (uttaravedi) behind it, according to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana.
"Regarding the sacrifice to the quarters."

Regarding this, Śālīke said that Baudhāyana used to say: one should offer oblations to the common quarters prior to the Vanaspati offering; having offered with "Svāhā to the Quarter," he should worship with "Svāhā to the Quarters! Homage to the Quarters!"
"Of the movement of the tree," [it is said].
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should proceed with four spoonfuls taken from the speckled butter (pṛṣadājya).
Regarding the placement of the *vaniṣṭhu*, Baudhāyana says that one should prepare it as a sixfold portion (*ṣaḍavatta*),
while Śālīki says it should be left entirely intact.
Regarding the *aupayaja* offerings: thus [it is said].
Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "Having drawn out embers from the Āhavanīya fire toward the north, the upayaj-offerer should perform the upayaja offerings upon them."
"Third from the anus," it is said.

"One should perform the *upayaj* offerings by dividing [the material] into eleven parts," says Baudhāyana; "by cutting off [portions]," says Śālīki; "having thrown it all into the fire, one should consecrate it with all the mantras," says Aupamanyava.
Then he wipes his hands on the sacrificial grass.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that they should also bring water for him here, [and that] there is an offering of the *svaru*.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should offer after having placed [the oblation] upon four portions of ghee.
"The joint offering for the wives."
The Sūtra of Baudhāyana states that one should perform the Saṃyāja offerings with clarified butter alone; Śālīki holds this same view.
He sacrifices to the wives of the gods with the upper part of the tail, and to Agni Gṛhapati with the lower part.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki, however, says that all of this should be performed with the tail-flesh placed face upwards.
From the upward-turned tail-tendon, he cuts the *iḍā* for the *hotṛ*; from the downward-turned [tendon], he cuts the sixfold portion for the *agnīdh*.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should perform all of this with the tail-flesh while it is held face upwards.
The performance of the *phalīkaraṇa* oblation.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
"The swelling of Dhruvā."

Baudhāyana used to say that both the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer should replenish the *dhruvā* vessel; Śālīki, however, says that the Adhvaryu alone, having replenished the *dhruvā*, should offer the *samiṣṭayajus* oblations.
The oblation of the *samiṣṭayajus* formulas.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should offer three portions taken four times each.
Regarding the dismissal of the heart-spike (hṛdayaśūla).
Regarding this, Baudhāyana says that one should perform both the *sumitra* and *durmitra* rites, while Śālīki says that one should not perform them.
Regarding the preparation of the sacrificial fuel sticks (*samidh*).
Baudhāyana says that all the wood-piles, including their leaves, should be prepared; Śālīki says that both the sacrificer and his wife [should do so].
Regarding the burning of the sacrificial grass (barhis) from all sides.
"One should burn it around on the southern shoulder of the altar," says Baudhāyana; "on the northern altar," says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of the oblation of parched grain flour (saktu).
"One should perform three oblations of groats," says Baudhāyana; "only one," says Śālīki;
"one should proceed with the oblation of groats only in the forest fire," says Aupamanyava.
The attendance upon the deities has been explained.
Regarding the worship of the sacrificial post (yūpa).
The Sūtra [states] that according to Baudhāyana one should worship the Āhavanīya fire alone with this Yajus formula; Śālīki says [one should worship all three fires].
"Pay attention," [he said].
"One should not heed the Sūtra of Baudhāyana," says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of the final oblation (pūrṇāhuti).
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
"Regarding the gift for the sake of the sacrificial fee."
"One should give either a cow or a bull," says Baudhāyana; "or some other single object of value," says Śālīki; "or some other single object of value," says Śālīki.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the Cāturmāsya sacrifices.

Baudhāyana used to say that the Cāturmāsya sacrifices should be performed throughout one's entire life, with the pairing [of animals] occurring within the first year itself, and one should observe the vow during that first year; regarding this, Śālīki used to say that the Cāturmāsya sacrifices are indeed annual and involve celibacy;
while Aupamanyava says they should follow the specific ritual application.
Regarding milk, there is [the case] with a mantra and [the case] without a mantra.

"Both the evening and morning milkings should be accompanied by mantras," says Baudhāyana; "they should be silent," says Śālīki. Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "The milk-offerings for the Cāturmāsya sacrifices that precede the Soma sacrifice should be silent, but after the Soma sacrifice, they should receive the mantras. Regarding this, Añjīgavi used to say: "Only these five milk-offerings are accompanied by mantras: the curd-mixture for Mitra and Varuṇa in the New and Full Moon sacrifices, the one in the Dākṣāyaṇa sacrifice, the one in the Kauṇḍapāyina sacrifice, and the one in the Sautrāmaṇī sacrifice."
Regarding the performance of the Vaiśvānara and Pārjanya offerings.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
On the full moon day of Phālguna or Caitra, the calves are separated from their mothers for the sake of the Viśvedevas.
According to Baudhāyana, [the time for the rite] is the northern course of the sun, during the waxing fortnight on an auspicious day; according to Śālīki, it is the same.
"The sacrificial grass-strew consists of shoots."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki, however, holds that all this sacrificial grass (barhis) should consist of fresh shoots.
The oblation of the Pañcahotṛ.
The Sūtra says that one should offer the Pañcahotṛ oblation on the very day of the Upavasatha; this is the view of Śālīki, who follows Baudhāyana.
Regarding the consecratory formulas for the fore-sacrifices (prayāja).

Baudhāyana says that one should consecrate four [vessels] with four [mantras] and then follow the others with the fifth; Śālīki says that after consecrating four with four [mantras], one should consecrate all of them at the end with the fifth.
Regarding the single-pot offerings, there is the question of whether they are accompanied by mantras or are mantra-less.
"They should be accompanied by mantras," says Baudhāyana; "they should be silent," says Śālīki.
Regarding the cutting of portions from cakes offered on a single potsherd.

Baudhāyana used to say that one should not cut portions from the Cāturmāsya offerings alone, but rather one should cut portions from the others; regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one should cut portions from those performed on the principal day (tantra-hara) alone, but not from the others; regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that one should not cut portions from that which belongs to the Vaiśvadeva-puruṣī, but rather one should cut portions from the others.
Regarding the supplementary oblation for those offerings made on a single potsherd.
"One should offer with whatever residue remains in the *sruc*," says Baudhāyana; "one should offer each [cake] with four names of the seasons each," says Śālīki;
[this concerns] the sequential carrying away of the remains of the cakes baked on a single potsherd (*ekakapāla*).
"One should carry [the fire] along with [the oblation]," says Baudhāyana; "one should not carry it along with [the oblation]," says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of the Vājina offering.
"One should perform it in a low voice," says Baudhāyana; "aloud," says Śālīki.
Regarding the consumption of the *vājina* [mixture].
Regarding this sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated that while the others should consume [the portion] merely by smelling it, the sacrificer alone should consume it directly.
Regarding the term "nivartana": it means returning.

Baudhāyana says that after shaving with the *nivartana* formula, one should have both the hair and the beard shaved; Śālīki says that after shaving with the *nivartana* formula, one should shave only the beard and not the hair; Aupamanyava says that after shaving with the *nivartana* formula, one should shave neither the beard nor the hair.
Regarding the preparation of the vessels for the southern sacrificial fire-altar during the Varuṇapraghāsa rites.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says they should be made of gold or silver,
while Aupamanyava says they should be made of *śamī* wood.
Regarding the removal of the sacrificial grass and the *yajuṣ* formulas.
Baudhāyana says that in the event of an overlap, one should transpose the two *stambayajus* formulas; Śālīki says they should be performed together.
Regarding the inspection of the clarified butter:
