Baudhāyana says that one should sit to the south of the offering for the New and Full Moon sacrifices, look at the southern [end], and then look at the northern [end]; Śālīki says that one should sit at the junction of the altars, look at the southern [end], and then look at the northern [end]; Aupamanyava says that one should do so from the middle.
"The winnowing basket is made of reeds."
According to Baudhāyana, it should be made of *darbha* grass or *kuśa* grass; according to Śālīki, it should be made of *darbha*; and according to Aupamanyava, it should be actual [fresh] *darbha*.
Regarding the throwing-in of the winnowing basket:
Baudhāyana says that one should throw it in; Śālīki says that one should not throw it in; Aupamanyava says that one should sprinkle it with water and then use it.
Regarding the cutting off of portions from the two curd-masses (āmikṣā).

Regarding the Sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana [stated]: "Having taken portions from the two *āmikṣās*, one should add the ewe; one should not take portions of the *śāmī* leaves, the *karīra* fruits, and the parched barley flour, for these are said to be fodder. Aupamanyava says that one should add all of them together as a single combined portion with the final offering, for the sake of the offering to the Maruts.
The Sūtra [of Baudhāyana] states that one should perform the offering to the Maruts in the northern fire alone; Śālīki says this.
Regarding the throwing of the stirring-stick into the Māruta oblation: [it is done] after the pouring of the clarified butter.
"One should throw it into the fire," says Baudhāyana; "one should not throw it into the fire," says Śālīki.
"The purificatory bath," he says.
Regarding this, the Sūtra of the two teachers states that Upamanyu said: "One should go down for the purificatory bath (avabhṛtha) with both the dregs and the scum."
It is declared that the removal [of the fire] takes place at the edge of the water.
The ritual bath has been described.
The preparation of the fuel-sticks has been explained.
"The offering of Ānīkavata."

"One should wait for the rising of the sun by touching it with the hand," say the two teachers; "one should grasp only the fist as if about to seize it," says Aupamanyava; "one should proceed together with the rays [of the sun]," says Aupamanyavīputra.
This indeed is also the section for the Sāṃtapana [rite], and this is the section for the Kraiḍina [rite].
Regarding the Gṛhamedhīya sacrifice, there is the question of whether it has mantras or is mantra-less.
Baudhāyana says that it should be accompanied by a mantra, while Śālīki says it should be performed silently.
Regarding the offering of the Gṛhamedhīya sacrifice.
Baudhāyana says that [the offering] should be made with a vessel provided with a strainer and accompanied by a mantra; Śālīki says it should be done without a strainer and silently.
Regarding the cooking of the Gṛhamedhīya oblation.
"One should cook it in milk," says Baudhāyana; "in water," says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of the Śākalas.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
Regarding the setting down of the Gṛhamedhīya offering.
Baudhāyana says that one should place the offering on the sacrificial grass itself; Śālīki says it should be placed on those other kuśa blades that have not been used.
Regarding the performance of the Gṛhamedhīya rite.
"One should recite it in a low voice," says Baudhāyana; "aloud," says Śālīki.
Regarding the throwing-in of the Śākala splinters.
"One should throw it into the fire," says Baudhāyana; "one should not throw it into the fire," says Śālīki.
Regarding the cooking for the neighbor.
Baudhāyana says that one should cook [the rice] on the Anvāhāryapacana fire; Śālīki says it should be done at the head of the village.
The oblation of one who has filled the ladle.
Gautama says that after reciting the verses of the two teachers from the Sūtra, one should offer the oblation upon the *hiṃkāra* of the Brahman priest,
using the two blades of grass from the Mahāpitṛyajña.
"Baudhāyana says that this sacrificial grass (barhis) is with its roots,
and in that case there is no touching [of it] again; Śālīki says that it is with a remainder."
Regarding this, as for the established rule that one should touch [the grass] individually, Aupamanyava says that since it has already been cut down at its very root, one should simply cut it again.
Now, this is the half-vessel of milk [milked] for the cow that has been milked by a man.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; however, Śālīki says that if there should be less [liquid], one should top it up with water.
For them, he causes the preparer of the oblation to call out over the rice alone; they set aside the barley.

Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīke said, "Baudhāyana used to say that from the sowing onwards, the ritual involving mantras should be repeated for the barley, but the *haviṣkṛt* call should be performed as a single common rite (*tantra*)."
Regarding the pouring of water for the consecration.
"One should pour out [the water] for the Āpyas behind the Gārhapatya," says Baudhāyana; "having passed it in front," says Śālīki; "either in front or behind," says Aupamanyava.
"By means of the altar as the instrument."

Having gone out from the fire-hall, one should perform [the rite] in the south-eastern intermediate direction, says Baudhāyana; "in that very direction," says Śālīki; "on both sides of the Anvāhāryapacana fire itself," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the kindling of the *anvāhāryapacana* fire.
"They should kindle [the fires] in their own places," says Baudhāyana; "they should carry forward the fuel alone," says Śālīki.
Regarding the taking of the butter-drawings.
Baudhāyana says they may be either fivefold-portions or sixfold-portions,
while Śālīki says they must be sixfold-portions only.
Regarding the sacrificial grass-bundle (prastara), [the question is] whether it is accompanied by a mantra or without a mantra.

Baudhāyana says that both the taking up and the placing down of this [fire] should be done silently, while the rest should be accompanied by mantras; Śālīki says that both the gathering and the placing down of it should be done silently, while the rest should be accompanied by mantras; Aupamanyava says that only the placing down itself should be done silently, while the rest should be accompanied by mantras.
"Strewing [the grass] with three turns from left to right, he goes around."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should mix it with the very substance as it was produced.
"O altar, for the spreading! Thus [he says].
Regarding the laying of the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*), the *Sūtra* of Baudhāyana says one should simply say, "I spread thee, the wool-mouthed," while Śālīki says [the same].

Regarding this, Śālīke said, "Baudhāyana used to say that one should lay down all the enclosing sticks when a rite for the ancestors is being performed, and one should place the northern stick to the south."
Regarding the removal of the oblations.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should remove the oblations exactly as they were cooked.
The movement of the oblations and the duties of the Adhvaryu priest.
Baudhāyana says [it should be done] to the south; Śālīki says to the north.
These officiating priests move about and transpose the oblations.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana:

"In this case, they should not exchange the oblations," says Śālīki; "In this case, they should not exchange the oblations, but the Adhvaryu and the Agnīdhra should simply walk around in opposite directions," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the term "āśrāvaṇa": it refers to the formal announcement.
"Oṃ svadhā," says Baudhāyana; "ā svadhā," says Śālīki; "svadhā," says Aupamanyava.
"Excellent! he said.
The learned Aupamanyava says that one should recite "sūtram ācāryayoḥ" and "vidvān śikṣitvan."
The gift of alms-food has been explained.
The [root] *ākhyā* is prescribed for the acts of applying collyrium and ointment.
The throwing back of the lumps has been explained.
The mantra for the Traiyambaka offerings is "mantra-mantra."
"They should be accompanied by mantras," says Baudhāyana; "they should be silent," says Śālīki; furthermore, Aupamanyava says that one should cook them on a single potsherd.
Regarding "the carrying away of a single firebrand":
"One should take it from the Anvāhāryapacana fire," says Baudhāyana; "from the village fire," says Śālīki.
Having taken this up, they stand in attendance upon the Gārhapatya fire.
Baudhāyana used to say that this mantra belongs to both [the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer], being both an Adhvaryava and a Yājamāna;
Śālīki, however, says it belongs to the Yājamāna alone.
"The uprooting of the Traiyambaka [offerings]," so it is said.

Regarding this, Śālīke said that Baudhāyana used to throw [the grains] up three times without interweaving them, having gone around [the fire] three times, saying, "For Bhaga, thee! For Bhaga, thee! and then he would pour them into the joined palms of the sacrificer.
Regarding this matter, Śālīke said that one should pour [the grain] for the sacrificer alone with the mantra, but silently for the wife if she desires good fortune; so said Baudhāyana.
Then, having poured them into a bag and tied it with two threads, one blue and one red, he fastens it to a dry stump or to a forked branch.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the pouring of water from a water-pot: it means bringing water near [the fire].
"One should pour [the water] while circumambulating to the right," says Baudhāyana; "according to convenience," says Śālīki.
Regarding the sacrifice at the Śunāsīrīya parvan: thus [it is said].

Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana used to say: "If the moon should rise while the fortnight of the waxing moon is still to come after this point, one should perform the Śunāsīrīya sacrifice during that [period];
for this is seen as being for the purpose of sacrificing even in the thirteenth month."
"For the sake of making the object of knowledge known."
"It should be according to the New and Full Moon sacrifices," says Baudhāyana; "it should be according to the Animal Sacrifice," says Śālīki.
Regarding the giving of sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*).

Regarding this, Śālīki said; but Baudhāyana said that one should give gold to the Vaiśvānara [offering], a milch-cow to the Pārjanya, twelve to the Vaiśvadeva, twelve to the Varuṇapraghāsa oblations, three to the Ānīkavata, three to the Sāṃtapana, four to the Gṛhamedhīya, a bull to the Pūrṇadarvya, three to the Kraiḍina, twelve to the Mahāhavis oblations, three to the Āditya, and twelve to the Śunāsīrīya oblations. Regarding this, Upamanyava said that sixty-four dakṣiṇās are traditionally prescribed for the Cāturmāsya sacrifices.
If he should not obtain them, he should give as many churned drinks or cooked rice-messes as there are [verses];
by that means, indeed, he attains that desire.
"At the end of the four-month periods."
"They should end with the Soma," says Baudhāyana; "they should end with the animal sacrifice," says Śālīki;
"one should perform the sacrifice with a Savaneṣṭi," says Aupamanyava.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the Agniṣṭoma.

Baudhāyana used to say: "One should not initiate the sacrificer and the officiating priests without having first seen the King (Soma). Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "If the initiations were to be long, they would have to be performed by those who provide sustenance; therefore, the Udgātṛ may be initiated at his own will."
Regarding the settling upon the hall.

Baudhāyana used to say that one should settle in the hall at midday; the waters should go first, followed by the sacrificer, the King Soma, and the two fire-drills. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one may settle in the hall at will, either in the forenoon or in the afternoon, but one should ensure that the *Dīkṣaṇīyā* offering is completed before sunset.
Regarding the carrying forward of the fires.
Baudhāyana says that one should take up the fires continuously; Śālīki says that one should consign them into the two kindling woods.
"The oblation of the seven hotṛ-priests."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that after having offered the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ, one should offer the Saptahotṛ.
Regarding the oblation for the sacrificial post, it says: "At the invocation."
The former alternative belongs to Baudhāyana, the latter to Śālīki.
Regarding the preparation of garments:
There are eight, says Baudhāyana; there are seven, says Śālīki.
Regarding the preparation of black antelope skins: [the rule is that] one should prepare them.
"Baudhāyana says there are five; Śālīki says there are six."
Regarding the preparation of the black antelope horn.
"It should have three folds," says Baudhāyana; "five folds," says Śālīki;
"it should be made entirely whole," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the "bestowal of the vow":
Regarding the "kam̐sa," Baudhāyana says it is a cup, while Śālīki says it is a goblet.
Regarding the performance of the Pravargya rite.
Baudhāyana used to say, "One should not perform the Pravargya at the first Soma sacrifice, for the subsequent sacrifice will be one that brings him near [to success].
Śālīki says that one should not even go toward the Pravargya; rather, it is a journey to a sacred ford (tīrtha).

Baudhāyana used to say: "Having turned clockwise, one should go to this bathing-place (tīrtha), and then one should turn back from there with the feet away from the body. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Having turned with the feet away from the body, one should go to this bathing-place, and then one should turn clockwise from there."
Then, while he is facing eastward, [the teacher] moistens his right godāna lock with water.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki, however, says that one should perform both of these with the mantra.
"Anointing."

Regarding this sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "Having taken it with the formula, 'Thou art the milk of the great ones,' he should anoint himself with the formula, 'Thou art the bestower of splendor; bestow splendor upon me.'"
Regarding the term "āñjana": [it means] "ointment."

Regarding the sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "Having taken [the ointment] with [the formula], 'Thou art the pupil of Vṛtra,' he should apply it with [the formula], 'Thou art the protector of the eye; protect my eye.'"
Having rubbed three times downwards and twice upwards, he does it five times; for the Brāhmaṇa says, "He anoints five times," and indeed five times on the right side and five times on the left side.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"Wind," it is said.

Baudhāyana used to say: "Having divided [the strainers] into three groups of seven, one should purify [the sacrificer] at the region of the breath with one of them, then at the region of the navel with another, and then at the region of the ankles with the other; then, having sprinkled them with water, one should pull them out toward the north. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One purifies with two, one purifies with three"—having thus purified him by means of these [twenty-one] in twenty-one successive portions, then, having sprinkled them with water, one should pull them out toward the north. Regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say: "One should purify him at the region of the breath using all [the strainers] together."

"May the Lord of Speech purify you; may the Lord of Speech purify you; may the god Savitṛ purify you with an unbroken filter, with the rays of the bright sun"—having recited this for each deity, he should sprinkle it with water and dig it up toward the north.
Then, having laid him down on his left side, he says: "Come hither."
"The southern" is what has been stated; the former ritual procedure belongs to Baudhāyana, while the latter belongs to Śālīki.
Then he should lead him around the front of the Āhavanīya fire.
"With the buttocks" is what was stated previously; this is the ritual procedure of Śālīki, while the latter is that of Baudhāyana.
Regarding the leading forward of the wife.
Regarding this, Śālīki said, but Baudhāyana said that one should purify her while she is indeed pure, lead her forward with the entire verse, and have her sit down behind the Gārhapatya fire.
"The initiation of the wife."
Regarding this, the two teachers cite a Sūtra; therein Aupamanyava said that one should initiate the wife at the end of the *haviṣkṛt* call during the *prāyaṇīya* sacrifice.
"He does not lead the sacrificer to the vow."

Regarding this matter, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "In the ritual procedure (*tantra*) of the Soma sacrifice, the *yājamāna* (duties of the sacrificer) pertaining to the cake-offering (*puroḍāśa*) should be repeated, except for the re-undertaking of the sacrifice."
"He does not gird the wife."

Regarding this, Śālīki said; however, Baudhāyana used to say that one should bind her at the *dīkṣaṇīyā* offering, unbind her once it has been completed, and then, along with the *adhvarika* and the *yājamāna* rites, bind her again according to the *tantra* at each respective *tantra*, thereafter following the ritual procedure pertaining to the cake-offerings (*pauroḍāśika*).
"The swelling of Dhruvā," so it is said.

Baudhāyana used to say that both the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer should replenish the *dhruvā* vessel; Śālīki, however, says that the Adhvaryu alone, having replenished the *dhruvā*, should offer the *dīkṣā* oblations.
The oblation of the initiation-offerings is thus performed.

The Sūtra of Baudhāyana states that one should offer the oblation on the fourth verse after having recited the fifth. Regarding this, Śālīki said that Aupamanyava used to say: "Having offered three consecutive oblations with 'For Ākūti,' 'For Prayuj,' and 'For Sarasvatī, for Pūṣan, for Agni,' one should pass over [the next] and offer this [verse]: 'O divine waters, vast, all-beneficent. Then follows the taking up of the vessel," [and the rule regarding] the two black antelope skins.

"Baudhāyana says that one should consecrate [the sacrificer] with both [skins] joined together; however, Śālīki says that if there is only one, one should sew it against the right side of the abdomen, and thus there should be only a single black antelope skin."
It is the thorough investigation of the white and the black.
"In the bright fortnight it is the thumb, and in the dark fortnight it is the finger; thus one should touch the junction of the bright and dark fortnights," says Baudhāyana.
"One should touch this junction with the flat of the hand," says Śālīki. "And one should touch it with a single finger," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the crawling over the black antelope skin.
Regarding this, Śālīkeṭra said that Baudhāyana used to say: "One should pause after either the first or the second half-verse; with the third [half-verse], one should proceed to the middle part."
The tying of knots has been explained.
Then he wraps his head with the uṣṇīṣa, circumambulating it from left to right.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that he should be completely covered by a garment alone.
Regarding the presentation of the black antelope horn.

Regarding the sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana used to say: "One should hand over the black antelope horn to him with the entire mantra; one should dig up the edge of the altar silently; and one should touch the hairline silently."
Regarding "the infliction of punishment":
Regarding this, Upamanyava said that the two teachers should hand over the staff to him with the entire mantra: "O divine Vanaspati, well-established, standing upright, protect me from misfortune."
Then he causes him to recite the formula for taking hold of the sacrifice.

Regarding the *sūtra* of Śālīki, Baudhāyana used to say: "Indeed, these mantras are seen as being for the purpose of forming the handfuls: 'Svāhā! [I take] the sacrifice with the mind; svāhā! [to] Heaven and Earth; svāhā! from the wide atmosphere; svāhā! I undertake the sacrifice from the wind. Thus [it is said regarding] the forming of the handfuls.

Baudhāyana says that the clenching of the fists should occur when joined with the *vāco yama* (the vow of silence); Śālīki says it should occur from the release of the intermediate consecration (*āvāntaradīkṣā*).
Regarding the term "āvedana":
"One should announce him according to his caste," says Baudhāyana; "one should simply say, 'This Brāhmaṇa has been initiated,'" says Śālīki.
"The milking for the vow."
The Sūtra [follows] Baudhāyana’s view that the sacrificer’s vow should indeed be through the western door; Śālīki says it is by means of the appendage of the two Yajus formulas.

Regarding the two [formulas], Baudhāyana says they should be attached up to the throwing of the black antelope skin; Śālīki says until the release of the intermediate consecration (āvāntaradīkṣā); Aupamanyava says until the bringing of the sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā).
Regarding the two *yajus* mantras for lying down:

Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana used to say: "One who is about to undertake the vow should lie down with the mantra, 'O Agni, do thou watch well,' and he should sip water with the mantra, 'We meditate upon the divine thought.'"
Then he sends out those who carry the sacrificial gifts.

"Baudhāyana says [it should be used] except for the Ugra and the Śūdra; Śālīki says [it should be used] except for the Ugiras; Aupamanyava says [it should be used] for the accomplishment of all sacrifices—namely, the yajus for lying down, the yajus for waking up, the yajus for setting out, and the yajus for mounting."
"Baudhāyana says that these [rites] are numerous as secondary attachments;
Śālīki says they should be performed only once, either for the day or for the night."
Regarding the acceptance of sacrificial gifts.

Baudhāyana used to say that one should accept with the mantra whatever has been born [as an animal], and when it has returned again, one should likewise accept it with the mantra. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one should accept with the mantra whatever has been born; for him, that would indeed be accepted, but from this point forward, only what is newly arrived should be accepted with the mantra.
Giving to one who is unknown.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the term "prayāṇa" (departure).
The former ritual procedure belongs to Śālīki; the latter belongs to Baudhāyana.
Now, if while he is walking, someone approaches him at the time for his vow.

Baudhāyana says that one should churn the fires, spread them out, and then observe the vow; Śālīki says that one should place the two fire-sticks (araṇī) to the north, enclose the area to the south, and then observe the vow.
Now, if he comes upon water that has not been bridged over.

Regarding this, Śālīke said; however, Baudhāyana used to say that wherever one comes upon water that has not yet been crossed over, one should mutter: "O divine waters, O child of the waters, that wave of yours which is fit for oblation, powerful, and most intoxicating—that I take from you.

He should take three clods of earth; he should place one of them at the edge of the water with the words, "May I not step upon you. Then, while walking along, he should follow another with the verse, "The unbroken thread [of life]. Then he should place the last one at the edge of the water with the words, "May I go along the earth."
"He either plunges in or crosses over; having made a bridge, he passes beyond," so says the Brāhmaṇa.
"On a red hide," [it is said].
According to Baudhāyana, the Sūtra states that it should be unmarked; according to Śālīki, it should be marked.
"Gold is indeed the grasping of immortality."
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
Regarding the settling upon the sacrificial ground for the gods.

Regarding this, Upamanyava said that the two teachers [Āśvalāyana and Śāṅkhāyana] maintain that one should settle upon the sacrificial ground (*devayajana*) only after the threefold classification has been determined; for it is known from scripture: "This earth is indeed the entire altar."
The offering of the Prāyaṇīya oblation has been explained.
Regarding the cooking of the *prāyaṇīya* offering.
"One should cook it in milk," says Baudhāyana; "in water," says Śālīki.
Regarding the placing of the *prāyaṇīya* [offering].
"One should set down the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ-oblation," says Baudhāyana;
"silently," says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of the *prāyaṇīya* [offering]:
"One should perform it in a low voice," says Baudhāyana; "aloud," says Śālīki.
Regarding the gazing at the sun: [it is performed] thus.
"One should cause [the sacrificer] to gaze at the sun with gold interposed," says Baudhāyana; "without interposing anything at all," says Śālīki.
"By means of the purchase-cow, [he] overcomes [the enemy]," so it is said.
Baudhāyana says that one should cause [the sacrificer] to know [the time] at the time of the Sadas; Śālīki says it is at the time of the Uparavas.
The following of the footprint of the cow intended for the purchase of Soma.

Baudhāyana says that for one who has passed beyond the time of the *pṛṣṭhya* [stotra], one should step along the front part of the right foot; Śālīki says that for one who has passed beyond [the time], it may be done on any part whatsoever of the great altar (*mahāvedi*).
Regarding the tracing around the footprint of the animal intended for purchase.

Regarding the pouring of water from the water-vessel, Śālīkeira said in the Sūtra, "Baudhāyana used to say that one should trace around the footprint with both the wooden sword (*sphyá*) and the black antelope horn (*kṛṣṇaviṣāṇā*), with the black antelope horn being on the inside."
"One should pour [the water] while moving clockwise," says Baudhāyana; "according to convenience," says Śālīki.
"Attendance upon the king."

Baudhāyana used to say: "There is this herb named Uṣas; one should make it the messenger and say to Soma on her behalf: 'This is your Gāyatra portion,' 'This is your Triṣṭubh portion,' 'This is your Jagatī portion,' and 'May he attain the sovereignty of the Chandomas. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Since this King [Soma] is indeed present in person, one should worship him as if he were visibly present, saying: 'This is your Gāyatra portion, this is your Triṣṭubh portion, this is your Jagatī portion.'"
"O portion of the Chandomas, go to sovereignty!"
"The pride of the king."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should measure this verse five times while reciting it as a Nigada.
"The king's wager."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; however, Śālīki says that one should simply say, "I will purchase [the Soma] with a cow for you."
Regarding the seizing of the she-goat.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should mutter the mantra without even holding the goat close.
This is the ritual for the handing over of the staff to the Maitrāvaruṇa priest.
Regarding this, the two teachers state in the Sūtra; however, Aupamanyava says that one should approach the soma-seller with a water-pitcher and hand over the staff to the Maitrāvaruṇa right there.
Regarding the king's counter-attack.
Baudhāyana says that one should fasten it with a skin having the hair inside; Śālīki says with a skin having the neck upwards and the hair outside.
"The grasping of the pole."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should mutter the mantra while moving westward without any physical contact with them.
Regarding the king’s carrying away [of the body].
"One should carry it around clockwise," says Baudhāyana; "as it happens," says Śālīki.
Regarding "waiting upon the king": [it means] attending to the king.

Baudhāyana used to say that one should worship the King (Soma) with rice grains, two kindling-sticks, and the royal throne-seat (*rājāsandi*). Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one should worship the King with a fresh piece of wood held by the handle, a firebrand, and the royal throne-seat.
It is known from tradition: "The animal sacrifice for Agni and Soma should be a reddish-brown, hornless, castrated goat, possessing a dewlap and being fat;
this constitutes the preparation of the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) for the guest-offering (*ātithya*)."
"One should perform the mantras beginning with the taking up of the sword," says Baudhāyana;
"those beginning with the cord," says Śālīki;
"those beginning with the gathering of materials," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the offering of the guest-oblation (ātithya).

Regarding this, Śālīke said that one should offer the guest-offering after having unyoked both [the oxen] and caused the King Soma to enter. Baudhāyana, however, says that one should offer the guest-offering after having unyoked both and caused the King Soma to enter.
Regarding "in service to the king":
Regarding this, Śālīke said that Baudhāyana used to say: "One should attend upon the King with the Ṛgveda verses alone; one should present the guest-offering (arghya) with the Ṛgveda verses alone."
Regarding the term "arhaṇa": it means "worthy of honor" or "veneration."
"One should honor them in the order they arrived," says Baudhāyana; "having honored the King, one should then honor the officiating priests," says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of hospitality.
Baudhāyana says there should be both a sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa) and a cow;
Śālīki says there should be only a sacrificial cake.
Regarding the taking of the butter-offerings.
"They may be either fourfold-drawn or fivefold-drawn," says Baudhāyana;
"only fivefold-drawn," says Śālīki.
Regarding the setting down of the guest-offering (ātithya).
Baudhāyana says that one should set down the Caturhotṛ cups with the formulas; Śālīki says silently.
"Regarding the performance of hospitality."
"One should perform it in a low voice," says Baudhāyana; "aloud," says Śālīki.
Regarding the consumption of the *tānunaptra* offering:
Regarding this, Śālīke said that Baudhāyana used to say: "Having caused it to be deposited in a well-concealed place, one should consume it together with the *vrata* at the time of the *vrata*."
It is the consecration of the sacrificial grass for the *aupasada* rite.
"One should perform the mantras beginning with the taking up of the sword," says Baudhāyana;
"those beginning with the cord (śulba)," says Śālīki; "those beginning with the gathering of materials (saṃbharaṇa)," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the question of whether the *upasad* rites have mantras or are mantra-less:
"They should be accompanied by mantras," says Baudhāyana;

"they should be silent," says Śālīki; "that which is poured out [paryājyam] should be silent, while the rest should be accompanied by mantras," says Aupamanyava; "one should perform this entire rite according to the ritual procedure (āvṛt)," says Aupamanyavīputra.
The offering of oblations.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should conclude these oblations facing eastward.
This is the oblation of the Upasads.
Regarding the Sūtra, Baudhāyana says that one should offer the Upasad oblations without stepping across; Śālīki says the same.
Regarding the resting of the offering-ladles: [the rule is as follows].

Regarding the carrying away of the *stambayajus*, Baudhāyana says that they should lie down for a full day and night; Śālīki says for the day alone; and Aupamanyava says that one should perform it at the commencement of each individual ritual act.
According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, the Āgnīdhra should carry [the stones] even from the time of the uparava holes; so says Śālīki.
And the tracing out of the *cātvāla* pit has been explained.
The removal of the world-fires has been explained.
Regarding the attendance upon the wooden sword and the winnowing basket.

Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana [prescribes] that one should perform the second tracing around while the fire is present, and having leveled the ground and fixed the wooden sword (sphya) across it, one should cause the sacrificer to stand upon the heap of rubbish (utkara) facing the wooden sword and the mallets.
The consecration of the sacrificial grass (barhis) for the offering to Agni and Soma.
"One should recite the mantras beginning with the taking up of the sword," says Baudhāyana;
"those beginning with the cord," says Śālīki;
"those beginning with the gathering of materials," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the following walk of the animal dedicated to Agni and Soma.
"One should follow along," says Baudhāyana; "one should not follow along," says Śālīki.
Regarding the placing of the fuel and the sacrificial grass.
Regarding this, the two teachers say that Upamanyu used to say: "One should bring the fuel and sacrificial grass for him while he is still seated right here;
having taken them, he should go forward with kusha grass in his hand, proceeding eastward until the time for the *prṣṭhyā* line, spreading [the grass] as he goes."
Regarding the turning toward the two *havirdhāna* carts:
"One should turn [the fire] back after placing either wood or grass in between," says Baudhāyana; "without placing anything in between," says Śālīki.
Regarding the sprinkling of the two Havirdhāna carts.
"One should sprinkle with water consecrated silently," says Baudhāyana; "with water from water-pots," says Śālīki.
Regarding the phrase "the oblation over the two paths":

Regarding this, Aupamanyavīputra says that one should offer oblations upon the track of the southern *havirdhāna* cart; one should anoint all the axles and hubs, and touch them all around. Regarding this, Baudhāyana says that one should offer oblations upon the track of the southern *havirdhāna* cart, anoint all the axles and hubs, and touch them all around. Regarding this, Śālīki says that one should offer oblations upon all the tracks, anoint all the axles and hubs, and touch them all around.
"Thus is the destruction of pride."
Baudhāyana used to say that one should fix the central post to the south of the southern *havirdhāna* cart and to the south of the northern one;
Śālīki said it should be both to the south and to the north; Aupamanyava said it should be in the middle.
Regarding the sewing together of the door-posts and the beams.
"One should sew all the door-arms with the mantra," says Baudhāyana;
"the ones on the east first," says Śālīki; "the ones on the south first," says Aupamanyava—this concerns the offering over the Audumbarī post.

The Sūtra belongs to Aupamanyavīputra; however, Baudhāyana used to say that while offering in this very manner, one should offer after placing gold in between; Śālīki says that one should place the gold upon both forks (of the ladle) and then offer.
Regarding the drawing of the *vasatīvarī* waters.
Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana used to say: one should draw the *vasatīvarī* waters so that they are bright on both sides and contain the sun;
those [waters] are bright, and with them one should cause [the Soma] to swell.
Aupamanyava says that one should press with those [waters], having poured them over the hearth-mounds (dhiṣṇiya), and then take up the Vasatīvarī waters.
Regarding the scraping of the sounding-holes.
"One should draw each one three times," says Baudhāyana; "once each," says Śālīki.
"The carrying away [of the Soma] from the slaughter-ground to the high-pressing stones."
Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "Having stepped over the footprint of the sacrificer and having carried away the utkara, one should touch water."
Regarding the sprinkling of the *uparava* holes.
"One should sprinkle each one three times," says Baudhāyana;
"once each," says Śālīki; "one should pour water into it and scatter barley-grains into it—one should perform this threefold rite in this manner," says Aupamanyava.
"Aupamanyavīputra says that one should perform all of this while covered."
Regarding the pouring out of the *dhiṣṇiya* hearths.

Baudhāyana used to say: "One should pile the Āgnīdhrīya hearth at the edge of the altar, and the Mārjālīya at the edge of the altar; having piled the Dhiṣṇiya hearths, one should effect a northward alignment. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should pile the Āgnīdhrīya within the altar, and the Mārjālīya within the altar; having piled the Dhiṣṇiya hearths, one should not effect a northward alignment."
"O altar, for the spreading! [he says].

Regarding the Sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana [stated]: "Three [bundles] from the south, three from the north, and the seventh in the middle; they should proceed while spreading them eastward at the time of the *pṛṣṭhyā*.
Aupamanyava, however, says: "They should step over it from the front while spreading them westward."
Regarding the taking up and setting down of the clarified butter portions for the offering to Agni and Soma.

According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, one should take the clarified butter portions for the Agniṣomīya sacrifice in the wife’s hall itself and place them on the mound; according to Śālīki, one should do so [in the same manner].
Regarding the term "samanvānayana": it means bringing together or reflecting upon.
"One should not heed the Sūtra of Baudhāyana," says Śālīki.
Regarding the "bestowal of the vow of the half-breast."
Baudhāyana says that one should offer the old Gārhapatya fire, whether it has been consecrated or not, with the vow of half-a-cup; Śālīki says that one should not offer the vow of half-a-cup.
The oblation for the concluding rites.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should offer four oblations of four-draught portions.
The carrying forward of the *vasatīvarī* waters.
"One should carry them along," says Baudhāyana; "one should not carry them along," says Śālīki.
This is the supplementary oblation of the omenta.
"One should offer each of those [oblations] individually," says Baudhāyana; "both from the beginning and from the end," says Śālīki.
"The dismissal of heart-pains."
"One should remove them one by one," says Baudhāyana; "all together," says Śālīki.
Regarding the carrying around of the *vasatīvarī* waters.

Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana used to say: "While carrying them around in this very manner, having placed them in front of the sacrificial post and having set them down behind the Gārhapatya fire, one should touch them while they are deposited in the Āgnīdhra shed with the formula, 'Be watchful at the sacrifice,' at the time of taking and placing the portions of clarified butter for the *savanīya* offering."
The Sūtra [of Baudhāyana] states that the Āgnīdhra alone should take the clarified butter portions for the Savanīya [offering] and place them on the mound;
Śālīki says they should be placed there.
Regarding the laying of the great enclosing-sticks made of Udumbara wood.
Regarding this point, Upamanyava said that these should indeed be *sruva*-mantras for both teachers.
Regarding the king’s descent: [the ritual procedure].
Regarding this, the two teachers say in the Sūtra; however, Aupamanyava used to say that one should bring down the King (Soma) at the morning pressing itself from all the pressings.
The oblation of the Pañcahotṛ.
The Sūtra [prescribes] Baudhāyana’s view that, having offered the Caturhotṛ oblation, one should offer the Pañcahotṛ; thus says Śālīki.
Regarding the commencement of the Prātaranuvāka.
Regarding this, the two teachers state in the Sūtra: "Ārtabhāgīputra used to say that one should commence the morning litany (prātaranuvāka) with a silent offering of a single potsherd."
Regarding the offering of the *savanīya* oblations:
Regarding this, the two teachers say in the Sūtra; among them, Aupamanyava said that one should offer the *savanīya* oblations at the morning pressing alone for all three pressings.
For them, he causes the preparer of the oblation to call out specifically over the rice; they then take up the barley.

Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "From the pouring [of the grains] onwards, the ritual actions accompanied by mantras should be repeated for the barley; however, the *haviṣkṛt* call should be performed as a single, common procedure (*tantra*)."
Regarding the pouring of water for the consecration.
"One should pour out [the water] for the Āpyas behind the Gārhapatya," says Baudhāyana; "having passed it in front," says Śālīki; "either in front or behind," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the placing of the vessels: thus it is said.
Regarding this, Śālīkīra said that Baudhāyana stated: "One should place the vessels on the mound (khara) and take them up as required."
Then he draws the Ekadhana cups, either with the formula, "O Indra, I draw you who are pleasing," or silently.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana, the latter that of Śālīki; [the view] of Apta is that it spills over.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana says that one should cause [the water] to spill from the Hotṛ’s cup so as to obtain it; Śālīki says it should be from the Vāsatīvara jar.
"Kratukaraṇa" means the instrument of the sacrifice.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should perform his ritual acts according to the specific sacrifice itself.
Regarding the drawing of the *dadhigraha* cup.

Regarding this, Śālīke said; however, Baudhāyana used to say that one should take it with a vessel made of udumbara wood, and having offered it, one should throw that very vessel into the fire right there.
"Regarding the gift for the sake of the sacrificial fee."
This sūtra is indeed twofold.
Over those *nigrābhya* waters, he causes the sacrificer to recite.

Regarding this, Śālīke said that Baudhāyana [prescribes] that one should hold [the ladle] either on the thigh or against the chest, and while grasping them, cause the sacrificer to recite the formula.
Regarding the offering for the king: [it is performed] thus.
Regarding this, the two teachers say in the Sūtra; however, Aupamanyava used to say that one should prepare the King [Soma] at the morning pressing itself for all the pressings.
When the two portions have been spilled, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite.

Regarding the mantra for when the *upām̐śu* cup is spilled, Baudhāyana says one should have it recited at the very moment of spilling, while Śālīki says one should do so after the *upām̐śu* offering has been completed.
The oblation for Śvitra and Antaryāman follows next.

The Sūtra [of Baudhāyana] states that one should offer when both [the moon and the sun] have risen; Śālīki says one should offer when both have not yet risen; Aupamanyava says [one should offer when both have risen].
Regarding the drawing of the Āgrayaṇa cup:

Regarding this sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "One should draw [the draughts] from two streams at the morning pressing, from three at the midday pressing, and from four at the third pressing."
Regarding the verses to be recited over the portions of food: "dra psānumantraṇīyāsu."

Regarding the drawing of the Pavamāna cups, Baudhāyana’s Sūtra states that one should offer these as spoon-oblations (sruvāhuti), while Śālīki maintains that they should be offered as such during the drawing of the Pavamāna cups.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should wipe them clean while they are still joined together and then set them down.
The oblation of the *saṃtanī* verses.
Regarding this, Śālīke said; however, Baudhāyana used to say that one should also pour down the *vasatīvarī* waters with these same mantras.
Regarding the introductory rite for the Pavamāna hymns.
According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, one should take up two blades of sacrificial grass from the *sadas* itself and perform the *upākaraṇa*; so says Śālīki.
Regarding the seating of the Brahman priest.
Baudhāyana says that one should sit down just as in the *sadasya* rite; Śālīki says it should be just as in the *darśapūrṇamāsa* sacrifices.
Regarding the seating of the sacrificer.
Baudhāyana says that one should sit down just as in the case of the sacrificial assembly; Śālīki says it should be just as in the case of the New and Full Moon sacrifices.
Then he hands two blades of sacrificial grass to either the Udgātṛ or the Prastotṛ.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"Thou art the under-layer for the Ṛg and Sāman, for the procreation of the pair," or silently.
The former ritual manual belongs to Śālīki; the latter belongs to Baudhāyana.
When the fifth [vow] has been introduced, he causes [the student] to recite.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one may cause [the sacrificer] to recite on any [verse] whatsoever.
"The oblation of the seven hotṛs."
The Sūtra says that one should offer the Saptahotṛ formula at each pressing; this is the view of Baudhāyana, while Śālīki holds that it should be offered only at the morning pressing.
Regarding the distribution of the hearths (dhiṣṇiyas).

Baudhāyana used to say: "Having taken embers from the Āgnīdhrīya fire, one should scatter them there in the Āgnīdhrīya; then, having spread the other hearths (dhiṣṇiyas) in their proper sequence, one should make them lie with their tops facing north. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Having taken embers from the Āgnīdhrīya fire, one should scatter them there in the Āgnīdhrīya; then, having spread the other hearths in their proper sequence, one should not make them lie with their tops facing north."
Regarding the sprinkling of the *dhiṣṇiya* hearths.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the production of the *svaruraśana* (the sacrificial post-girdle).
Baudhāyana says that one should produce the sacrificial post, the svaru-chip, and the cord; Śālīki says it is the animal;
Aupamanyava says it is the ritual procedure (tantra); and Aupamanyavīputra says it is the deity.
Regarding the term "sarpaṇa": it means "creeping" or "gliding."
According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, the sacrificer should stand at the western door; according to Śālīki, he should stand at the eastern door.
Regarding the divisions of the *ukthya* chants during the third pressing.

Baudhāyana used to say that one should indeed proceed from the Ukthya-vigrahas belonging to the third pressing, to the Ṣoḍaśin, to the night-rounds, and to the Rathantara-sandhi; regarding this, Śālīki used to say that this is merely an extension of the third pressing, and whatever one proceeds with at the third pressing, that should be considered as already proceeded for them; Aupamanyava, however, said that one should proceed from all the pressings together at the morning pressing itself.
Regarding the curd-mixture (āmikṣā), [the question arises] whether it is with a mantra or without a mantra.

"It should be accompanied by mantras and one should follow all the pressings," says Baudhāyana; "it should be silent and one should follow all the pressings," says Śālīki; "it should be accompanied by mantras, and it should be performed specifically at the morning pressing," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the removal of the *savanīya* offerings.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should remove the Savanīya offerings in separate vessels.
"Every morning, [he recites] 'prātaḥsāvasya'."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should simply say, "of the morning pressing."
Regarding the carrying forward of the portions for the *savanīya* offerings.
"One should carry it along," says Baudhāyana; "one should not carry it along," says Śālīki.
Regarding the apprehension of those things to be refuted.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should draw the Pratinirgrāhyas only from the cups for the dual deities.
Regarding the term "āghāra" (libation):

The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana: "One should offer this Āghāra-libation from the very moment of taking [the ladle]. Śālīki says it should be from the Droṇakalaśa with the *pariplu* ladle. Aupamanyava says one should merely mutter this Yajus formula and not offer this Āghāra-libation at all; so says Āñjīgavi.
"The lid for the vessel of the residue."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should cover up whatever residue of the mixture remains.
"The place of origin of the cups."

"One should extend the *sruva*-ladles forward from the front," says Baudhāyana; "one should extend the *sruva*-ladles backward toward the north," says Śālīki; [this concerns] the junction of the two ladles.
Regarding the two *aratni* and the two cups, Baudhāyana says they should be joined together, while Śālīki says they should be only the two cups.
"To him who possesses seed, to him who possesses the churning-stick," [he says].
Śālīki says that one should simply say "of Baudhāyana" and "of Manthivant."
"The oblation of the sediment of the parched grains is performed with the Manthin cup."
Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "Having drawn out embers from the Āhavanīya fire toward the north, one should offer the residue of the Manthin cup upon them."
The offering of the cups belonging to the Hotrakas.

Baudhāyana used to say: "One should offer these together with the Śukra and Manthin cups once, [after they have been] drawn twice. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should not offer these together with the Śukra and Manthin cups once; rather, one should offer them only after they have been drawn twice."
Regarding the consumption of the cups belonging to two deities.

The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana: "One should consume the cups for the dual deities while holding them to one's breath," says Śālīki; "One should consume them with the long formula alone," says Aupamanyava.
Now, he makes these vessels for the dual deities non-empty.
According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, these [vessels] should be emptied by means of the Soma sacrifice; according to Śālīki, they should be emptied by means of the Soma sacrifice alone.
Then he places them on the northern track of the southern *havirdhāna* cart.
The Sūtra [is that] of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should place these very [vessels] below the upahavya.
Either saying, "I place speech into speech," or silently.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the individual consumption of the goblets of the *hotraka* priests.
"One should consume it in return," says Baudhāyana; "one should not consume it in return," says Śālīki.
Regarding "the touching back": [it refers to] the subsequent touching.
Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "While still consuming [the portions], one should touch them at the conclusion of the consumption."
Regarding the drawing of the cup for Indra and Agni.
Regarding this, the Sūtra says that Dīrghavātsya, one of the two teachers, stated: "One should take it with the primary vessel."
"The non-trembling after the *nārāśamsa* cups."
"They should cause them to tremble," says Baudhāyana; "they should not cause them to tremble," says Śālīki; "one should not even lift them up," says Aupamanyava, regarding the midday pressing.
Baudhāyana says that they should approach the *nigrābha* after pressing nine times and again nine times; Śālīki says [they should do so] an unlimited number of times.
Regarding the drawing of the two Marutvatīya cups:
Regarding this, Śālīke said that Baudhāyana used to say: "One should take [the draught] after the Āgrayaṇa;
for this constitutes the world of what is to be grasped."
When the eighth [recitation] has been introduced, he causes it to be recited.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one may cause [the sacrificer] to recite on any [verse] whatsoever.
Regarding the taking of the curd-heat offering (dadhigharma).

The Sūtra [prescribes] Baudhāyana’s view that the Āgnīdhra should take it; Śālīki says it should be done after enclosing the area and performing the pacification (śānti) on both sides; Aupamanyava says it should be done by the Āgnīdhra alone.
Regarding the performance of the curd-heat offering.
"One should perform it in a low voice," says Baudhāyana; "aloud," says Śālīki.
Regarding the consumption of the curd-heat offering (dadhigharma).

Regarding this, Śālīke said; however, Baudhāyana said that the others should consume [the portions] by means of the *avadāna-bhakṣaṇa* (consumption of the cut-off portions) alone, while the sacrificer himself should consume [his portion] directly with the mantra recited in the forest (*araṇye’nuvākyena*).
Regarding the non-rejection of sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*).
Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīke said, "Baudhāyana used to say that one should cause only a single sacrificial fee to go by the southern path, while the others may go according to their convenience."
"Transmigration."

Baudhāyana says that once the sacrificial fees have been led away, they may move about as they please; Śālīki says that the Adhvaryu should not pass westward toward the Sadas while the Soma has not yet been established.
Regarding the throwing away of the black antelope horn.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that once the sacrificial fees have been led away, one should throw the black antelope horn into the Cātvāla pit.
"In the dialogue of Ātreya."

Regarding the Sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated that one should ask three times without intermingling the questions, "Who is an Ātreya? Who is an Ātreya? at the point of the giving of the sacrificial gifts.
Baudhāyana used to say that one should give these [gifts] to the great officiating priests (mahartvijas), but they should not follow after the Hotraka priests;
Śālīki says that they should neither follow after the Hotrakas nor give to the Sadasya, for the specific distribution of this [offering] is not known.
Regarding the oblation of the two Marutvatīya offerings:

Baudhāyana used to say that whichever [oblation] the Adhvaryu should offer, that one should be accompanied by both the *vaṣaṭ* and the *anuvaṣaṭ* calls, while the other should be without the *anuvaṣaṭ* call; Śālīki said that both should indeed be without the *anuvaṣaṭ* call; Aupamanyava said that both should indeed be accompanied by the *anuvaṣaṭ* call.
Regarding the drawing of the third Marutvatīya cup.
Regarding this, the Sūtra says that Dīrghavātsya, one of the two teachers, stated: "One should take it with the primary vessel."
"The non-trembling after the *nārāśamsa* cups."
"They should shake them along," says Baudhāyana; "they should not shake them along," says Śālīki; "one should not even lift them up," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding Saumya, there is the mantra and the non-mantra.
Baudhāyana says that [the cake] should be accompanied by mantras; Śālīki says it should be silent;
Aupamanyava says that only the Soma-cake should be accompanied by mantras, while the single-potsherd cake should be silent.
Regarding the pressing at the third libation: |||
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
however, Śālīki says that when one causes [the milk] to swell, one should say "śumad" (prosperous) for them.
Regarding the taking of the Āditya cup.
Regarding this, Śālīke said that Baudhāyana stated: "One should draw it before the pressing; one should silently pour in the boiled *śṛtātaṅkya*."
Regarding the drawing out of the Āditya cup.
"One should recite by half-verses," says Baudhāyana; "verse by verse," says Śālīki.
Regarding the mixing of the *āśira* with the milk for the offering to Mitra and Varuṇa, it is as follows: [the pouring of the *āśira*].
Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "One should indeed curdle the Maitrāvaruṇa cup with milk, and one should pour the *āśira* (milk-mixture) into it."
When the ninth [chapter] has been introduced, he causes it to be recited.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one may cause [the sacrificer] to recite on whichever [verse] it may be.
This is the satiation of the Hotrakas.
Regarding the *sūtra*, Śālīki said that one should satisfy the *hotṛ*-priests at each pressing;

Baudhāyana says one should satisfy them at every pressing—five at the morning pressing, six at the midday pressing, and seven at the third pressing—while Aupamanyava says [one should do so] at the third pressing.
"In the domestic fires."

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say that one should follow along and consecrate the domestic fires (*aupāsana*) with mantras, cast portions of the sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa-śakala*) into the cups (*camasa*), and recite the *Ṣaḍḍhotṛ* formula right there. Regarding this,

Śālīki used to say that one should indeed follow along and consecrate the domestic fires with mantras, cast portions of the sacrificial cakes into the cups from the side, and recite the *Ṣaḍḍhotṛ* formula afterwards— at the time of the taking up and the placing of the Sāvitra cup.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should wipe it with the *sajuṣṭam* formula and then set it down.
"He responds with the *pratigara* from that other side."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should respond with "madā moda iva."
"The non-trembling after the Nārāśamsa cups."
"They should shake them along," says Baudhāyana; "they should not shake them along," says Śālīki; "one should not even lift them up," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the conduct of one who is gentle.
"One should perform it in a low voice," says Baudhāyana; "aloud," says Śālīki.
"Of the worship of Saumya."

Baudhāyana used to say: "Whether the two fires are combined or separated, Agni and Viṣṇu should both be addressed in a low tone," whereas Śālīki says they should be addressed in a low tone when combined and in a loud tone when separated.
This is the ritual procedure for the distribution of the hearths belonging to the third pressing.

Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "Having performed [the ritual] or not having performed it, one should arrange the four *dhiṣṇiya* hearths with the embers of the *saumya* offering."
Regarding the mixing of the Pātnīvata [offering]: it is as follows.
The Sūtra [prescribes] that of Baudhāyana:

"One should mix the Pātnīvata [oblation] with curds or with milk," says Śālīki; "One should mix the Pātnīvata with the remnant of the clarified butter used for the sprinkling of the hearths (dhiṣṇiyas)," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the leading forward of the wife.
The Sūtra is Baudhāyana’s; Śālīki says that one should remain right here [after the *apohiṣṭhīyā* verses].
"He responds to that which is intoxicated on both sides."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should respond with "modā moda iva" (rejoice, as it were).
"The casting down of Dhruva."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki holds that this entire mantra for the pouring down should be used at the place where the cups are set down.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Into those three [vessels], he throws three knots of dūrvā grass and one tuft of darbha grass each.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that these daksinas should consist of water alone.
Regarding the *aupayaja* offerings.

Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: one should bring the embers for the Agniṣomīya and the Savanīya from the Āgnīdhra fire, and those for the barren cow (vaśā) dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa from the Śāmitra fire.
The oblation consists of the two offerings of contempt.

Regarding this, the two teachers state in the Sūtra: "Aupamanyava used to say that one should offer the two *minda* oblations first; having offered the two *minda* oblations, one should then take the *hāriyojana* cup."
"Of the sovereignty of Śākala."
Regarding this, Śālīke said, "Baudhāyana used to say that one should add as many [pieces] as one recognizes to have been prepared, with the formula: 'Thou art the expiation for them.'"
"The worship of the Sun."
Śālīki says that one should worship the Āhavanīya fire itself with this Yajus formula, according to the view of Sūtra Baudhāyana.
Regarding the throwing away of the black antelope horn.
The former alternative belongs to Baudhāyana, the latter to Śālīki.
"The final purificatory bath," he says.

Regarding this, the Sūtra of the two teachers says that Upamanyu used to say: "Right here, having planted this [sacrificial post] mixed with a water-jar upon the sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila), one should descend for the purificatory bath (avabhṛtha) with the cooking-pots, the pressing-stones, and the Vāyavya cup."
"The floating of the pressing-stones for the Vāyavya [cup]."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that they should recite it after having washed [the vessels].
Baudhāyana says that they should wash these pots and bring them forward, and in them they should cook these offerings for the Devikās;
Śālīki says that they should simply let them float away.
Regarding the washing of the black antelope skin.

Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: having unfastened the black antelope skin and sprinkled it with water, one should give it to a son or a pupil; or one should use it as a support for the offering ladle; or one may undergo initiation again with it; or one may sacrifice again with it.
"The consecration of the sacrificial grass (barhis) for the concluding oblation."
"One should perform the mantras beginning with the taking up of the sword," says Baudhāyana;
"those beginning with the measuring cord," says Śālīki;
"those beginning with the gathering of materials," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the offering of the concluding oblation.
Having placed it in the *sruc* ladle, or having placed it in a cooking pot that has a scorched rim, one should pour out the offering.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the cooking of the *udayanīya* [offering]:
"One should cook it in milk," says Baudhāyana; "in water," says Śālīki.
Regarding "the non-avoidance of the caru."
"One should carry it around," says Baudhāyana; "one should not carry it around," says Śālīki.
Regarding the placing down of the concluding oblation (udayanīya).
Baudhāyana says that one should set down the ṣaḍḍhotṛ-oblation with the formula; Śālīki says silently.
Regarding the performance of the concluding oblation.
The Sūtra [prescribes] that one should perform the *udayanīya* sacrifice in the Āhavanīya fire; Baudhāyana [holds this view], while Śālīki [says otherwise].
Regarding the performance of the *anūbandhya* animal sacrifice.

The Sūtra of Baudhāyana is that one should sacrifice with the curd-mixture (āmikṣā) dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa; regarding this, Śālīki says that one should indeed also immolate a goat as the victim, but one should cause the ritual procedure to conclude with only eleven after-offerings (parayāja).
This is the supplementary offering for the omenta.
"One should offer each of those [oblations] individually," says Baudhāyana; "from the beginning and from the end," says Śālīki.
"The removal of heart-pains."
"One should remove them one by one," says Baudhāyana; "all together," says Śālīki; [and] "at dawn," [says] Usraṇa.
"One should immolate all the animals," says Baudhāyana; "except for the bull and the barren cow," says Śālīki.
Regarding the curdled milk (āmikṣā), there is the question of whether it is accompanied by a mantra or without a mantra.
Baudhāyana says it should be accompanied by mantras, while Śālīki says it should be silent.
"To Maitrāvaruṇī, in the enclosing sticks," [he says].

Regarding this, Śālīke said; Baudhāyana used to say that one should break off two front pillars of either the *sadas* or the two *havirdhāna* sheds and make the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*) for the *maitrāvaruṇī* offering out of split bamboo.
Regarding the term *udavasāna*: [it refers to] the place where they have moved out.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should conclude with the full-offering alone.
"The gift is for the sake of the sacrificial fee."
The rule is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that in this case, it should not be given unless there is a specific desire to do so.
Regarding the performance of the oblations to the Devikās.

Regarding the son of Aupamanyava’s Sūtra, Baudhāyana used to say that three offerings should follow the animal cake (paśupuroḍāśa) of the Anūbandhya sacrifice, and three should follow the Udavasānīyā offering; Śālīki, however, said that all [the offerings] should follow the animal cake of the Anūbandhya, while Āñjīgavi said that one should sacrifice to the Devikās with clarified butter alone.
Regarding the re-entry with the fires.
"One should resume with the perpetual fires," says Baudhāyana; "having consigned them into the two kindling woods," says Śālīki.
Regarding the two *agnihotra* offerings, there is a supplementary oblation (*pratihoma*).
"One should offer the counter-oblation," says Baudhāyana; "one should not offer the counter-oblation," says Śālīki; "one should not offer the counter-oblation," says Śālīki.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the ritual procedure for the fire-altar (agnikalpa).
Regarding the phrase "the making of the ass."
Baudhāyana says one should perform it in the intermediate direction between the north and the east; Śālīki says it should be performed in the north alone.
The oblation of the Sāvitrī verses.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
however, Śālīki says that one should offer the fourfold-drawn butter here for the sake of prosperity.
Regarding the taking up of the donkey’s halter.
"One should take it with a mantra," says Baudhāyana;
"silently," says Śālīki.
"For the ant-hill mound" [is used] at the depositing; "for the Vaiśya, the sitting down" [is used].

Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīke said; however, Baudhāyana said that one should place a termite mound [as a marker], one should not seat a Vaiśya there, one should go to where the excavation is, and if someone should ask there, one should answer him.
Regarding the word "khanana" (digging): [it means] digging.
"One should dig by half-verses," says Baudhāyana; "verse by verse," says Śālīki.
He spreads [the grass] with a lotus leaf as the upper handle.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should strew [the grass] exactly as it has grown.
Regarding the removal of the rice-balls.
Regarding the *sūtra*, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated, "One should take [the portions] with all [verses] and deposit them with all [verses]";
Aupamanyava, however, said, "One should take [the portions] with *gāyatrī* verses and deposit them with *triṣṭubh* verses."
Regarding the phrase "the surpassing of the horse."
Regarding this, Śālīke said that one should lead up the horse silently; Baudhāyana, however, said that this entire mantra for the donkey should apply [to the horse as well].
Regarding the "Beholding of Heaven and Earth."
"One should look at both [the sun and the moon] six times," says Baudhāyana;
"three times," says Śālīki;
"looking toward the eastern quarter at the juncture, one should mutter this mantra," says Aupamanyava.
They bring water for the cords, or else they eat after sprinkling them with water.
The former alternative belongs to Baudhāyana, the latter to Śālīki; this concerns the fashioning of the fire-pan (ukhā).

Baudhāyana used to say: "One should make even the Aṣāḍhā brick for this Yājuṣī rite one foot in measure; and whatever size of brick one might mix with clay, in this way his entire fire-altar becomes Yājuṣa. Śālīki, however, says: "One should fashion only a single *ukhā* (fire-pan) with a mantra, while the others should be done silently."
When all [the causes] are distinct, it is called a "condition" (pratyaya).
Baudhāyana used to say that one should repeat the ritual actions accompanied by the mantras, including those dedicated to Savitṛ.
"Whatever else besides those dedicated to Sāvitra," says Śālīki.
Then he takes twenty-one dung-clods from a stallion, the hoe, and the fire for baking.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one may take [the hair] from any horse whatsoever.
Regarding the fumigation of the cauldrons.
Sūtra: Baudhāyana says that one should fumigate with an unlimited number of mantras; Śālīki [says the same].
Regarding the heating of the cauldrons.
According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, one should prepare only a single ukhā with the mantra, while the others are prepared silently; thus says Śālīki.
He stretches them out either toward the east or toward the north.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the term "pacana": it means "cooking."

Baudhāyana used to say: "One should cook the fire-pan (ukhā), the bulls, the maṇḍala-bricks, the Bārhaspatya, the Mahāvīra, and the lokaṃpṛṇā bricks on the Gārhapatya fire; and everything else on the village fire.
Śālīki says: "Whatever is prescribed as being made of brick should be cooked on the village fire, but whatever is prescribed as an oblation (havis) should be cooked on the Gārhapatya."
Regarding the fashioning of animal heads.
Baudhāyana says they may be either actual [stones] or made of clay;
Śālīki says they must be actual ones; Aupamanyava says they should be made of gold; and Aupamanyavīputra says one should recite those mantras over the head of the Vāyavya animal.
"He draws around [the site] three times from left to right with a leafy branch."
Śālīki says that according to Baudhāyana’s Sūtra, one should scatter the beans all around and then sing the Yama-gāthās.
Regarding the term *āghāra*: it refers to the pouring of clarified butter.
"One should offer this Āghāra-libation with both mantras," says Baudhāyana; "one should offer this Āghāra-libation with only this [mantra], 'Hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgre,'" says Śālīki;
[this applies] to the offering of the Adhvara-dīkṣā oblations for one who has not yet performed his first Soma sacrifice.

Baudhāyana says that after having offered the initiation oblations of the sacrifice, one should offer the oblations pertaining to the fires; Śālīki says that they should be only those pertaining to the fires.
"During the consecrations at the Vairāja [Sāmans]," so it is said.
Baudhāyana used to say: "One who intends to perform the *sava* (consecration) before a year has passed should not undergo the *vairāja* initiations;
however, one who intends to perform the *sava* after a year has passed may undergo the *vairāja* initiations.
Or, having maintained [the fires] for a year, he should perform the one-day rite (*ekāhika*); for the fire is indeed one-day," so said Śālīki.
"In the case of the optional [rite], it is the subsequent placing [of the fire]."
Baudhāyana says that one should add the *kāmya* [mantra] once it has been produced;
Śālīki says that one should do so only beforehand.
Regarding the placing of fuel-sticks made of Udumbara wood.
Regarding this, Śālīki’s Sūtra says that Baudhāyana used to say: "One should place a single fuel-stick with five verses; that itself shall be the Rākṣoghna."
"The placing of fuel sticks for Annapatīyā."
Regarding this, Śālīki said that one should place these [bricks] upon the fire: the Annapatīyā, the Pratisamedhanīyā, and the Vaiṣṇavī; so says Baudhāyana.
This concerns the conjunction of the Vātsapra and Viṣṇukrama rites.
"One should bring them together day by day," says Baudhāyana; "from the beginning and from the end," says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of the expiation when the *ukhya* fire goes out.

Baudhāyana used to say: "Having consecrated [the fire] and having handed it over, one should offer the Arka oblations and then perform the rest of the ritual according to the standard procedure. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Having consecrated [the fire] and having handed it over, one should offer the Arka oblations, but one should not perform the rest of the ritual according to the standard procedure."
Regarding the term "prayāṇa" (departure).
Baudhāyana used to say that one should proceed with both [rites], the Adhvarika and the Agnika; Śālīki says that one should proceed with the Agnika alone.
Now, if he comes upon water that has not been bridged over.

Regarding this, Śālīke said; however, Baudhāyana used to say: "Wherever one finds water that has not been carried [from elsewhere], one should pour that ash into it, and one should not leave it without its contents (vigarbhā). Having taken as much as is required, one should replenish it with the formula, 'Having settled in the womb by means of the ash. Then, the remainder one should cause to be deposited in either jars or vessels."
Regarding the settling upon the sacrificial ground for the gods.
Baudhāyana used to say that one should settle [the site] by means of both the Adhvarika and the Agnika rites; Śālīki says it should be by the Agnika rite alone.
This concerns the pouring down of the ritual materials (saṃbhārāṇām nivapana).
Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "One should pour down the ashes and the saline soil with the mantra, but the other two materials silently."
"In the piling of the Gārhapatya fire-altar," so it is said.

Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated that one should perform all these rites—the taking of the fire, the self-piling, the touching of the white and black [spots], the ascending, and the descending—in accordance with the ritual procedure (*āvṛt*).
"One building it for the first time should pile up a thousand [bricks], consisting of five layers."

Baudhāyana used to say: "Having completed these, while building the fourth layer, one should take up [the altar] knee-high from that point upward, and it should consist of five layers. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Having completed these, while building the fourth layer, one should take up [the altar] neck-high from that point upward, and it should consist of a single layer."
Regarding the conjunction of the Vātsapra and Viṣṇukrama rites.

Baudhāyana used to say: "If the Vātsapra should fall on the Upavasatha day, one should perform the Vātsapra and then pour the grains together. But if the Viṣṇukrama steps should fall on the Upavasatha day, one should step with the Viṣṇukramas, perform the Vātsapra, and then proceed with the pouring together. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "If the Vātsapra should fall on the Upavasatha day, one should perform the Vātsapra and pour the grains together on the following day; but if the Viṣṇukramas [fall on the Upavasatha day]..."
Having performed the Viṣṇu-strides and having worshipped with the Vātsapra hymn, on the following day he should proceed with the *saṃnivāpa* (the mixing of the grains) alone.
Looking away from it, he throws drops of curd into it, either with the formula, "I place that pure [substance] for you," or silently.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Then, having filled it with sand and covered it over from above with curds—thus [he says].
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should fill it with sand and place it on the northern part of the shed.
Regarding the taking up of the sling.
"One should take it with a mantra," says Baudhāyana;
"silently," says Śālīki.
This is the attendance upon the Nairṛtis.
Regarding this, Baudhāyana says one should perform the *tayādevata* and *sūdadohas* [verses], while Śālīki says one should not.
Regarding the pouring of water from a water-pot: it means bringing water near [the fire].
"One should pour [the water] while circumambulating to the right," says Baudhāyana; "according to convenience," says Śālīki.
Regarding the worship of the Gārhapatya fire.
Regarding the carrying away of the *stambayajus*, Baudhāyana says that one should worship the Āhavanīya fire itself with this *yajus* formula, while Śālīki [holds the same].
According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, the Āgnīdhra should take [the earth] even from the time of the uparava holes; however, Śālīki says that he should take it at this point.
And the tracing out of the *cātvāla* pit has been explained.
The carrying away of the world-fires has been narrated.
The ritual service for the *sphya* and *vighana* has been explained.
"The tying on of the black-antelope skin."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
This is the pillow for the Vajriṇīs.
Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: standing in front of the peg at the sacrificial post-hole, having strung the bow, one should shoot an arrow eastward;
running after it, one should place a stone there. In the same way on the south, likewise behind, and likewise on the north.
"The Aindri bricks are the supporting layers."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should place the Aindrī brick on the tail.
Regarding the phrase "he pours [the water] near the supporting vessel":
Baudhāyana says one should pour it while moving clockwise; Śālīki says according to the position of the feet.
"Upon a cushion of a bunch of darbha grass."
"Or let Vāk-tvak place thee upon the ocean," or silently.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the laying down of the *dūrvā*-brick: [the rule is as follows].
Baudhāyana used to say that one should place it together with *dūrvā* grass, or even just the *dūrvā* itself;
Śālīki, however, says that this [brick] should be made of *mantra-dūrvā*.
"The Audumbara [tree] has a pair of ploughs."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should make this from a Dārḍhya tree.
Baudhāyana says that men alone should take up this pair of yokes and ploughs from the front, while the Adhvaryu follows behind;
Śālīki says that one should plough after having joined them directly before one's eyes.
Regarding the term "karṣaṇa": it means plowing.

Regarding the drawing back [of the yoke-poles], Baudhāyana says one should draw them back together, while Śālīki says one should draw them back individually; regarding the consecration of the pairs of oxen, [the same applies].
"One should consecrate each [offering] individually," says Baudhāyana;
"all together," says Śālīki.
Regarding the sowing of all medicinal herbs.
"One should sow by half-verses," says Baudhāyana; "verse by verse," says Śālīki.
"One exchanges one thing for another; 'one thing for another' means this."

Baudhāyana says that one should reach this direction even while not yet taking up the Sūtra; Śālīki says that one should transpose the Yajus formula with the Yajus; Aupamanyava says [one should do so] with the Yajus.
Having placed bundles of *darbha* grass into the water for sprinkling, he sprinkles the fires with them, either with the formula, "I sprinkle you, the fires, acceptable to the fires," or silently.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the laying down of the jar-bricks.
Regarding the Sūtra, Baudhāyana says that one should place these bricks only on the wings and the tail, according to the school of Baudhāyani.
"While the various directions, each with its own mantra, are being occupied."
Baudhāyana says that one should recite the *tayādevatā* formula for each brick in sequence and then perform the *sūdadohas* verse at the end;
Śālīki says that one should complete the laying of each individual brick with its respective formula.
Regarding the laying down of the groups of bricks:
Baudhāyana says that one should proceed with the *tayādevatā* formulas and then perform the *sūdadohas* verses at the end;
Śālīki says that one should complete that very same group of bricks.
In the case of touching, there is an oblation.
Regarding this, the Sūtra of the two Teachers says that Aupamanyava used to say: "One should perform the *tayādevata* and *sūdadohas* verses before the touching and the offerings."
"The pillow has the head of a serpent."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
And an udumbara vessel, together with a mortar and pestle.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana.
Śālīki says that one should make this very from the Dārḍhya tree,
