[and] regarding the threshing of all herbs.
"One should strike it with a mantra," says Baudhāyana;
"silently," says Śālīki.
Regarding the placing of the fire-pan (ukhā).
According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, one should place only a single ukhā with the mantra, while the others are placed silently; thus says Śālīki.
Regarding the laying down of the animal heads:
"One should place them in the middle," says Baudhāyana; "one should place them at the ends, having shifted them apart from that [central point]," says Śālīki.
"The placing [of the head] of the Atharvaśiras."
Baudhāyana says that one should place the nine-verse Atharvaśiras in front, facing all directions, with its head toward the Svayamātṛṇṇā; Śālīki says not the Atharvaśiras.
Regarding the placement [of the bricks] for the Sarvatomukha sacrifice.
Regarding the Sūtra, Śālīki says that one should place the Gāyatrīs exactly according to the direction of Baudhāyana.

Regarding the laying down of the limbs: Baudhāyana’s view is that one should lay down the limbs only when the limbs have been identified; Śālīki [holds] that one should do so even when they are not identified.
"The pillow of Ṛṣabha."
Regarding this, Śālīkī said that Baudhāyana used to say: "One should place it so that its head is slightly turned away, just as a bull stands to bellow toward a cow in heat."
It is the laying down of the past sets of bricks.
"One should place the foundation," says Baudhāyana; "at the end of the piling," says Śālīki.
Regarding the "bestowal of the vow":
"One should offer the vow at midday," says Baudhāyana; "at the conclusion of the piling," says Śālīki; [and] "at the laying down of the loose soil," [says Āpastamba].
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should complete the layering of the loose earth on the very day before.
Two horses should stand on either side: a black one to the north and a white one to the south.
"Baudhāyana says that one should have fodder brought for these two while they remain right here;
Śālīki says that one should lead them out at each respective time."
"The pillow of the Vālakhilyas."
Baudhāyana says that one should place the Bālakhilya bricks above;
Śālīki says on the sides.
"The abode of created beings."
With its tip facing north, he should lead it toward the *svayamātṛṇṇā* stone from the northern shoulder-joint, or from all sides.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"The laying down of the *vyuṣṭi*-bricks."
Regarding the *sūtra*, Śālīke said, but Baudhāyana said that one should lay them down facing west from the east, for the night dawns facing west from the east.
Of these, one places the Purīṣavatī brick in the middle.

Baudhāyana used to say that one should place it either together with the loose earth (purīṣa) or as loose earth itself; Śālīki, however, says that it should consist of both the mantra and the loose earth.
Regarding the laying down of the Vairāja bricks.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"The pillow of Yājñasenī."
The former ritual procedure belongs to Śālīki, the latter to Baudhāyana.
Regarding the laying down of the ghee-bricks: thus it is said.

Baudhāyana used to say that one should either place them together with clarified butter or anoint them with clarified butter, for these [bricks] should be "mantra-buttered"; Śālīki [said] that one should place lumps of clarified butter here; [and] Aupamanyava [said] that one should place only lumps of clarified butter here.
This refers to the place for the insertion of the bricks.
Between the Jyotiṣmatī bricks and the Bhūteṣṭakā bricks, this constitutes the place for the insertion of these bricks.

Baudhāyana used to say that one should place here the *saṃveśana-yajus*, the *prabodhana-yajus*, the *prayāṇa-yajus*, the *aparyāṇa-yajus*, the *sāmidhenīs*, the *āprīs*, and the groups of bricks that have already passed. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one should not cause a mantra that is not for a brick to attain the status of a brick; rather, one should place here only those groups of bricks that have already passed.
Regarding the laying down [of the bricks] on the full moon day.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should place the full-moon brick on the northern side of these.
Regarding the laying down of the asterism-bricks.
Regarding this, Śālīke said that Baudhāyana stated: "One should place the *pratitāraka* bricks here and there, and one should cause them to shine in each respective place."
"The pillow for the one facing all directions."

Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana used to say: "This [altar] indeed becomes separated from the touching of the black horse; one who is about to lay down the *sarvatomukha* altar should touch a white horse."
Regarding the phrase "in the cases of increase":

Regarding this, Śālīke said; however, Baudhāyana used to say that on a single day, as many *vardhana* offerings as may coincide, one should perform the *tayādevata* and *sūdadohas* formulas at the conclusion of all of them.
Then, he throws pieces of gold into the *prokṣaṇī* waters—more than three, or an unlimited number; "a thousand" is what has been declared.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"The oblation of the Śatarudrīya."
Gautama says that one should offer the thread [of the sacrifice] to the two teachers in the very first division.
"Attendance through prostrations."

Baudhāyana used to say that one should perform the worship while still holding the bow; having turned from the northern direction alone, having returned by the same way he came, and standing behind facing east, he should worship the upward-pointing [post]. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that one should perform the worship after having indeed laid aside the bow; having turned from this very direction, having returned by the same way he came, and standing behind facing east, he should worship the upward-pointing [post].
While the water is being sprinkled, he causes the sacrificer to recite.

Regarding this, Śālīke said; however, Baudhāyana used to say that one should pour water around [the vessel] repeatedly and then place the jar upon a stone, pointing it out with the formula: "O stone, may hunger be yours; may pain reach so-and-so," naming the one whom he hates.
Regarding "drawing away" (vikarṣaṇa):
"One should draw it out half-verse by half-verse," says Baudhāyana; "verse by verse," says Śālīki.
Regarding the sprinkling of the Svayamātṛṇṇā stone.
The Sūtra [states] Baudhāyana's view that one should sprinkle this [altar] with the four-cornered fire; Śālīki [says it should be done] otherwise.
Regarding the Vaiśvānara and Māruta [deities], there is the mantra and the non-mantra.
Baudhāyana says that they should be accompanied by mantras;
Śālīki says they should be silent; Aupamanyava says that only the Vaiśvānara cake should be accompanied by mantras while the Māruta cakes should be silent.
"The oblation for Ānīkavata."
The Sūtra says that one should offer the Anīkavat oblation in the Āhavanīya fire; this is the view of Baudhāyana, while Śālīki holds that it should be offered in the Gārhapatya.
Then he sprinkles this piled altar with the sprinkling of clarified butter.
Regarding this, Śālīke said; however, Baudhāyana said that one should sprinkle him with the formulas according to direction and according to the view of the formulas.
Regarding the laying down of the sacrificial fuel.

Baudhāyana used to say that one should place the fuel with both [sets of formulas], those belonging to the *ādhvarika* (sacrificial) rite and those belonging to the *āgnika* (fire-related) rite; Śālīki says it should be done with the *āgnika* ones alone, and that the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*) should be made of *śākala* wood.
"One should consign the Āhavanīya fire," says Baudhāyana; "only the tail [of the sacrificial fire-altar]," says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of the oblations with the *sruva* ladle.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
Regarding the performance of the final oblation (pūrṇāhuti).
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
In this context, while offering oblations, one should meditate upon the directions with the mind.
"Either [he should do so] with the formula, 'I shall collect the fire from all directions,' or silently."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the phrase "the sphere of the flow":
The former ritual procedure belongs to Śālīki, the latter to Baudhāyana.
While spreading four [blades of grass] upon it, he says:
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should not spread [the underlayer].
Regarding the pouring out of the libation and its subsequent offering.
"One should throw it into the fire," says Baudhāyana; "one should not throw it into the fire," says Śālīki.
Regarding the cooking of the *brahmaudana* (the Brahmin’s rice porridge).
"One should cook it as at the Agnyādheya," says Baudhāyana; "in this very [manner]," says Śālīki.
Regarding the consumption of the Brahmaudana.
Baudhāyana says that they should eat at the northern end of the buttocks, while Śālīki says [they should eat] on both sides of the tail.
The oblation for those named after Vāta.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should offer even the wind here with the joined palms;
Aupamanyava says that one should offer it using a hollowed-out black antelope skin as a vessel.
Regarding the throwing-in of the Śākala pieces.
Regarding the laying of the fire-hearths, Baudhāyana says that one should throw [the earth] into the fire, while Śālīki says that one should not throw it into the fire.
According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, one should lay down all the bricks belonging to the Yajus formulas; thus says Śālīki.
"The sowing of various seeds."
Baudhāyana says that one should touch [the offering] after following it with the pouring out;
Śālīki says that one should complete each respective oblation exactly as it is.
For them, he causes the call for the preparer of the oblation (*haviṣkṛt*) to be raised specifically over the rice; they then gather up the barley.

Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated that from the time of the pouring [of the grains] onwards, the ritual actions accompanied by mantras should be repeated for the barley, but the call to the *haviṣkṛt* should be performed as a single common procedure (*tantra*).
Regarding the pouring of water for the consecration.
"One should pour out [the water] for the Āpyas behind the Gārhapatya," says Baudhāyana; "having passed it in front," says Śālīki; "either in front or behind," says Aupamanyava.

One should cut the *iḍā* portion from the other oblations including the animal-cake (*paśupuroḍāśa*) either from the center or from the front half; thus it is said regarding those including the animal-cake.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding "transgressing": [it refers to] stepping over.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana: one should step across together with the Sviṣṭakṛt offering; thus says Śālīki.
Regarding "consecration" (abhiṣeka):

Regarding this, Sūtra and Ācārya say that Aupamanyava declared: "One should consecrate him with the formula as it is handed down before the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering; here there is no black antelope skin, no two gold plates, and no *pārtha* offerings; having merely spread out *kuśa* grass, one should consecrate him upon those."
"Emancipation in yoga."

"One should yoke it day after day and release it day after day," says Baudhāyana; "one should yoke it day after day and release it at the end [of the ritual]," says Śālīki; "one should yoke it only at the beginning and release it at the end," says Aupamanyava.
"The performer of the sacrifice."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should perform his ritual acts according to the specific sacrifice itself.
Regarding the dedication of the animals belonging to the set of eleven.
The Sūtra [of Baudhāyana] states that one should dedicate the animals of the set of eleven at a single sacrificial post; Śālīki says that this applies specifically to the offering of the omenta.
"One should offer each of those individually," says Baudhāyana; "from the beginning and from the end," says Śālīki.
Regarding "the making of the horse smell [the offering]":
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should have the horse sniff the offering only at the midday pressing.
Regarding the "seating of the animals."
"One should place each animal with the Pañcahotṛ formula," says Baudhāyana; "only the principal one," says Śālīki.
"The removal of heart-pains."
"One should remove them one by one," says Baudhāyana; "all of them together," says Śālīki.
Regarding the curdled milk (āmikṣā), there is the question of whether it is accompanied by a mantra or without a mantra.

"It should be accompanied by mantras and fit for being cut out," says Baudhāyana; "it should be silent and fit for being cut out," says Śālīki; "it should be accompanied by mantras, and one should sacrifice with this *nirūḍhapaśubandha* as a model for the performance," says Aupamanyava.
Regarding the performance of the oblations to the Devikās.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the Vājapeya sacrifice.
"One should pile the fire at the Vājapeya," says Baudhāyana; "one should not pile it," says Śālīki.
On an udumbara wood chariot wheel with seventeen spokes.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should make it from the Dārḍhya tree itself.
"Prepare a split post made of khadira wood, bound with leather straps."
The Sūtra follows Baudhāyana; however, Śālīki says that one should also prepare here a goat-skin and a piece of gold weighing a śatamāna.
During the final days of summer, he undergoes initiation before the full moon of Āṣāḍhā.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should sacrifice with the Vājapeya in autumn.
The oblation of the Sāvitrī verses.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
The mixing with the Sura used for the Vājapeya sacrifice.
Regarding this, the two teachers [hold different views]; here Upamanyu said that one should fetch it from wherever the *surā* may be.
He ties knots at intervals of one cubit each, or he winds the loops of the bowstring.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
And the *caṣāla* is made of wheat.
According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, one should prepare [the offering] even from wheat flour; thus says Śālīki.
The fastening of the drums.
This sūtra is indeed twofold.
"The performance of the sacrifice."
Regarding this, Śālīke said; however, Baudhāyana used to say that one should also undertake the Atirātra sacrifice here as a ritual, and one should cause it to conclude within the same fortnight;
furthermore, one takes five *natigrāhya* cups for Indra.
According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, all these soma-offerings are to be drawn; according to Śālīki, they are all to be drawn.
Regarding the grasping of the Surāgrahas.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should wipe them clean while they are still together and then set them down.
He extends it towards the north with two rows or three rows.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"One should approach the sacrificial post having taken six ropes," says Baudhāyana;

"one should approach the sacrificial post having taken five ropes," says Śālīki; "one should approach the sacrificial post having taken four ropes," says Aupamanyava; "one should approach the sacrificial post having taken only one rope," says Aupamanyavīputra; and "one should fasten [the animal] using only the rope of the Agnīṣomīya sacrifice," says Āñjīgavi.
Regarding the dedication of the animals belonging to the Vājapeya sacrifice.

Baudhāyana says that after having consecrated the animals of the Ekādaśinī set, one should consecrate those belonging to the Vājapeya; Śālīki says that one should consecrate only those belonging to the Vājapeya, and not the Ekādaśinī animals at all.
Regarding the dedication of the animals dedicated to Prajāpati.
"One should offer them one by one," says Baudhāyana; "all together," says Śālīki.
This is the supplementary offering of the omenta.
"One should offer each of those [oblations] individually," says Baudhāyana; "from the beginning and from the end," says Śālīki.
"The extinguishing of heart-pains."
"One should remove them one by one," says Baudhāyana; "all together," says Śālīki.
Regarding the yoking of the chariots.

Regarding this, Śālīke said; however, Baudhāyana used to say that one should first employ that mantra which is for the simultaneous casting down among the yoking-mantras, and then one should silently cast down the horses.
Regarding the phrase "attaining the limit":

Baudhāyana used to say: "Having turned clockwise, they should go to that goal; then from there they should turn back with their left sides toward the center. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Having turned with their left sides toward the center, they should go to that goal; then from there they should turn clockwise.
Now, he causes the sacrificer to put on the *tārpya* garment.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should cause the sacrificer to put on both of these.
"Having resorted to the basis."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
One ascends it in ten eons.
The Sūtra [of Baudhāyana] states that one should descend with these very same mantras; Śālīki says this.
At this point, he places a throne for him after he has descended from it.

According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, one should descend from this [chariot] with a goat-skin and a hundred-māna weight of gold; according to Śālīki, one should do so with a goat-skin and a hundred-māna weight of gold.
Then they carry him to the Sadas on this very seat, or he goes by himself.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the consumption of the *atigrāhya* cups.
The former ritual manual belongs to Śālīki; the latter belongs to Baudhāyana.
Regarding the consumption of the portions belonging to Prajāpati.
The former ritual procedure belongs to Śālīki, the latter to Baudhāyana.
"In the third from the anus," it is said.
"Regarding this, Baudhāyana says that one should offer two additional oblations (upayaja) for each of the three [parts] of the rectum; Śālīki says [they should be offered] by cutting them off;
Aupamanyava says that having thrown all of these together into the fire, one should consecrate them with all the mantras.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the Rājasūya."
"One should pile the fire-altar at the Rājasūya," says Baudhāyana; "one should not pile it," says Śālīki.
Baudhāyana says that one should scatter [the grains] again, grind them into flour, and then cause them to be eaten; Śālīki says that they should remain exactly as they were scattered.
Regarding the mantra and non-mantra of Nairṛta.
Baudhāyana says that it should be accompanied by a mantra, while Śālīki says it should be performed silently.
Regarding "the carrying of a single firebrand":
"One should take it from the Anvāhāryapacana fire," says Baudhāyana; "from the village fire," says Śālīki.
"The oblation for Nairṛta," it is said.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should offer it after enclosing it with the *visraṃsikā* and *kāṇḍābhyāma* formulas.
Regarding the giving of sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*).
"One should give every day," says Baudhāyana; "at the beginning and at the end," says Śālīki.
Regarding the pouring of water from a water-pot.
"One should pour it out while circumambulating," says Baudhāyana; "as it happens," says Śālīki.
Svāhā! Homage to him who has done this!
Regarding this, the Sūtra of Baudhāyana states that one should carry forward the *svāhā*-utterance even at the end; Śālīki, however, holds a different view.
The application of the *saṃtanī* [sacrifice] follows.

Baudhāyana used to say: "On whichever day one should sacrifice with a *iṣṭi* or with an animal sacrifice, on that very day one should employ the *saṃtanī* oblations. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "These two [oblations] are indeed seen for the purpose of the daily *āśrāvaṇa* (calling for the response). On whichever day one should sacrifice with a *iṣṭi* or with an animal sacrifice, on that day one should not employ the *saṃtanī* oblations."
The supplementary performance of the Cāturmāsya sacrifices.

Baudhāyana used to say: "On whichever day one performs the Cāturmāsya sacrifices, on that very day one should also perform the Saṃtanī. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "These two [offerings] are indeed seen for the purpose of the daily *āśrāvaṇa* (invocation); therefore, on whichever day one performs the Cāturmāsya sacrifices, on that day one should not perform the Saṃtanī."
The procedure for the five-fuel rite has been explained; now, [the text] says that one sweeps up the embers with the upaveṣa.

Regarding this, Śālīki said that one should silently collect the embers and then offer oblations over them with the dipping-spoon (sruva), saying "To Agni, the slayer of Rakṣas, svāhā! and so on with five [mantras]; at this point, one should give a chariot drawn by a mule as a gift. Baudhāyana, however, says that one should silently collect the embers and then offer oblations over them with the dipping-spoon, saying "To Agni, the slayer of Rakṣas, svāhā! and so on with five [mantras], and at this point, one should give a chariot drawn by a mule.
The oblation consists of flour-grains of Apāmārga.
Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana used to say: "One should offer the groats of *apāmārga* to him with the entire mantra;
one should throw the wooden spoon into the fire silently;
and one should rise up silently."
Regarding the performance of the oblations to the Devikās:
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana:
"They should follow each Soma [offering] with a Soma. Śālīki says one should not sacrifice with the Devikā oblations; Āñjīgavi says one should not.
Regarding the re-entry with the fires.
"One should conclude with the perpetual [fires]," says Baudhāyana; "having consigned them into the two kindling woods," says Śālīki.
"The pouring together of the milk-rice."
Baudhāyana says that one should pour [the water] into a leather bag or a vināḍī vessel, while Śālīki says it should be poured into a new water-pot (kumbhī).
Regarding the phrase "in those committed by oneself":

Regarding the Sūtra, Śālīki said; however, Baudhāyana said that one should bind the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) from *kuśa* blades crushed by the hooves of cattle, and the fuel (*idhma*) from wood fallen of its own accord; whatever is the form of the altar (*vedi*), that itself shall be the altar; and having placed either a leather bag or a water-skin on a chariot, one should carry it around, and whatever fresh butter (*navanīta*) might spill there, that shall serve as the clarified butter (*ājya*).
The offering of the oblation for Maitrābārhaspatya.
Baudhāyana says that the two [portions] should consist of four handfuls each,
while Śālīki says they should consist of four handfuls separately; [the latter also specifies] on a red hide.
According to Baudhāyana, the Sūtra says it should be reddish-brown; according to Śālīki, it should be non-red.
Regarding the animals purchased for the Soma, Baudhāyana says that the regular ones should be included in the hundred; Śālīki says that these very animals should be the hundredth.
Regarding the drawing of the *vasatīvarī* waters.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki, however, says that one should also take the Sarasvatī waters here as the Vasatīvarī waters.
"The animal to be seized for Indra-Agni follows that of Agni."
The Sūtra [of Baudhāyana] states that the Savanīya offering should be dedicated to Indra and Agni; Śālīki, however, holds that it should be dedicated to Indra alone.
Regarding the making of bowls.
Baudhāyana says that one should have the vessels made without any modification; Śālīki says that these should be exactly as prescribed in the archetype.
The supplementary oblation for the Sarasvatīs is as follows.

Regarding this, Śālīki said; however, Baudhāyana used to say that with those two verses with which one would offer over the flowing waters, one should offer them at each drawing of the cup (graha), and then one should offer the Sarasvatī offerings silently.
This refers to the taking up of the cups for the consecration.
Regarding this, the two teachers state in the Sūtra; however, Aupamanyava says that one should draw the cups for the consecration ceremony (abhiṣecanīya) in front of the Sadas.
Regarding the gift of a bow.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
The placing of the potsherds for the cake on twenty-one potsherds dedicated to Māruta.
Baudhāyana says that one should place them with groups after having placed [the bricks] with the iṣṭi formulas; Śālīki says that one should place them with groups alone.
Regarding the curdled milk (āmikṣā), there is the question of whether it is accompanied by a mantra or without a mantra.
Baudhāyana says it should be accompanied by mantras,
while Śālīki says it should be silent at the place of the eunuch.
"One should stand within the altar," says Baudhāyana; "outside the altar," says Śālīki.
Regarding the phrase "the making of jewels":
Baudhāyana says that it should be covered with an Audumbara vessel or an iron one; Śālīki says it should be made of Audumbara wood alone.
Upon that chariot-stand, together with the charioteer, he places the chariot.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that for those who establish the sacred fires, there should be only one charioteer.
Regarding the giving away of the wooden sword (sphya).
Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "One should hand it over with the mantra to the sacrificer alone; the others should hand it over silently."
Regarding the phrase "the instrument of the senses":
"They should be made of gold," says Baudhāyana; "of silver," says Śālīki; "of ivory," says Aupamanyava; "of Vibhītaka wood," says Aupamanyavīputra.
Then, having cut off five dice from it, he hands them over to him.
Regarding this, Śālīki says that Baudhāyana used to say: "Whatever part of it might be incomplete, one should supply that there as well, [reciting] 'The king has come hither from the quarters.'"
Then, at the equinox, he offers an oblation upon a bunch of darbha grass.
Regarding the carrying of the fires, the Sūtra of Baudhāyana states that one should go to wherever there is a bunch of Darbha grass; this is the view of Śālīki.
Baudhāyana says that one should carry the fires continuously; Śālīki says that one should consign them into the two kindling woods.
"For the sake of making [the altar] knowable."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that the altar should be progressively larger.
Then, having brought him from the bathing place and purified him, he brought forth the Puṇḍarīka-sraj.
Baudhāyana used to say that one should have both kinds of lotuses made—those of gold and those grown in water;
Śālīki, however, says that they should be only those grown in water.
They set this remnant of the oblation aside for him as his portion of the vow-food.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should not place the remnant of the oblation here as a portion for the vow-food.
Regarding the animals purchased for Soma, Baudhāyana says they should be the regular ones, while Śālīki says these very ones should be used.
Regarding the oblations of the *aupasada* rites, there is the question of whether they are accompanied by mantras or are mantra-less.
"They should be accompanied by mantras," says Baudhāyana; "they should be silent," says Śālīki.
"For the animal dedicated to Agni, a hornless goat dedicated to Prajāpati is to be offered as an additional victim."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki, however, maintains that the Savanīya offering should belong to Prajāpati alone.
"The Bhārgava becomes the Hotṛ," so it is said.
Baudhāyana says that one should choose a Bhārgava as the Hotṛ from the very beginning; Śālīki says that the Hotṛ should be a Bhārgava specifically at the Daśapeya sacrifice.
"A hundred Brahmins are drinking."
Baudhāyana says that the sacrificer should be the hundred-and-first; Śālīki says that the sacrificer himself should be the hundredth.
Regarding the giving of sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*).

"Baudhāyana says that one should give these very same sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā) as prescribed by the Brāhmaṇas; Śālīki says that this [set] is the beginning of the thousand; [the rule applies] to their respective terminations."
"They should proceed until the final purificatory bath (āvabhṛtha)," says Baudhāyana; "until the end of the Apsuṣoma offerings," says Śālīki; "until the end of the Dhruva offering," says Aupamanyava.
"Having offered each oblation, he pours clarified butter over the portion belonging to Bṛhaspati."

Baudhāyana says that after having sacrificed to the offering for Bṛhaspati, one should pour the clarified butter over the portion for Bṛhaspati; Śālīki says this applies only to the other oblations, but not to the one for Bṛhaspati.
He calls for the formal announcement loudly for the oblation to Āditya, and softly for that to the Maruts.

Baudhāyana says that from the *āśrāvaṇa* of the Āditya offering onwards, one should recite softly, and the rest loudly; Śālīki says that from the *āśrāvaṇa* of the Māruta offering onwards, one should recite softly, and the rest loudly; Aupamanyava says that the entire Āditya offering should be recited loudly, and the entire Māruta offering softly.
Regarding the phrase "among the messengers of truth":
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should simply say, "This person has sent it to you."
"The two-night [rite]" means:
The rule of Baudhāyana is that on the day of sacrifice, the preceding day occurs first and the following day occurs later; Śālīki holds the opposite view.
Regarding the performance of the oblations to the Devikās.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the ritual procedure for the bricks (iṣṭikalpa).

Baudhāyana used to say that there should be fifteen *sāmidhenī* verses, the two *ājyabhāga* offerings should contain the word "slayer of Vṛtra" (*vārtraghna*), and the deities should be invoked loudly; on this point, Śālīki used to say that there should be seventeen *sāmidhenī* verses, the two *ājyabhāga* offerings should contain the word "increasing" (*vṛdhanvant*), and the deities should be invoked in a low voice (*upāṃśu*).
"It is the performance by the sacrificer."
Baudhāyana says that one should perform the duties of the sacrificer (*yājamāna*) according to the path of the *siddha-iṣṭi*;
Śālīki says that one should perform the duties of the sacrificer as occasion permits.
"One who, being a regular performer of the New and Full Moon sacrifices, should omit either the new moon day or the full moon day, should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Pathikṛt."

Regarding this, Baudhāyana used to say: "Having offered the *pāthikṛt* oblation, one should subsequently offer the *vaiśvānara* on twelve potsherds; then one should perform the expiation for what has been omitted. On this point, Śālīki used to say: "Having offered the *pāthikṛt* oblation, one should subsequently offer the *vaiśvānara* on twelve potsherds within the same ritual framework (*samānatantra*), and one should not perform the expiation for the omission separately. Aupamanyava said: "One should perform the expiation for the omission together with either of the two [the *pāthikṛt* or the *vaiśvānara*]. On this point, Āñjīgavi used to say: "The sacrifice of that person is indeed torn asunder whose ritual framework, once extended, is joined by another ritual framework."

One should perform that very same eight-potherd cake for Agni, which is the unswerving (acyuta) one, as the Pathikṛt offering on either the full moon or the new moon day; one should not, however, perform a subsequent sacrifice for what has already been omitted.
One who, having established the sacred fires, should act as if contrary to his vows, shall offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Vratapati.
Baudhāyana says that this [period] is stated as beginning from the laying of the fires; Śālīki says it is when the fires have been laid and the fuel has been added.
"One for whom the Rakṣases might pursue [him] should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni, the slayer of Rakṣases."
Baudhāyana says that one should conclude the iṣṭi after having offered the agnihotra;
Śālīki says that one should offer the agnihotra once the iṣṭi has been concluded.
"One practicing exorcism should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni accompanied by Rudra."
Baudhāyana used to say that the officiating priests (ṛtvij) should proceed wearing red turbans and red garments;
Śālīki, however, says that this is already expressed by the *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* verses themselves.
One whose cattle or men have died, or who is afraid, should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Surabhimat.

Baudhāyana used to say that they should throw fragrant substances into the *prokṣaṇī* waters, and that the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) should perform their duties while possessing fragrance; Śālīki, however, says that this is already expressed by means of the *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* verses themselves.
One for whom a desire does not come to pass should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Kāma.

Baudhāyana used to say: "If one offers that [oblation] which is prescribed therein and yet the desired object is not attained, then one should act in this manner; thus, this very [offering] shall be effective for all desires. Śālīki says: "This [offering] may be for each individual desire. Aupamanyava says: "It may be for every single desire."
"One whose fire, having been taken out, should go out before the Agnihotra has been offered, should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Jyotiṣmat."
Regarding this, Śālīke said that Baudhāyana maintained that one should recite these formulas: "the churning," "the further churning," and "the kindling."
"One should offer a cake on twelve potsherds to Vaiśvānara when a son is born."

Baudhāyana used to say that when the ten-day period has passed, one should offer a cake on twelve potsherds to Vaiśvānara and have the child lick the remnants of the oblation; Śālīki says this should be done as soon as [the child] is born, and that one should not have the child lick the remnants of the oblation; Aupamanyava says it should be done at the next *parvan* (lunar festival), and that the two oblations are to be reversed.

Baudhāyana says that the Mārutas should first receive the mantra-rite; Śālīki says it is from the time of the cutting (avadāna); Aupamanyava says it is from the time of the offering (pradāna); and Aupamanyavīputra says it is from the time of the fourfold tasting (cātuṣprāśya).
"Having gone to a place of refuge, one should offer an oblation to Vaiśvānara on twelve potsherds."

Regarding the matter of where one who intends to depart should go, Baudhāyana says that one should go to that very place and offer a cake on twelve potsherds to Vaiśvānara; Śālīki says that it should be offered in the fires themselves, each in its own proper place.
"By means of which rope one might lead away the best cow."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should simply say, "This one has sent it to you."
One should arm even children and women with armor.
The Sūtra follows Baudhāyana's view; however, Śālīki holds that even for those with weak or small teeth, the sacrificial grass (barhis) should be tied together here.
"One who practices sorcery should offer an oblation on eleven potsherds to Agni and Viṣṇu."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should do so only after ascertaining that the person is indeed practicing malevolent magic against him.
"The clarified butter belongs to Sarasvatī."
"Baudhāyana says this ghee should be poured out with a mantra; Śālīki says it should be done silently;
Aupamanyava says one should take it from the *dhruvā* at each respective time."
"In the Adhvarakalpā" means:

Baudhāyana used to say that one should perform the first ritual procedure (tantra) ending with the *iḍā*, and likewise the second; one should then carry forward the remainder together with the third. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say that from the time of the carrying forward of the fires, one should let the first procedure rest, and likewise the second and the third; one should carry forward the remainder together with the third, including the full-vessel offering (*sapūrṇapātra*) and the Viṣṇu-strides (*viṣṇukrama*), so says Aupamanyava.
For one who desires spiritual luster, he should offer this oblation of cooked rice to Soma and Rudra on the full moon day of the Tiṣya constellation.
Baudhāyana says that one should offer [the oblation] on the day of the fast (upavasatha), while Śālīki says it should be on the day of the sacrifice (yajaniya).
The sprinkling is with clarified butter; they purify themselves with clarified butter.

"One should throw the water-pot into the clarified butter and the dipping-spoon," says Baudhāyana; "one should perform both the sprinkling and the wiping with clarified butter, while the rest one should perform with water," says Śālīki; "whatever must be done with water, all that one should do with clarified butter," says Aupamanyava.
If one who suffers from skin disease should fear, "I shall become afflicted with a bad skin," he should offer a sacrificial pap (caru) to Soma and Pūṣan.
Baudhāyana says that one should offer when the forms have been perceived;
Śālīki says that one should do so even while anticipating them beforehand.
Regarding the phrase "in the halves":

Baudhāyana says that one should add the half-portions when the sacrifice has been completed; Śālīki says that they should remain lying right there; [and regarding the two oblations,] they are reversed.

Baudhāyana says that the Mārutas should first receive the mantra-rite; Śālīki says [it should be from] the portioning; Aupamanyava says [it should be from] the offering; and Aupamanyavīputra says [it should be from] the fourfold tasting.
"The Hotṛ priest performs the sacrifice with the two Mārutī offerings."

Baudhāyana used to say that the Hotṛ should invoke the Maruts from the very beginning, while the Adhvaryu does so at the time of the recitation; Śālīki, however, says that this is already stated by means of the invitatory and offering verses themselves.
"One desiring prosperity should offer a caru-oblation to the Ādityas who are accompanied by the word 'bhuvat'."

Regarding the Sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana used to say: "All [the rites] should have their footprints; all should have the Sāvitra formulas; all should have their fuel-sticks with their blades intact."
Regarding the taking away from the footprints of the empty ones.

Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "Having extracted the soil from the footprints with the entire mantra, one should pour in the northern row; then, one should silently pour water over the breast."
"One hundred gold pieces (suvarṇa) are equal to one kṛṣṇala."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that these [verses] should be exactly one hundred, and that one should exclude some of them.
"He cuts off four *kṛṣṇala* seeds each, for the attainment of the fourfold portion."

Baudhāyana used to say: "Those portions which have been cut off, one should indeed offer them; then those which are for the purpose of consumption should be separated [into individual portions]; as for the others, they should be divided equally. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Those portions which have been cut off, one should indeed offer them; then those which are for the purpose of consumption should be separated [into individual portions]; as for the others, having poured them into the *prāśitra-haraṇa* vessel, one should hand them over to the Brahman priest."
"For one who is seized by the evil consumption (pāpayakṣman), he should offer this oblation of cooked rice (caru) to Āditya on the new moon day."
Baudhāyana says that one should offer the oblation on the day of the fast (upavasatha), while Śālīki says it should be on the day of sacrifice (yajaniya).
"For the sake of gathering [the people], [place them] upon the enclosing-sticks."

Baudhāyana says that one should enclose [the altar] with the implements used for the cake-offering (puroḍāśa) after having first enclosed it with those used for the iṣṭi; Śālīki says that one should do so using only the implements used for the iṣṭi.
The offering of oblations.

Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana used to say: "One should offer these oblations with vessels made of udumbara wood; having offered them, one should throw those very vessels right there into the fire."
Regarding the inspection of the clarified butter.
According to Baudhāyana,
one should purify the clarified butter that has been looked upon with these very verses, "That which was fresh became fresh butter" and so forth; according to Śālīki,
one should offer as many four-potherd oblations to Varuṇa as there are horses one receives, plus one extra.
Baudhāyana used to say: "One should perform the Vaiśvānara [offering] for one gift; likewise for two;

but having accepted a group [of gifts], one should perform it. For many, however, one should perform the Vāruṇa [offerings] with one extra. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should perform the Vaiśvānara for one gift, but not for two;
nor, having accepted a group, should one perform it. Nor, for two or for many, should one perform the Vāruṇas with one extra."
Regarding the curdled milk (āmikṣā), there is the question of whether it is accompanied by a mantra or without a mantra.
"It should be accompanied by mantras," says Baudhāyana; "it should be silent," says Śālīki.
Again he sweeps it together; having swept it together, he cuts off [the portion].
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should collect [the portions] with these very same mantras and then cut them off.
"He offers a cake on thirty-three potsherds."
The Sūtra belongs to Baudhāyana;
Śālīki, however, maintains that this should apply only to the case of a doubtful sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa).
The supplementary oblation (abhihoma) is performed with a stalk of Varṣāhū grass.
The Sūtra is Baudhāyana's: "One should go to that very place where there is a clump of *varṣāhū* grass," says Śālīki.
Regarding the shaking out of the black antelope skin.
Baudhāyana says that one should shake out the black antelope skin while standing within the altar; Śālīki says it should be done outside the altar.
Regarding the performance of the Añjaḥsava and Kārīrī sacrifices.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
Thus ends the section on the performance of penance for the creation.

Regarding this, the two teachers [have spoken]; here Upamanyu said: "Now, as for the Āhavanīya fire, since it is drawn forth from that very source, whereas the Anvāhāryapacana fire has its origin in the village, there is no expiation for it in each such case, for the emission of a fire in vain is indeed commended."
Thus, indeed, these sacrifices have been explained;
"he offers while stepping forward."
To what extent, indeed, has this been stated?
Regarding the five fore-offerings (prayāja), Baudhāyana says they are [performed] before the shed, while Śālīki says they are [performed] within the shed.
If the portion of the victim should be lost, one should cut off [the portion] from clarified butter as a substitute.

Baudhāyana used to say: "If a portion of the animal victim is lost—if one or if two—having offered a substitute with clarified butter and having performed that rite, one should sacrifice again. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "If a portion of the animal victim is lost—if one or if two—one should offer a substitute with clarified butter, perform that rite, and consider it already accomplished; but if more than that is lost, then one should act in this manner [as Baudhāyana prescribed]."
Thus, "all."

"Baudhāyana says that wherever there may be navigable waters or a river between [two villages], or even a mountain range, there is a *saṃsava* (a simultaneous performance). Śālīki says that wherever sounds do not mingle, there is a *saṃsava*. Aupamanyava says that wherever one can travel between them, there is a *saṃsava*. Aupamanyavīputra says that there is a *saṃsava* only between two distinct regions (*janapada*). Āñjīgavi says that no *saṃsava* exists between those who are not at enmity, for such is the *Chāgaleya Brāhmaṇa*."
The oblation for the Abhibhūtis.
Baudhāyana says that after performing the *ādhvara* offerings, one should perform the *sāttvāyaṇika* offerings;
Śālīki says that they should be *sāttvāyaṇika* ones only.
Regarding the phrase "when they have broken out and spread":

Regarding this, Śālīki said; however, Baudhāyana used to say that with those two verses by which one would offer into the *pūtabhṛt* and *ādhavanīya*, one should offer at each cup (*graha*), and then one should pour out the residue silently.
In the case of a permanent reception, one follows it with the verse addressed to Viṣṇu.
According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, this [verse] is to be recited only over the speckled butter (pṛṣadājya); so says Śālīki.
After each hymn (uktha), he either responds with "O reciter of hymns! (ukthaśas) or says "The libation" (savana).
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the taking up of the *pṛṣṭhya* cups:

Regarding the Sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "Wherever these days might coincide, one should indeed take the Pṛṣṭhya cups there. Aupamanyava, however, says: "These [cups] are seen [prescribed] specifically for the year; therefore, one should take them only within the year."
Regarding the consumption of the *pṛṣṭhya* cups.
Baudhāyana used to say that one should consume them both with the consumption formula used at each pressing and with the regular formula;
Śālīki says it should be with the regular formula alone.
"Strike down the openings of the slaughter-houses! Thus [he says].
"One should remove them one by one," says Baudhāyana; "all at once," says Śālīki; [regarding] the shaking [of the vessel], so it is said.
Baudhāyana says that one should shake off the transgression; Śālīki says it should be according to the manner of the fan; Aupamanyava says it should be wiped clean.
"Am̐ śorhoma," thus [it is said].

Regarding this, Śālīki states the Sūtra; however, Baudhāyana says that one should offer to him with those two verses with which one would otherwise touch [the water], and then one should touch [the water] silently.
Regarding the taking of the *pṛśni* cups.
The former alternative belongs to Baudhāyana, the latter to Śālīki.
Therefore, he kindles the armpit.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; however, Śālīki says that even in this case, one should fast by eating only cake.
"The bull grows old among the cows."

Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana used to say: "Even if one should sacrifice another animal outside the main ritual framework (*tantra*), one should perform these same rites for it—namely, for the two preparatory offerings, for the omentum, and for the deities."
With eight verses, there is the oblation of the fetus's fat.

According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, one should not offer the *vasāhoma* (fat-oblation) for the embryo; according to Śālīki, one should neither offer the *vasāhoma* for the embryo nor the *iḍā* nor the *sviṣṭakṛt*; according to Aupamanyava, this applies to the introductory ritual (*upākaraṇa*) of a goat-ewe.

The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana: "One should dedicate it with a verse addressed to Vāyu," says Śālīki; regarding this, the elder Kātyāyana used to say: "Just as one displaces the dedication during the act of dedication itself, so too would the subsequent mantras be displaced."
When it has not been obtained, there is non-existence.

Baudhāyana used to say: "If, at the end of the day, there are clouds that are not black, one should indeed conclude [the rite]; but if they should be black, then one should act in this manner. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "If they do not obscure the sun, one should indeed conclude; but if they should obscure it, then one should act in this manner. Gautama, however, says: "There is no such thing as failing to conclude [the rite] as long as the animal has not been sacrificed."
Regarding the phrase "jayeṣu":
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the *abhyātāna* [verses]: thus it is said.

The former ritual manual belongs to Śālīki, the latter to Baudhāyana; regarding this, Aupamanyava used to say that one should offer these as spoon-oblations—namely the Abhyātānas, the Jayas, and the Rāṣṭrabhṛts—and thus the Darśapūrṇamāsa sacrifices would be properly attended to.
"On the yoke-pins and the enclosing-sticks."
Baudhāyana says that one should make the śamyā-paridhis out of the very śamyā; Śālīki says that these should be the same as those used in the archetype sacrifice.
He offers the Rāṣṭrabhṛt oblations twice with the utterance of svāhā.
"One should offer the oblation with the *vigrāha* formula," says Baudhāyana; "two spoonfuls [of clarified butter] each," says Śālīki.
"He offers in the place of worship; he offers at the front of the chariot; he offers on the pole of the chariot."
This is the Sūtra of Baudhāyana; Śālīki, however, says that these should be fire-altars alone.
The fuel consists of wood from the Nyagrodha, Udumbara, Aśvattha, and Plakṣa trees.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana:
"Having separately anointed these fuel-sticks, one should place them on the fire separately," so says Śālīki.
"Whatever is harsh in speech, with that he utters the *vaṣaṭ*."

Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana used to say: "One should offer [the oblation] mixed with whey and alkaline salt together with an *arka* leaf; one should utter the *vaṣaṭ* call as either 'ajahī' or 'kaḍ'."
Regarding "procreation":
Baudhāyana used to say that one should consecrate [the sacrificer] with both— the Vāsiṣṭha verses and the Sāvitra formula;
Śālīki says it should be with the Sāvitra formula alone during the steps across.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the phrase "in the Prātimokṣas":
The former ritual procedure belongs to Śālīki, the latter to Baudhāyana.
Regarding the seizing of the breath-seizers.
According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, these [bricks] are seen as belonging to the year; therefore,
one should take them from the year itself— so says Śālīki.
Having milked her, one should give her to a Brahmin whose food one would not otherwise eat.
Regarding this matter, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana used to say: "If he should sit down even before the desire to know [the truth] has arisen, then one should act in this manner."
"If the Gārhapatya fire should go out while the Āhavanīya has not yet gone out," so it is said.

Regarding this, Śālīke said that Baudhāyana used to say: having poured this entire fire together into a vessel, having carried it around to the south of the sacrificial ground, having removed the ashes from the site of the *gārhapatya* fire and smeared it with a lump of cow-dung, having piled it up and added fuel; then, having taken out the blazing *āhavanīya* fire, having removed the ashes from the site of the *āhavanīya* and smeared it with a lump of cow-dung, having piled it up and added fuel; then, when the *āhavanīya* is provided with kindling wood, he should offer six oblations with the *sruva*-ladle, [reciting]: "Awake, O Agni," and "O Agni, you who are far-extending."
"O Sword, may the mind, as light, enjoy [the sacrifice], spreading the thread; 'Upwards that bright one'."
"In the case of the *atirikta-soma* sacrifices," [it is said].
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
When the *dhruva* has been omitted, there is the performance of an expiation (*prāyaścitta*).

Baudhāyana used to say: "If the Chhandogas and Bahvṛcas should obtain [the Soma] before the final purificatory bath (avabhṛtha), they should repeat the Stotras and Śastras; having performed that, one should sacrifice again. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "If the Chhandogas and Bahvṛcas should obtain [the Soma] before the avabhṛtha, they should repeat the Stotras and Śastras; having performed that, one should consider the rite as already completed."
Regarding the phrase "the grasping of days."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that on whichever day follows immediately, one should draw the cups beginning with those for Mitra and Varuṇa.
Regarding the performance of an expiation when the sacrificial post has sprouted.

According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, one should perform the expiation when the sacrificial post has sprouted; however, Śālīki says that this expiation should be performed only within the ritual framework itself.
If one's *soma* should be exhausted, he should divide his gold and forest produce into two parts; he should shake one portion onto the *ārjīṣa* and offer the other as an oblation.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
however, Śālīki maintains that from this point onward, the principal cups (camasas) should be offered with gold included and should be refilled.
"In the cases of the Ādārasoma offerings."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one may even cause another to obtain the Soma by means of a purchased Soma (adārasoma).
Regarding the phrase "in blessings" (āśiḥṣu):
"Benedictions should follow," says Baudhāyana; "these very benedictions should be used," says Śālīki.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the twelve-day sacrifice (dvādaśāha).
"One should pile the fire-altar on the twelfth day," says Baudhāyana; "one should not pile it," says Śālīki.
"The ones to be seized beyond."

Baudhāyana used to say: "The householder alone should consign [the fires] into the two kindling woods; this constitutes the form of the *atigrāhya* cup. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "They should consign [the fires] separately into their respective kindling woods; having churned out the fire for the first one, the householder, they should release the burning [fires] while they are still burning; this constitutes the form of the *atigrāhya* cup."
This is called the "pouring together."

Baudhāyana used to say that those intending to perform the *saṃnivapa* (the mixing together of fires) should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni accompanied by the Brahman, to Agni accompanied by the Kṣatra, and to Agni the bearer of the Kṣatra; regarding this, Śālīki used to say that this sacrifice is indeed for the purpose of joining the fires, so one should offer it at the very place where one intends to pile the fire-altar; and Aupamanyava said that one should follow the animal-cake offering dedicated to Prajāpati.
"Wind," it says.
"Baudhāyana says that one should purify them one by one and then draw them up one by one;
Śālīki says that one should purify them all at once and then draw them up one by one; Aupamanyava says that one should purify them all at once and then draw them all up together."
Regarding the choice of the ancestral seer (ārṣeya).

Baudhāyana used to say: "If there are any who belong to the same *gotra* and are not separated [by others], even if they are otherwise of different *gotras*, their selection should be by the selection of a single *ṛṣi*-lineage. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "Whether they are separated or unseparated, if they belong to the same *gotra*, their selection should be by the selection of a single *ṛṣi*-lineage."
"Milk for the vow."
"They should milk together and divide [the milk] equally," says Baudhāyana;
"their cows for the vow-milk should be kept separate," says Śālīki.
Regarding the rule that "on the sixth day, having approached [the altar], they pile up the *uttaravedi*," the *sūtra* of the two teachers also prescribes this as an alternative on the eleventh day.
Regarding the taking up of the *vasatīvarī* waters.

Regarding this matter, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana used to say: "If the pitcher should have a residue remaining, one should pour it out silently; but if the smearings have been entirely collected together, then one should act in this manner," so says Śālīki.
He then mutters the "re-seizing" formula of the sacrifice either at the Yajñāyajñīya stotra or at the Śaṃyuvāka.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
They turn the enclosing sticks and strike down the prastara-bunch.

The sūtra [is] that of Baudhāyana: "One should throw the prastara and the paridhis into the fire here," says Śālīki; "Having closed his eyes, the adhvaryu offers the upāṃśu [oblation]," so it is said.
Regarding the Sūtra, Śālīki says that one should offer the oblation even without looking at it, according to Baudhāyana.
"By means of crafts, there is the preparation."

Baudhāyana used to say that one should perform the *upākaraṇa* with both—the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) and the artistic implements (*śilpa*); Śālīki, however, says it should be done with the artistic implements alone.
Regarding the term "nyūṅkhana": [it refers to] the nasalization (nāsikya).
One inserts the *nyūṅkha* either at the beginning of the *virāj* verses or during the *śastra* recitation.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the churning-stick, there is the view that it is both with a mantra and without a mantra.
Baudhāyana says that it should be accompanied by a mantra, while Śālīki says it should be performed silently.
The oblation is for the sake of the sacrificial fee.

Baudhāyana used to say: "One should indeed offer the oblations and mutter the formulas for the responses. Regarding this, Śālīki used to say: "One should indeed offer the oblations, but one should not mutter the formulas for the responses.
Aupamanyava said: "Whatever formulas are connected with the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), one should pay no heed to them at all;
[this is] the 'avivākya' [rite]."
"Baudhāyana says that this day is one on which no dispute should arise; Śālīki says that one should simply respond [to any challenge]."
Regarding the phrase "the extraction of the Ṛcs":
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana:
"The Adhvaryu should perform the rite exactly according to the archetype; only the Chandogas and Bahvṛcas should perform the modifications," says Śālīki.
Regarding the term *sarpaṇa*: it means "creeping" or "gliding."
Baudhāyana says that they should move along with the edges of their black antelope skins and touch the northern *havirdhāna* cart; Śālīki says that they should not touch it.
"In the case of those beginning with the Āgrayaṇa," it is said.
Baudhāyana says that the Adhvaryu, remaining silent, should draw the first cups; Śālīki says he may do so after having released his speech.
Having taken up the semen, he retains it until he takes up the other two humors.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana:
"Whichever [cup] one should take, having wiped it around, one should set it down," says Śālīki.
Regarding the installation of the sacrificial fires and the subsequent wandering.
"One should follow after," says Baudhāyana; "one should not follow after," says Śālīki.
"In the animal-sacrifice manuals."

Śālīki maintains that for Baudhāyana, all sacrificial sessions—whether one-day rites, multi-day rites, or night-sessions—are indeed devoid of the Āindrāgna animal sacrifice throughout all the ritual periods.

Regarding those [sacrifices] among them which have the *mahāvrata* chant, Baudhāyana says that they should be accompanied by the piling of the fire-altar (*agnicityā*), whereas the others should be performed on the high altar (*auttaravedika*); however, Śālīki maintains that the fire-altar should indeed be the one belonging to the one-day sacrifice (*aikāhika*).
"In the cases of the *ākṣīya* [stomas]," it is said.
Baudhāyana says that these—the Abhijit, the Viṣuvat, the Viśvajit, the tenth day, and the Mahāvrata—are the ones that become deficient.
Śālīki says they are those other than the Pṛṣṭhya and the Abhiplava [sacrifices]. Aupamanyava says they are those other than the Pṛṣṭhya and the Abhiplava, as well as the tenth day.
Gautama says that these eight—the Prāyaṇīya, the Ārambhaṇīya, the Abhijit, the Viṣuvat, the Viśvajit, the tenth day, the Mahāvrata, and the Udayanīya Atirātra—are the ones that become deficient.
"In the animal-sacrifice manuals."
Śālīki holds that for Baudhāyana, all the year-long sacrificial sessions (sattras) throughout all the ritual cycles consist exclusively of sets of eleven sacrificial animals.
The arrow has a hundred strands.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that this [lute] should be a vīṇā with a hundred strings.
Regarding the performance of the artistic crafts belonging to the Māhāvrata day within the multi-day sacrificial session (ahargaṇa).
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
Regarding the shaving of the crest-locks during the Ahargaṇa sacrifice.
"They should follow [the fire]," says Baudhāyana; "they should not follow [the fire]," says Śālīki;
this concerns the two-night rite.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana: "The preceding day belongs to the first [rite], and the following day to the latter," says Śālīki.
In that regard, there are those who are tall, dwarfish, or short.
"These [cows] should be the constant ones in the thousand," says Baudhāyana; "these very ones should be the thousandth," says Śālīki.
Regarding the smelling of the Droṇakalaśa vessel.
"One should cause [the animal] to smell within the enclosing sticks," says Baudhāyana; "outside the enclosing sticks," says Śālīki.
"The oblation of forms," so it is said.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki, however, says that one should also offer oblations of the forms belonging to the Aśvamedha here.
"Among those who have raised their hymns," etc.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the sacrificial cakes (puroḍāśa) of the Aupasadha rites, there is the question of whether they are accompanied by mantras or are mantra-less.

"They should be accompanied by mantras," says Baudhāyana; "they should be silent," says Śālīki; "one should offer them together with a single spoonful (sruvāhuti) as oblations to Agni," says Aupamanyava.
"They prepare two kinds of paths."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says that one should also prepare goats here.
"The sacrificial post has its base in the mortar," so it is said.
"One should perform all the preparatory rites," says Baudhāyana;
"having sprinkled it, one should raise it," says Śālīki.
Having sprinkled and worshipped it, one should erect a chip of the sacrificial post; so says Aupamanyava.
"From the empty place, the carrying away."

Regarding the fire-places, the pit for the Audumbarī post, the Uparava holes, the rubbish heap, and the Uttaravedi—Baudhāyana says that one should carry the earth from these places along the path; Śālīki says that one should not carry it along the path.

Now, if they should report an obstacle during the *dīkṣā* or *upasat* days, Baudhāyana says that they should disperse and rise after performing the *udavasānīya* offerings; Śālīki says they should rise after pressing [Soma] for one day; Aupamanyava says they should rise without having completed the *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period. These are the rules regarding their rising.
"They should proceed until the final purificatory bath (āvabhṛtha)," says Baudhāyana; "until the end of the Apsuṣoma offerings," says Śālīki; "until the end of the Dhruva offering," says Aupamanyava.
Baudhāyana says that there is an Atirātra followed by a Janaka-saptarātra and a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha;
Śālīki says there is a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha followed by an Atirātra.
"One who is about to undergo initiation for the ten-night sacrifice, having offered the Daśahotṛ oblation, undergoes initiation for the ten-night sacrifice."
The Sūtra [prescribes] Baudhāyana’s view that, having offered the Saptahotṛ, one should offer the Daśahotṛ; thus says Śālīki.
Thus indeed is one possessed of the Brāhmaṇas.
Then there is the Gobalada ten-night rite, an Atirātra, a Pṛṣṭhya Ṣaḍaha, a Vājapeya, and a Mahāvrata followed by an Atirātra; on the eighth day, there is a Vājapeya.
In that regard, there is the performance of the oblations for the Devasū offerings.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki;
"they should follow the animal-cake of the thirty-three-fold [offering]," says Aupamanyava.
When the *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period is being omitted, there is the performance of the crafts.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
On the sixty-first night, there is the taking up of the Vaiśvakarman and Āditya cups.
Baudhāyana says that one should take these two [cups] on the three subsequent days;
Śālīki says that these two are seen [prescribed] specifically for the year-long sacrifice, and therefore one should take them only during the year-long sacrifice.
"The sixteen-cup vessel is made of udumbara wood."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; Śālīki says it should be made of khadira wood alone.
Regarding the dedication of the animals for the Atirātra sacrifice.
According to the Sūtra of Baudhāyana, one should perform the upākaraṇa ceremony for Sarasvatī alone; thus says Śālīki.
Regarding the consumption of the sixteen cups by the sixteen officiating priests.
"One should consume them as manifest," says Baudhāyana; "as drunk by Indra," says Śālīki.
In the nocturnal rounds, there is the touching of the principal cups.
Regarding this, Śālīke said that Baudhāyana stated: "With the mantra 'O Indra, you who [protect] Āpiśarvara,' one should touch each principal cup."
Regarding the mantra and non-mantra of the Āśvina [cup]: thus it is said.
Baudhāyana says that it should be accompanied by a mantra, while Śālīki says it should be performed silently.
Regarding the performance of the Āśvina cup.
Regarding this, Śālīke said, "Baudhāyana used to say that one should perform the offering with the Āśvina cup there, prior to the performance of the cups for the Tiroahniya days."
Regarding the consumption of the cups belonging to the subsequent days.
"One should consume [the portion] with the *anuṣṭubh* metre," says Baudhāyana; "with the *jagatī* metre," says Śālīki.
"In the third from the anus," it is said.

"One should perform the secondary offerings (upayaja) after dividing [the animals] into eleven groups," says Baudhāyana; "by way of severance (apaccheda)," says Śālīki; "having thrown all of them into the fire together, one should consecrate them with all the mantras," says Aupamanyava;
[this concerns] the handing over of the set of eleven.
Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīke said, "Baudhāyana used to say that there should be eleven Agniṣomīya victims, eleven Savanīya victims, and eleven Anubandhya victims."
Regarding the therapeutic regimen, there is the mantra and the non-mantra.

"One should obtain [the sacrificial ground] in the village, not in the forest," says Baudhāyana; "one should obtain it in the forest, not in the village," says Śālīki; "neither in the village nor in the forest," says Aupamanyava.
"The worship of the upaśaya."
Regarding this, Baudhāyana says that one should place the cord right here to the north; Śālīki says it should be placed there.
Regarding the tracing of the Pātnīvata [portion].
"One should trace around the stake at the front of the hall," says Baudhāyana; "one should erect the Pātnīvata post to the north of the set of eleven posts," says Śālīki.
"Of Tvaṣṭṛ's son, whether with or without a mantra."
Baudhāyana says that it should be accompanied by a mantra, while Śālīki says it should be performed silently.
"The release of the son of Tvaṣṭṛ."

Regarding this, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana used to say: "Having carried fire around it on all sides, having led it out northward between the *cātvāla* and the *utkara*, and having sprinkled it with water, one should release it among the goats of the sacrificer."
"Of the performance of the son of Tvaṣṭṛ."
"One should perform it in a low voice," says Baudhāyana; "aloud," says Śālīki.
"Furthermore, in the mind," it is said.

Regarding this, Śālīke said; however, Baudhāyana used to say that if one building the fire-altar should lose his way, he should pile a supplementary layer (punasciti) upon that very altar and set up the sacrificial post (yūpa) to the north of it.
"In the Kauṇḍapāyinīya sacrifices."

Baudhāyana says that the rites beginning with the adding of fuel to the fires (agnyanvādhāna) and ending with the *iḍā* should be completed; Śālīki says they should begin with the *ājyabhāga* offerings and end with the *iḍā*;
Aupamanyava says they should include the pouring out of the full vessel (*pūrṇapātra*) and the *viṣṇukrama* steps.
The giving of the Piṇḍapitṛyajña is [the first].
"One should give [the dakṣiṇā] day by day," says Baudhāyana; "at the beginning and at the end of the month," says Śālīki; this is the explanation regarding the Hotṛs.
One view is that [the offerings] include the *graha* cups, the *ṛta* formulas, and the *svāhākāra* exclamations;
another view is that they exclude the *graha* cups but include the *ṛta* formulas and the *svāhākāra* exclamations; yet another view is that all of these are included.
The first alternative belongs to Baudhāyana; the latter two belong to Śālīki.

Offering on each full-moon day, he should offer twelve times in a year; this is one way. Offering on both new-moon and full-moon days, this is another. Offering on all [new-moon and full-moon] days, this is yet another.
The first alternative belongs to Baudhāyana; the latter two belong to Śālīki.
"O you who possess the consciousness of the thirty-three."

Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "The taking of the fire, the self-piling, the touching of the white and black [spots], the ascending, and the descending—one should perform all this ritual action according to the established procedure."
"Day by day, in the consciousness."

Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīki said, but Baudhāyana said that one should perform all these rites—the taking of the fire, the self-piling, the touching of the white and black [spots], the ascending, and the descending—in accordance with the ritual procedure (*āvṛt*).
"The layering of the soil upon the patterned chariot wheels."

"One should make the ends of the loose earth [at the corners]," says Baudhāyana; "one should reach the end of the loose earth only at the bricks," says Śālīki; [regarding the covering], it is on a red hide.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana; however, Śālīki says it should be reddish-brown.
Regarding the instrument of that which is led by both.
Baudhāyana says that one should repeat both verses twice; Śālīki says that while saying "only once," one should actually recite them twice.
"Soma is in the east, Soma is in the west;
Soma is in the west, Soma is in the east."
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
The mixing of the *sautrāmaṇī* liquor with the *surā*.
Regarding this, the two teachers cite the Sūtra; here Upamanyu said that one should fetch [the materials] from wherever the surā might be.
Regarding the seizing of the *surāgrahas*.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
however, Śālīki says that one should also draw the milk-offerings (payograhān) here.
He extends those handles of the offering-ladles behind [the altar], either toward the east or toward the north.
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
"The mixing of the *surā* and the *soma*."

"One should carry it to the south and pour it out to the north," says Baudhāyana; "one should carry it to the north and pour it out to the south," says Baudhāyani; "one should pour it out from the very same place where one carries it," says Aupamanyava.
"One should perform the worship with the *pāvamānī* verses."
Baudhāyana says that having worshipped with the Pāvamānī verses, they should worship with the invitatory and offering verses (yājyā-anuvākyā) of the ancestors;
Śālīki says that they should worship only with the invitatory and offering verses of the ancestors, and not with the Pāvamānī verses.
"The final purificatory bath."
Regarding this, the two teachers state in the Sūtra; here Upamanyava said that one should go down for the purificatory bath (avabhṛtha) with the sacrificial spikes and the *māsara* liquor.
It is declared that the removal [of the fire] takes place at the edge of the water.
The ritual bath has been described.
The preparation of the fuel-sticks has been explained.
Regarding the subsequent offering of the Vaimṛdha [cake]:
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana:

"One who has not yet performed the first Soma sacrifice should not perform the subsequent offering," says Śālīki; one who has enemies should perform only the Full-moon sacrifice, not the New-moon sacrifice.
Regarding both occasions, Baudhāyana says that one should sacrifice with the full-moon oblations; Śālīki says that one should not perform any sacrificial form on the new moon day;
Aupamanyava says that one should perform the Piṇḍapitṛyajña.
"One desiring cattle should sacrifice with the Sākaṃprasthāyīya."
Regarding this, Śālīke said that Baudhāyana used to say: "One should offer the *puroḍāśa* with the two offering-spoons (*sruc*) and the *sāṃnāyya* with the cup (*camasa*)."
One who has not attained prosperity should sacrifice to Mahendra;
for there are three who have attained prosperity: the learned Brahmin, the village headman, and the noble warrior—for them, Mahendra is the deity.

Regarding this, Baudhāyana says that whoever should desire to sacrifice to Mahendra other than these [specified occasions], he should sacrifice to Indra for a year and then obtain the status of Mahendra; Śālīki says that one may even obtain the status of Mahendra after sacrificing to Indra for a year from this very point.
One should sacrifice to Indra for a year,
for one does not overstep the vow for a year.
Regarding this, Śālīke said that Baudhāyana [held]: "On whichever new moon day one first begins to sacrifice to Indra, when a year has elapsed, on that same day he should sacrifice to Mahendra;

from that point forward, he should indeed be a sacrificer to Mahendra. Regarding this, Aupamanyava said: "The year is indeed already completed for him who, on whichever new moon day he first begins to sacrifice to Indra, should sacrifice to Mahendra on the new moon day that occurs before the completion of the year;
from that point forward, he should indeed be a sacrificer to Mahendra."
"One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the Dākṣāyaṇa sacrifice;
he should offer the *saṃnaya* at the full moon, and he should sacrifice with the curd-mixture (*āmikṣā*) for Mitra and Varuṇa at the new moon."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki, however, says that one should also offer the Vaimṛdha oblation here.
Regarding the consumption of the Sāṃnāyya.
Regarding this Sūtra, Śālīki said that Baudhāyana stated: "The sacrificer himself, having set aside this half-month [of milk], should consume the *sāṃnāyya*."
Regarding the curdled milk (āmikṣā), there is the question of whether it is accompanied by a mantra or without a mantra.
"It should be accompanied by mantras," says Baudhāyana; "it should be silent," says Śālīki.
He places the *iḍā* on the four-wheeled [chariot]; this is the performance of the *upāṃśuyāja*.
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki, regarding the offering of the sacrificial fees at the Bṛhaspatisava.

"One should offer the sacrificial gifts (dākṣiṇāni) at each pressing," says Baudhāyana; "One should offer the sacrificial gifts only at the midday pressing, and at the other two pressings one should simply say, 'I give,'" says Śālīki.
"With gold he purifies the clarified butter."
"Baudhāyana says that this clarified butter should be poured out with the mantra, while Śālīki says it should be done silently."
"When the Vedyā is not agitated, he consecrates him with the Bṛhat-stotra facing south of the Āhavanīya fire."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should sprinkle [the sacrificer] after having spread out even a black antelope skin there.
"A water-pot filled with beans."
It should be made of gold and filled with gold māṣas, according to Baudhāyana; it should be made of clay and filled with grain-māṣas, according to Śālīki.
"He sacrifices seventeen speckled heifers dedicated to the Maruts."
Baudhāyana says that for these [animals], there should be separate *manotā* verses and separate animal-cake (*paśupuroḍāśa*) offerings;

Śālīki says that for these, there should be separate *manotā* verses but a single animal-cake offering; Aupamanyava says that for these, there should be a single *manotā* verse and a single animal-cake offering.
"The Agniṣṭut and the Indrastut," so it is said.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana:
"The Adhvaryu should perform [the rite] exactly according to the archetype; only the Chandogas and Bahvṛcas should make modifications," says Śālīki.
Regarding the phrase "in the case of additional hymns":
The former alternative is that of Baudhāyana; the latter is that of Śālīki.
Regarding the gift of the bow.
The former ritual procedure belongs to Śālīki, the latter to Baudhāyana.
"The end of the one-day rites."
The Sūtra of Baudhāyana [applies] up to the end of the Mṛtyusava, says Śālīki.
They set aside for him this remnant of the oblation as his portion of the vow-food.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
Śālīki says that one should not place the remnant of the oblation here as a portion for the vow-food.
Now, regarding this performance of the Pravargya rite, there is the immediate performance, the subsequent performance, the circumstantial performance, and the performance beyond [the norm].
"One should perform it," says Baudhāyana; "one should not perform it," says Śālīki.
The two pressing-boards are the two nostrils of the corpse; the two testicles are the two thighs of the man.
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana;
however, Śālīki says that one may also use fire-sticks (araṇī) from a funeral pyre for this purpose.
"Whatever cup he draws, he draws it in this very manner; whatever vessel he sets down, he sets it down in this very manner."
The Sūtra is that of Baudhāyana:
"Whichever cup one may draw, having wiped it all around, one should set it down," says Śālīki.
He gives a white horse;
he gives a white mare; he gives a black horse;
he gives a pregnant mare with a mark on her forehead; he gives a hundred oxen.
He gives thirty-three gold coins; he gives a Soma-cup; he gives a golden cup.
"He gives grain made into a heap;
he gives grain made into a stack."
"Baudhāyana says that one should offer these [oblations] as well as the regular ones; Śālīki says that one should offer only these.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the Sarvatomukha sacrifice.

"One should pile the fire-altar facing all directions," says Baudhāyana; "one should not pile it," says Śālīki.
